truth: The vein is not new. An Ascent Age array sealed it under the ice, and the array is still running further up the slope, beneath ice that has not melted yet.

lore: Before the sand came, the Passing River ran through here to the outer sea and its banks were lined with Ascent Age cities. Now the dunes move a few li a year, and every few decades they open a street, a palace roof or a tower top to the sky. Looter crews race the [[House of City-Openers]]'s licensed diggers to each one, and the finds go east to Fallen Star City for appraisal. Sand worms a li long hunt by vibration: walk softly or ride a camel, whose steps they ignore. Wells here are dug fifty zhang deep and still go dry, and the deep sand is spreading east.
name: The Buried Cities
summary: The oldest and deepest sand, where dunes a thousand zhang high walk with the wind and uncover Ascent Age cities for a season before burying them again. Looters, appraisers and worms.
truth: Every geomancer who has mapped the water table here has found the same thing: it slopes toward the [[Thirsting Sands]] from every direction, uphill included.

lore: The Thousand Lamps Temple does not kill its vow-breakers. It snuffs their lamps, strikes their names and walks them to this valley, and after that no monk will speak to them. Most starve. The rest band together, keep their temple arts and drop the temple rules: they rob travelers on the Roof road, sell technique manuals from memory and take lowland students who cannot afford a real master. A Foundation cultivator who walks in alone rarely walks out. The Askers never go in.
name: Valley of Snuffed Lamps
summary: A cold valley on the Roof where monks expelled by the Thousand Lamps Temple live after their lamps are put out. To the temple they are dead, and they act like it.
truth: The valley's eldest outcast was expelled for asking what the monk in the deepest hall is meditating on. He has a Nascent Soul and an answer.

lore: The Ringing Bell Fort's bell was cast from the armor of the Iron Bone dead and can be heard a hundred li away. The fort-city holds ten thousand people, the Kingdom of Linked Forts's court and the Cloister's wall command. In summer, ships from Black Frost put in under truce flags; in winter the harbor freezes and the gates close. The market sells black iron and furs, Roof salt and medicine, and the best ice-fishing gear in the world. Bounties for raiders' heads are posted on the bell tower and paid in Foundation pills.
name: Ringing Bell Fort
summary: The great bell-fort of the Precept Watch on the cliffs above the strait. Its bell warns the whole coast when the ice bridge forms, and its bounty board pays in pills.

lore: From the Butter Fair it looks like a white blade with the Mirror resting on its tip. Hermit monks live in caves up to the last ledge where breath still works; above it the gang wind strips skin and qi together. Climbers say a stele on the summit is carved with a Wind Dao insight, and that its strokes can be felt from the highest ledge as a pressure in the teeth. Each spring the hermits sell snow lotus from the ledges, three centuries old and colder than ice, to anyone who climbs up to buy it.
name: Crown-Touching Peak
summary: The highest mountain that touches the ground. Its summit stands inside the gang wind, and nobody has stood on it since the Ascent Age.
truth: The stele is real. It was cut by the last cultivator who tried to fly from the summit to the Mirror after the Ladder broke, and his body is still sitting beside it.

lore: The Kingdom of the Dusk Ferry's boats have crossed the strait for eight thousand years, and its ferry guilds know every current and every ghost toll on the water. The guild masters elect the Ferry King from among themselves. Children learn to row before they can walk far and learn the courtesies owed to the dead before they can read. Every family keeps a shrine to its ancestors on the far shore, and some have married their dead to the Long Dusk Continent's dead, which binds the living families as in-laws. Ghost cultivators court spirit-rooted children, which frightens their mothers.
name: Kingdom of the Dusk Ferry
summary: A kingdom of ferrymen on the western shore whose ships make the five-month crossing to the Long Dusk Continent. Ferrymen's families marry ghosts' families, and nobody there thinks it strange.
truth: The Ferry King drowned four years ago. His ghost still rules, because the guild masters found him more reasonable afterward.

lore: For twenty days the ring holds a gate onto a green, rainy world under a pale sky, where herds of spirit horses of Ascent Age breeds, long gone from Severed Heaven, run wild. The gate admits cultivators below Core Formation; a Core aura scatters the herds and closes the ring. A tamer who brings out a foal has a fortune. The tribes send their best young riders to every opening, and the khan has announced that this time every foal belongs to him. The next opening is in 3,128.
name: The Pasture Garden
summary: A shard world of endless grassland where Ascent Age sects bred their war mounts. Every fifteen years its gate opens on the steppe inside a ring of standing stones.

lore: The Gate of Gathered Dew's founding art, the Dew-Gathering Palm, condenses water from desert air; a Core Formation elder can fill a cistern under a cloudless sky. The sect sells dew arrays to oases, which makes it rich and makes the water court its enemy, since a dew array needs no allotment. It tests children by leaving them in a dry room with an empty cup for a day. Disciples study Water Dao, array making and medicine, and spend their third year on water service in a dying village, which is how the sect learns which villages to buy.
name: Gate of Gathered Dew
summary: A Water Dao sect that teaches cultivators to pull dew from dry air. In a land where water is power, its disciples carry their own.
truth: The dew arrays yield less every year. The air over the Sand Sea is drying faster than the elders can explain, and they have stopped publishing their measurements.

lore: Its water is milky with glacier flour from source to mouth. In the gorge it is a white torrent no boat survives, crossed only on the Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings rope bridges; below the gorge it slows, spreads and floods the delta every summer. Fishermen catch blind white river eels whose fat makes a renowned eye salve. The flow is steady because the Wet-Nurse never shrinks, and the Kingdom of the White Delta's kings call the river Heaven's one gift to the Myriad Sands Continent.
name: The Milk River
summary: The only river in Myriad Sands that reaches the sea every year. It rises from the Wet-Nurse Glacier, cuts the great gorge through the Withered Rivers and spreads into the white delta on the inner coast.

lore: Her snout is a blue cliff six hundred zhang high, and the river leaves it through a cave, already white with rock flour. Herders bring sick yaks to drink at the cave mouth. Ice cultivators cut cores of thousand-year ice from her flanks to lay ice-element foundations, and the Cloister takes one core in ten as tithe. In summer the ice falls from her face as loud as war drums.
name: Wet-Nurse Glacier
summary: The great glacier at the head of the Milk River, called the Wet-Nurse because every drop of the river is her milk.
truth: She is the only glacier in Myriad Sands that is still growing. Whatever is pulling water from under the Roof's other glaciers has not reached her yet.

lore: The living poplars turn gold in autumn, and the dead ones stand among them grey and twisted, some since before the Thousand Lamps Temple was built. Poplar tears crystallize on the bark in summer and are scraped off by the Kingdom of the Desert Poplars's children for a few coppers a jar. Spirit poplars, the trees that woke, move their roots at night toward water, and a grove can walk a li in a year. Foragers say the dead trees listen, and never say anything rude about them under their branches.
name: Forest of Three Thousand Years
summary: The great desert poplar forest on the delta's tail, half alive and half standing dead. Its trees weep poplar tears, a cooling salt alchemists prize.
truth: The spirit poplars are walking west, toward the [[Thirsting Sands]], following the water down. A grove that reaches the edge drinks itself to death in a season.

lore: Sixty years ago an engineer from the ports showed the coastal fishing villages how to flood shallow pans with seawater and let the sun do the rest. Now the shore is a checkerboard of white pans, and the villages have become a kingdom under the Lu family, the engineer's in-laws. The Kingdom of the Salt Pans salt is coarse and grey and costs a third of pan salt. Children rake salt from dawn and are paid by the basket. The kingdom has no army and is hiring the Kingdom of Escorts escorts and anyone with a sword, because its caravans keep disappearing on the pan.
name: Kingdom of the Salt Pans
summary: A coastal kingdom of sea-salt pans on the southeastern shore, newly rich and newly hated. Its cheap sun-dried salt is breaking the old salt kingdoms' prices.
truth: The Heavenly Scale Pavilion lent the Lu family the money to build the pans, and lent the Ban family the money to fight them. Whoever wins, the Pavilion owns the salt.

lore: Sand whales swim under the dunes as fish swim in water, sixty zhang long and blind, and surface only to breathe and to calve. Each spring the pods converge on this basin, and their spouts throw up plumes of damp sand and real water from the deep aquifer. Caravans camp on the rim and run out to fill skins between surfacings, which kills a few people every year. Nobody has tamed an adult, but a calf raised from birth will follow its tamer's footsteps through the sand. The pods are smaller every spring.
name: Sand Whale Bay
summary: A deep basin in the dunes where pods of sand whales gather each spring to calve. Their spouts bring up water from far below, and caravans camp on the rim to catch it.
truth: The oldest bull carries an Ascent Age harpoon in its back, stamped with the seal of the river cities. It slept through the Dim Age with the harpoon in it.

lore: The gate holds for twenty days and admits Core Formation cultivators and below; a Nascent Soul aura splits the ice and brings the grotto down on everyone. Inside is a windless world of ice caverns lit by blue fungus, where ice-silk worms spin the thread artifact refiners use for armor linings. The last opening was in 3,121. The Cloister sends its third-winter monks in as a trial, and the Kingdom of the Ice Crossing smugglers sell maps of the caverns that are wrong in interesting ways.
name: Grotto of Deep Ice
summary: A grotto in the Wet-Nurse Glacier that becomes the gate to a shard world of black ice every nineteen years, in the deepest month of winter.
truth: The black ice is not ice. It is the frozen blood of an outer demon killed at the Severance, and the worms that eat it are changing.

lore: The pan is so flat and white that by midmorning the horizon dissolves, and by noon the Mirage Sea shows what it is named for: water, harbors, towers, sometimes armies, all shimmering. Salt-cutters work in the cool hours and salt caravans cross by night, steering by the stars because the daytime landmarks lie. The Tamarisk River ends here in a bitter lake. Salt is money for the Myriad Sands Continent's mortals, and two salt kingdoms are fighting a price war that Heavenly Scale Pavilion is quietly refereeing. A demonic sect uses the mirages as bait.
name: The Mirage Sea
summary: A white salt pan the size of three kingdoms, the bed of an inland sea that died in the Dim Age. At noon the mirages turn it back into a sea, with phantom cities and fleets.
truth: The mirages have grown sharper every year since the tide began rising, and some now show places that are not in Severed Heaven at all. Even the sect that hunts with them is afraid of those.

lore: The living the Passing River is short: from the Roof's snows over the Sheer Wall to the Hundred Mouths, where it ends. Below that its old bed runs west for a hundred thousand li, a dry valley lined with half-buried Ascent Age quays that the looters use as a road. Once a generation, after a great snow year, a white flood runs the whole bed to the sea in a single night, and drowns whoever is camped in it.
name: The Passing River
summary: The river that falls off the Roof at the Hanging Curtain, feeds the delta oases and dies in the sand. Its dead bed runs on past the buried cities to the outer sea.
truth: Each year the river ends a few li further upstream. The last white flood was sixty years ago, and the bed has not run since.

lore: The Cloister teaches the Vajra Body in nine layers, each tempered with bronze bells, ice water and beatings, and a Fist Dao whose roar can stop a charging yak. Entry is the Bell: stand under the great bell while it is struck, and if you are still standing when the sound dies, you are in. Monks serve three winters on the wall before they may teach. They hate the [[Eternal Night Palace]] with calm thoroughness. Captured blood cultivators have their meridians broken and are then fed and taught sutras until they repent or die of old age.
name: Lion's Roar Cloister
summary: The Myriad Sands Continent's school of vajra-body fist monks and the Thousand Lamps Temple's border arm. They do not kill: they break you, heal you and offer to shave your head.
truth: Forty captured blood cultivators live in the lower cells. Six have truly repented. Two are spying for the Night Sovereign; the abbot knows which two and feeds them lies.

lore: Each figure holds a cup in its right hand and a sword at its belt, and the faces are worn smooth. They stand alone or in lines, and the tribes say each marks an enemy killed by a forgotten hero. Shamans meditate among them and claim to hear old battle songs. On the longest night of the year the stones are said to face west, and herders keep away. Formation masters have noticed that the lines make an array, broken in places, whose purpose nobody has worked out.
name: Plain of Stone Men
summary: A plain of ancient stone men, thousands of carved figures facing east across the steppe. Nobody knows who carved them, and the tribes say they turn at night.
truth: They do face west on the longest night. The array is a ward against something in the Buried Cities, and the broken places are where tribes took stones for their hearths.

lore: A Hall of Vows monk chooses a vow, of silence, of standing, of never refusing a beggar, and keeps it until it carves itself into his meridians; then it is a power, and breaking it shatters his cultivation. Old vow-keepers are frightening: one has not lain down in three hundred years and cannot be knocked over. The Hall also witnesses oaths. Every karmic contract the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] writes is sealed before a Hall of Vows monk for a mid-grade stone, and the Hall keeps a copy. It recruits by asking what you would never do, and waiting to see if you lie.
name: Hall of Vows
summary: The vow-keepers of the Roof. Its monks take vows that become laws of their bodies, and it witnesses the karmic oaths behind the Heavenly Scale Pavilion's contracts.
truth: The archive can unmake an oath as well as witness it. The Hall has done it twice, both times at the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]]'s request, and the Heavenly Scale Pavilion has never learned which of its contracts failed.

lore: In the Kingdom of Grave-Keepers the dead are buried with iron nails in the coffin lid, and a relative sleeps in a hut beside the grave for forty-nine days. Thieves come anyway, because a fresh body fetches a laborer's yearly wage in the City of Evening Light and a cultivator's corpse buys a farm. The ruling Kang family keeps a militia of grave guards and pays a bounty for every thief's head. Children learn grave-watch and staff fighting from eight. Spirit-rooted children are sent to the [[Vulture Burial Temple]] on the Roof, the only sect the Kang trust with bodies.
name: Kingdom of Grave-Keepers
summary: A farming and fishing kingdom where every family keeps watch over its graves. Corpse thieves raid the coast for bodies to sell across the strait, and the Grave-Keepers have learned to fight.
truth: The grave militia sells the bodies of the thieves it kills to the same buyers, and paid for the kingdom's new walls that way.

lore: Below the Hanging Curtain falls the Passing River splits into a hundred channels and feeds a crescent of oasis kingdoms: date groves, vineyards, spirit melon fields and poplar forests, watered by underground channels dug in the Dim Age. Every drop is allotted by the water court of the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]], which judges wells the way other courts judge murders. Each year the river's mouths close a few li further upstream, the tail oases die, and their people walk upstream with their goats into kingdoms that do not want them. Karez diggers, dew-gatherers and water diviners are the princes here.
name: Water's End
summary: The oases at the foot of the Sheer Wall, where the Roof's rivers fan out into inland deltas and die in the sand. The richest farmland in the Myriad Sands Continent, and it is shrinking.
truth: The river is not failing at the top. The Roof sends down as much water as ever; the delta is losing it into the ground, and the lost water slopes west toward the [[Thirsting Sands]].

lore: When the fragment struck it shattered, and splinters of Ladder jade are still found in the crater walls, each holding a trace of the arrays carved into the Ladder. The Broken Jade Workshop buys every splinter dug up, refines them over the crater's fire vein and sells the results at the Grand Auction: blades that cut space a little, rings that hold a room. Apprentices spend their first five years at the bellows and their first burn scar is a badge. The master is a Nascent Soul refiner who has not left the forge in eighty years.
name: Broken Jade Workshop
summary: Artifact refiners who buy splinters of Ladder jade dug from the crater walls and work them into artifacts nobody else can make.
truth: Some splinters still answer Upper Realm tokens, as the Fallen Ladder does. The Workshop sells those to the [[Armillary Pavilion]] alone, at ten times the price, and asks no questions.

lore: For eleven months the Butter Fair is three hundred stone houses and a monastery. In the twelfth, ten thousand tents go up and the butter is weighed on the temple's scales, one jar in ten taken as tithe. It is the only place on the high Roof where spirit stones are worth more than butter. Lowland alchemists buy worm-grass, the herb that is a caterpillar in winter and a blade of grass in summer, and pay double for live ones. Corpse buyers drink in the back rooms of the Red Door inn and call themselves salt merchants.
name: Butter Fair
summary: A market town on the high pastures where herders sell yak butter to the Thousand Lamps Temple's buyers each autumn, and lowlanders come up for snow lotus and worm-grass.

lore: An Ascent Age bronze guardian, rekeyed to a new master, fights at the realm it was built for, and the Workshop has learned to rekey them. It buys broken puppets from City-Opener crews and salvage captains, rebuilds them around new array cores and sells them to caravan houses, oasis kings and the Heavenly Scale Pavilion vaults. Apprentices learn puppetry, formations and casting, and spend their first year being knocked down by test puppets. The [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] has tried to buy the Workshop twice and burn it once, and the founder kept a puppet from each attempt.
name: Bronze Man Workshop
summary: Puppet makers at the port who rebuild Ascent Age guardian puppets dug from the Buried Cities and dragged up from the Shattered Sea, and sell them as guards that never sleep.
truth: Some rekeyed guardians still obey their first masters underneath. Three of the Workshop's puppets left their posts in the same month this year, all walking west.

lore: Once every eighteen years the sea draws back further than at any other time, and for seven days the cave at the foot of the Teeth stands dry. Inside, a gate opens on a shard world of shallow seas and drowned Ascent Age quays, with pearl beds and sunken cargo in water clear to the bottom. Cultivators up to Core Formation may enter; a Nascent Soul aura makes the shard's sea rise and fill the cave. The last opening was in 3,117, the next falls in 3,135, and the shark-folk claim the cave as theirs.
name: Cave of the Ebb Tide
summary: A sea cave on the fog coast that opens on a drowned shard world at the lowest tide of an eighteen-year cycle.

lore: Every caravan to the sea ends at the Harbor of Camels and Sails's camel yards, and every salvage ship unloads at its quays. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion, the Pavilion of True Assay and a dozen smaller houses keep appraisal stalls on the waterfront, and a lucky salvager can sell a sealed bronze box for a fortune before anyone opens it. The Port Syndicate, five shipping families, takes a twentieth of everything. Captains recruit crew in the Drowned Lamp tavern, where the pay is good and the odds of coming back are chalked on the wall.
name: Harbor of Camels and Sails
summary: The great port of the inner coast, where camel trains from Fallen Star City meet salvage ships from the Shattered Sea. Its quays are lined with appraisers and its taverns with liars.

lore: The Camel Bell Tribes travel in clans of a few hundred, each with a bell tuned so the worms hear it as wind. They own nothing that cannot ride a camel, and they hold the deep wells by memory, never maps. Children learn to smell water in sand at four and to sing the dune-songs that record which cities surfaced where. Chiefs sell guidance to looter crews for a share of the finds; crews that cheat them die of thirst a day from a well nobody mentioned. Spirit-rooted children go to the clan's dune-singers, who teach Earth and Wind arts.
name: Camel Bell Tribes
summary: Camel nomads of the deep dunes who read the sand like a book and know where the buried cities will surface next. They guide looters, and sometimes bury them.
truth: The oldest dune-songs describe the cities before the sand: green, rich, and singing about a lord under the river who must not be woken.

lore: The ruling council is drawn from star-watching families who have recorded the Stump's hum and the Mirror's width for five thousand years. They sell tide tables and Shattered Sea weather to salvage captains, and divination to anyone. Children learn the stars before the alphabet and are taught that the Pillar will be climbed again one day. The Kingdom That Watches the Pillar's harbor is where most salvage expeditions into the Shattered Sea set out, and its widows' quarter is the largest in the Myriad Sands Continent.
name: Kingdom That Watches the Pillar
summary: A port city-state on the cliffs facing the Stump. On clear nights the whole city climbs onto the roofs to watch the Pillar, and its astrologers sell what they see.
truth: The star families' records show the Stump's hum growing louder every decade. They have sold copies to the [[Armillary Pavilion]] and to a polite buyer who hums while he reads, and they did not recognize the [[Void Choir]] in him.

lore: The City of Evening Light's harbor faces the endless dusk, and its lamps are lit all day out of habit. Ships leave every morning on the five-month run to the Long Dusk Continent's sunlit coast, carrying salt, cloth and paying passengers; coffins ride in the holds and are not discussed. The Court of No Light's registry office, staffed by pale clerks who never eat, records every death in the city and issues passes to the living who want to visit the Pale City. Thousand Puppet Gate buyers keep a well-ventilated warehouse by the docks. The fish market is excellent.
name: City of Evening Light
summary: The port of the Last Light Shore, where ships leave for the Long Dusk Continent and the Court of No Light keeps a registry office. Everything that crosses the strait, living or dead, is counted here.

lore: The Kingdom of Fog Nets is ruled by the Net Mothers, a council of the oldest women, because the nets have always belonged to the women and the nets are water. A household's wealth is its net frames, and a marriage is a negotiation over net rights. Children wake in the dark to wring nets, and many learn the call for fog coming before their own names. Spirit-rooted children are rare and precious, and most are sold to the [[Gate of Gathered Dew]] for dew arrays. The Kingdom of Fog Nets hates the wreckers next door, whose false lights bring ships but also sea-clan reprisals.
name: Kingdom of Fog Nets
summary: Villages of fog nets on the dunes above the cold sea. Every family hangs fine nets before dawn, wrings them by sunrise and lives on what drips out.
truth: One of the Net Mothers is a shark-folk half-blood. She is the reason the Cold Tide Clan has never raided the Kingdom of Fog Nets, and the other Mothers know exactly what she is.

lore: At night the lamps of the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] can be seen from the sand a thousand li away, a line of light along the top of the Sheer Wall. Below it pilgrims climb the Prostration Stair one body-length at a time; above it lamp-makers, butter merchants and vow-keepers live off the temple. The Thousand Lamps Temple claims no land here and does not need to. When a monk's lamp goes out, the Askers walk down the stair to learn why, and nobody in the Eaves lies to an Asker twice. The temple's water court now sits every day, because the oases below are failing and every king is suing his neighbor.
name: The Eaves
summary: The southern lip of the Roof, where the plateau ends at the Sheer Wall and the Thousand Lamps Temple's thousand lamps burn along the edge. Pilgrims, vow-keepers, lamp-makers and the Askers.
top: Mahayana (a hidden monk in the Thousand Lamps Temple; the Abbot is Body Integration)
truth: One lamp in the deepest hall has not flickered in nine thousand years. Its monk is why the Askers always find their answer: he hears every lie told within sight of the Wall.

lore: The crust is a hand thick over most of the marsh and a finger thick in places nobody can see. Beneath it lies brine mud a hundred zhang deep that preserves whatever falls in, and drowned camels and men come up years later, pickled and perfect. Salt-cutters cross it in lines, probing with iron rods. The mud holds Dim Age caravans and their cargo, and divers in qi-shield arrays go down after it. Few come back up.
name: Brine-Crust Marsh
summary: A brine marsh under a salt crust, where the pan looks solid and isn't. Whole caravans have broken through and vanished into the black mud beneath.

lore: The Kingdom of Mended Antiquities's guild houses take broken artifacts from the Buried Cities and the Shattered Sea and make them whole: recasting bronze, recutting jade, re-inking faded arrays. Apprentices learn the scripts and maker's marks of every Ascent Age school, and the guild's ancient-style refining is the best in the Myriad Sands Continent. The town is ruled by the Masters' Table. Its children grow up among bronze filings and old scripts, and they are taught never to say the word copy. Every appraiser in Fallen Star City knows the guild by name.
name: Kingdom of Mended Antiquities
summary: A town of master restorers in the eastern canyons who mend Ascent Age relics broken by looters. Their work is so good that the relics sometimes look better than new.
truth: Most of what Kingdom of Mended Antiquities sells was never broken, because it never existed. The guild forges Ascent Age relics from scratch, and its work has sold at three Grand Auctions.

lore: Blood Sand disciples cultivate a Saber Dao fed on blood: each kill is drawn into the blade and dried into red sand that hardens the body. They hold three canyon forts, raid caravans that do not pay, sell captives to corpse buyers and the Thirsting Heart Sect, and sell safe passage to those who do pay. The sect recruits by offer: survivors of a raid are asked whether they would rather join or die, and most join. The [[Temple of the Merciful Blade]] kills them, they kill the Temple of the Merciful Blade's monks, and the caravan houses pay both.
name: Blood Sand Gate
summary: A demonic bandit sect in the red canyons that robs the coast road. They turn their victims' blood into sand, and they claim the canyon floors are red because of them.
truth: The Blood Sand Gate's master is the younger brother of the Temple of the Merciful Blade's abbot. They meet each year at the Dead Falls to agree how many of each other's people to kill.

lore: The Turquoise Mane has ruled the ridge for nine hundred years, and his pride of forty grown snow lions is the strongest beast power on the Roof. By the pact sworn with the [[Lion's Roar Cloister]]'s founder, the lions fight raiders on the ice and the monks never tame a cub. Herders on the ridge pay a yak a month and are left alone; the Black Yak Tribes refuse and lose ten. A lion's roar here can bring down a cornice, and avalanches are how they hunt. Beast tamers who try to steal cubs are found in spring.
name: Snow Lion Ridge
summary: A ridge of high crags ruled by a pride of snow lions under a Nascent Soul lion with a turquoise mane. The monks and the lions keep an old pact.
truth: The pact's full text, kept in the Cloister, gives the lions one human child every hundred years. The monks have paid it eight times and told no one.

lore: The Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings live in houses cut into both walls of the gorge a thousand zhang above the white water, and cross between them on rope bridges that sway in the wind. The Bridge Elders set the toll by the river's height. Children are lowered on ropes to gather cliff swallow nests, which medicine halls buy as a lung tonic. A Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings who drops a caravan's cargo owes its value; one who drops a passenger owes a life. Raiders who attack the bridges find the ropes cut behind them.
name: Kingdom of the Cliff Dwellings
summary: Cliff villages in the Milk River Gorge, joined by rope bridges and ladders. Their people hold the only crossing for five hundred li and ferry caravans over it.
truth: The Bridge Elders pay the [[Blood Sand Gate]] a tenth of every toll, and in return the sect robs every caravan that tries the fords instead.

lore: The Kingdom of Salt Houses cuts salt in blocks from the pan's crust, builds with it and sells the rest by the camel-load. The ruling Ban family has held the cutting rights for twelve centuries and set the price of salt from Fallen Star City to the Roof, until the sea-salt pans on the coast began undercutting it. Children grow up licking the walls, which their mothers forbid, and cut their first block at ten. Spirit-rooted children learn the Salt Body, a slow tempering that makes flesh resist rot and poison. A rare rain is a disaster: whole streets slump in a night.
name: Kingdom of Salt Houses
summary: A salt kingdom on the edge of the pan whose houses, walls and palace are built of salt blocks. It never rains, so they never melt, and the king fears clouds.
truth: The Ban family has hired the Gate of the Empty City to lure sea-salt caravans into the pan. Three have vanished this year.

lore: The Pavilion was founded by appraisers who walked out of the Heavenly Scale Pavilion over a forged lot, and it lives on one promise: it will appraise against anyone, the Heavenly Scale Pavilion included. Its masters read age, origin and curse from a shard by touch, and its ledger of Ascent Age maker's marks is the best in the Myriad Sands Continent. Apprenticeship lasts ten years and begins with a year of sorting sand by grain. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion tolerates it because buyers trust an auction more when a rival has checked the lots, and hates it for the same reason.
name: Pavilion of True Assay
summary: The world's second appraisal house, and the only one Heavenly Scale Pavilion does not own. Its seal on a certificate can double an item's price at auction.
truth: Its founder left because he found that a third of the Grand Auction's Ascent Age relics were made in the Withered Rivers. The Pavilion of True Assay still has his notes and has never published them.

lore: Families climb the cliff with lanterns, food and the names of the drowned written on paper boats. At midnight on the fifteenth, when the [[Nether Shard]] is closest, figures walk up out of the water, the newly dead first. Most want only to see their families once. Some want more, and the Grave-Keepers stand at the top with iron staffs. Ghost cultivators come to meditate in the yin tide, which is stronger here than anywhere else in the Myriad Sands Continent, and make the villagers nervous.
name: Cliff of Welcoming Souls
summary: A sea cliff where the shore villages gather in the seventh month to welcome back their dead. On the fifteenth night the dead walk up out of the strait to meet them.

lore: The beam is a gate only while the sun is overhead, about an hour, and anyone below Core Formation who steps in during that hour is carried into a shard world of red stone towers and fire springs. The way out is the largest spring, which throws people back onto the canyon floor each time it erupts; the eruptions stop after thirty days. Fire-element herbs grow around the vents, guarded by salamanders. The canyon fits about two hundred people, and the fighting for places starts a month early. The next midsummer noon is in 3,133.
name: One Thread of Sky
summary: The narrowest slot canyon in the Withered Rivers. Every twenty-one years, at noon on midsummer day, a single beam of sunlight reaches its floor and becomes a gate for one hour.

lore: On fog nights the lamps of the Kingdom of Luring Lamps look exactly like a harbor. Ships that steer for them break on the Teeth, and by dawn the wreckers are stripping the hulls. The ruling Gou family, two Foundation cultivators and a Core Formation patron nobody sees, takes half of every wreck. The Kingdom of Luring Lamps children learn to swim in surf that kills outsiders and to keep their mouths shut. The Cold Tide Clan takes its share too, which is why the shark-folk leave the wreckers alone. Salvage goes inland through Whalebone Harbor with forged papers.
name: Kingdom of Luring Lamps
summary: A wreckers' principality whose lords hang false lamps on the dunes to draw ships onto the shoals. Its people are rich in salvage and poor in friends.
truth: Last spring the lamps brought in a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] ship. The Gou family has its cargo and three of its crew in the cellars, and has not decided which is more dangerous to keep.

lore: Herders say the range is the spine of a god who lay down to keep the Roof from blowing away. Its passes close for seven months a year and are strung with the Kingdom of Sutra Flags sutra flags. Snow leopards hunt the lower flanks and the hermits of the [[Crown-Touching Peak]] keep the upper. Ice cultivators cut thousand-year ice from its north faces, which fetch a mid-grade stone a block in Fallen Star City.
name: Jade Bone Range
summary: The crest range of the High Roof: white peaks running east from the outer coast, with the Crown-Touching Peak at the top. Its snows feed every river on the continent.

lore: Look south from any beach in the Last Light Shore and the horizon glows like an evening that never finishes: the twilight of the [[Long Dusk Continent]] under the shadow of the [[Fallen Ladder]]. The coast is cool and heavy with yin qi, which ghost cultivators love and farmers hate. In the seventh month, when the [[Nether Shard]] passes close, the dead drift north across the strait, and the shore villages set out food and bar their doors. The rest of the year the ports ferry the living to the Long Dusk Continent's sunlit coasts, and the dead as well: bodies from the Roof and the sand go aboard here for the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] buyers.
name: The Last Light Shore
summary: The Myriad Sands Continent's southern shore, facing the Long Dusk Continent across the strait. The southern sky never quite darkens or brightens, ghosts cross the water in the seventh month, and the corpse road ends at its ports.
truth: The [[Court of No Light]] counts the Myriad Sands Continent's dead from its registry office in the City of Evening Light as carefully as its own, and is preparing a legal claim on every soul that dies within sight of the strait.

lore: The spring's overflow leaves the crater through a tunnel cut in the Dim Age and spreads into fields of alfalfa, dates and spirit rice below the rim. The Kingdom of the Overflow feeds Fallen Star City, and Fallen Star City could close the tunnel any day. The ruling Fang family pays water rent to the city council, keeps no army and marries its daughters to the Heavenly Scale Pavilion stewards. Children grow up with the roar of the tunnel in their ears and a fear of its silence. Whenever the flow drops, the kingdom panics, and the Fang buy another decade with another daughter.
name: Kingdom of the Overflow
summary: A small oasis kingdom watered by the overflow of Fallen Star City's crater spring. It is green, rich and entirely at Fallen Star City's mercy.
truth: The overflow has fallen by a third in a century. Fallen Star City's council has already voted, in secret, to close the tunnel when it falls by half.

lore: When the dunes part, a hundred towers stand up out of the sand in rows, joined by bridges at their thirtieth floors. They are full of sand to that height and empty above, with bronze doors, cold arrays and guardian puppets that wake when touched. Each uncovering lasts about a year before the sand returns, and for that year the Ruins of the Jade Towers is the busiest place in the Myriad Sands Continent. The last was in 3,098. The next is not expected until 3,138, but the dunes over it are already thinning, and claim-jumpers are camped on the crest.
name: Ruins of the Jade Towers
summary: The largest buried city yet found: a district of jade towers that the dunes uncover about every forty years. The House of City-Openers has dug it four times and never reached its center.

lore: Nobody knows how a ship built for the sky came to rest here. The dunes cover and uncover it every few decades, and right now its prow stands clear, hung with fog nets by the Kingdom of Fog Nets villagers who think it lucky. Its hull is warded by arrays that still burn anyone who cuts at it, and the hatches answer only to an Ascent Age token. Formation masters camp beside it for years trying to read the wards, which are said to include a flying array nobody alive can make.
name: Tomb of the Cloud Ship
summary: An Ascent Age cloud-ship half buried in the dunes twenty thousand li inland, its bronze keel longer than a city wall. Its upper decks are stripped; its holds are still sealed.
truth: The ship came down the Heaven Ladder, not up it. The log sealed in the captain's cabin names who was aboard, and some of those names are carried today by families in the Floating Peak Continent.

lore: Half the clerks in the Heavenly Scale Pavilion branches around the world were trained in the Kingdom of Counting Houses's counting schools, where a child who can sum ten thousand figures by sight is worth more than one with a spirit root. The Guild of Ledgers governs, and its prisons are offices: debtors bound by karmic oath sit at desks until the debt is paid, and their children inherit what is left. Spirit-rooted clerks learn the Abacus Heart, a Karma method that lets them feel when a number lies. The money market changes any currency in the world, at the worst rates in the world.
name: Kingdom of Counting Houses
summary: A city-state of clerks on the east road, where the Heavenly Scale Pavilion's debtors work off what they owe. Its children learn the abacus before they learn to talk.
truth: Some of the Kingdom of Counting Houses's debts were bought, not lent. A Guild bureau buys bad debts on six continents and brings the debtors here through the Fallen Star City array.

lore: The gate stays open for nine nights and admits only Qi Condensation cultivators: a Foundation aura shatters the reflection and closes it for everyone. Inside is a shard world of wind and snow, the outer court of an Ascent Age wind sect, where frost cranes nest and wind-pattern jade forms in the drifts. The Kingdom of Sutra Flags monasteries send their herder children in with shopping lists. The next opening is in 3,129, and lowland sects are already renting tent ground on the shore.
name: Mirror-Gazing Lake
summary: A glacier lake that holds the Mirror's reflection. Every twelve years, when the Mirror stands straight overhead at midnight, the reflection becomes a gate.
truth: The wind sect sealed its techniques in the frost cranes. Kill a crane and its method is lost; tame one and, in time, it teaches.

lore: Everyone in the Kingdom of Candlelight works for the lamps: butter clarifiers, wick spinners, bronze casters, scripture copyists. The Ling family rules as Lamp Wardens; every first son goes to the temple at seven, and the second sons fight over the throne. Children learn the hundred and eight prostrations before they can read. Those with spirit roots go to the temple's outer court and come home a year later with shaved heads or not at all. This year the Thousand Lamps Temple raised the lamp tithe by a third, and the Warden is quietly buying lowland butter at a loss to cover it.
name: Kingdom of Candlelight
summary: The lamp-makers' kingdom on the plateau behind the Thousand Lamps Temple. It pays its taxes in butter, wicks and sons, and its kings have been temple vassals for four thousand years.
truth: The tithe rose because nine hundred new lamps were lit last year, more than in any year since the Outer Demon War. The temple is recruiting, and it has not said what for.

lore: The tribes temper their bodies in blizzards and fight bare-handed to show contempt. A tribe's chief is whoever can lift the clan's ancestor stone. Every few generations they unite under a Great Khan and ride south across the ice, and every coast they reach remembers why it built walls.
name: Iron Bone Tribes
summary: Nomad clans of the Black Frost Continent's southern steppe who cultivate the body instead of qi. Some carry giant blood.
top: Deity Transformation (two war chiefs; the Bone Ancestor waking)
truth: The Bone Ancestor sleeping inside Ancestor Mountain is a Deity Transformation body cultivator from the Dim Age, and he is waking up. Two war chiefs have quietly reached Deity Transformation in body. The tribes only count the Ancestor.

lore: The League meets in Ten Thousand Sails when an outside power threatens the islands, and otherwise robs itself.
name: Thousand Isles League
summary: Island sects, pirate lords and free ports, allied only against anyone who tries to rule them.
truth: Half the League's pirate lords pay tribute to the Azure Wave Palace for safe passage. The other half don't know. Three of the League's island masters are at Deity Transformation, and each believes the other two are not.

lore: At low tide reef roads join each island to the next. A mortal who walks the whole chain spends about two years on it, and a Foundation cultivator who flies the gaps about six weeks, if nothing eats them. Every frontier war of the last thousand years started on these islands.
name: Jade Strait
summary: The strait between the Morning Star Continent and the Vast Wilds Continent, some thirty thousand li of sea crossed by a chain of islands that humans and beasts both claim.

lore: A Jar-Mother seals a hundred venomous creatures in a jar and lets them fight until one remains; that one becomes the Gu. Their villages hang in miasma no outsider can breathe. They trade antidotes to Apricot Grove Valley and curses to anyone who pays, and they have never lost a war, because nobody who starts one survives the year.
name: Jar-Mother Clans
summary: Matriarchal Gu-raising clans of the Vast Wilds Continent's poison valleys. Harm one, and every Gu in the valleys remembers your scent.
truth: The eldest Jar-Mother keeps a Gu that has eaten a Nascent Soul. It is the real reason the Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains leaves the valleys alone. She reached Deity Transformation forty years ago and lets the clans believe she is still Nascent Soul.

lore: Ten million mortals, a hundred thousand cultivators, walls no Core Formation cultivator can break, and a palace array nobody has ever tested.
name: Jing Capital
summary: Capital of the Great Jing Dynasty and the largest city in the world, built over three spirit veins. A hub of the Heavenly Circuit.
top: Body Integration (the Ancestor Emperor, in the palace)

lore: The Grand Auction of Fallen Star City is held every ten years and sets prices for the world. A spring rose in the crater after the fragment struck, and it is the only reason a city can live there.
name: Fallen Star City
summary: The world's greatest market, built inside a crater a falling piece of the Ladder left in the Sand Sea. Seat of the Heavenly Scale Pavilion and a hub of the Heavenly Circuit.

lore: Mortals pray to the Mirror as Heaven. Cultivators know it as the Upper Realm, where ascension leads. Severed Heaven swings around it on a long, lopsided orbit of about ninety thousand years. When the world draws close, the Mirror's qi spills across the gap: the High Tide. When it swings away, qi thins: the Ebb. The Mirror has been widening in the sky for twenty-five thousand years.
name: The Mirror
summary: The great thousand world that Severed Heaven circles. It hangs in the night sky as a pale disc three times the width of the moon, and it is slowly growing.
truth: The Mirror's immortals cut the Heaven Ladder from their end. They have not forgotten Severed Heaven, and they are watching the tide too.

lore: Ghost Month is Severed Heaven's oldest festival and its most dangerous. Souls of the newly dead drift toward the Nether Shard as it passes, which is why rebirth is uncertain and why Ghost Way cultivators grow fastest in the seventh month.
name: The Nether Shard
summary: A cold shard world drenched in yin. Each year in the seventh month it passes closest, the barrier thins, and the dead walk.
truth: Under the Fallen Ladder the barrier to the Nether Shard never fully closes. Things come through that were never alive in Severed Heaven.

lore: Night Banquet Sect cultivators devour qi from the living, and they do it with exquisite manners. They run the black markets of half of the Morning Star Continent, buy secrets from every court, and hold a banquet each new moon to which rival cultivators are invited. Not all of them leave. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has sworn three times to burn them out.
name: Night Banquet Sect
summary: An aristocratic demonic sect in the Morning Star Continent's southern marshes. Every guest at their banquets is either a diner or the meal.
truth: The Banquet Master reached Deity Transformation sixty years ago and is hiding it, waiting for the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's ancestor to die.

lore: Each clan carries a bloodline: thunder, crane, qilin and six more. Their children are born with it awake or not at all, and those without it are sent down to the ground to serve. They marry among themselves, sneer at every sect founded after the Severance, and settle disputes by duel on an arena floating above the clouds.
name: Conclave of Nine Clans
summary: Nine bloodline clans that claim descent from the Age of the Ascent and hold the floating peaks of the Floating Peak Continent.
truth: Three of the nine bloodlines come from Upper Realm envoys who stayed after the Severance. The Conclave's Old Ancestor is a Mahayana who still remembers the Mirror's language. Below him, the First Elder is at Body Integration and three clan ancestors are at Void Refinement.

lore: The Court registers every death under the Fallen Ladder, judges each soul and assigns it a place. Living visitors need a pass, paid in years of lifespan. The Pale Sovereign has ruled since the Severance; she was there when the Ladder fell, and she has never said what she saw.
meaning: Court of No Light (also: Court of Ignorance)
name: Court of No Light
summary: The ghost court that rules the Long Dusk Continent's dead from the Pale City, with laws, registers and judges older than any sect.
truth: The Sealer's name was erased from the living, not the dead. The Pale Sovereign remembers it and keeps it as leverage. Under her, the Chief Judge is a Body Integration ghost and two judges sit at Void Refinement.

lore: Streets of white stone, lanterns that burn without heat, and a market where a ghost will sell you a dead man's memories by the ounce.
name: The Pale City
summary: Capital of the dead under the Fallen Ladder. Living travelers arrive by array among ghosts and pay for their stay in years.

lore: Each monk who takes vows lights a life lamp in the great hall; when a lamp goes out, the temple knows its monk has died and sends someone to ask why. The Thousand Lamps Temple arbitrates disputes for all sides because it claims no territory. Its arhats will not kill, but they will beat a demonic cultivator to within an inch of his life and then offer to shave his head.
name: Thousand Lamps Temple
summary: The great Buddhist monastery on the Roof of the Myriad Sands Continent, where a lamp burns for every monk alive.
top: Mahayana (a hidden monk; the Abbot is Body Integration)
truth: The Thousand Lamps Temple owns the water rights to two thirds of the Myriad Sands Continent's oases, and its compassion has a price list. A monk in the deepest hall has been meditating for nine thousand years and reached Mahayana without telling anyone. The Abbot is at Body Integration and believes he is the temple's peak.

lore: The Morning Star Continent holds more people than the other five continents together. The Great Jing Dynasty rules its mortal heartland, the Clear Heaven Sword Sect rules its northern peaks, and Apricot Grove Valley sells pills to both. In the southern marshes, the Night Banquet Sect waits for any of them to stumble. The continent's southwest tip nearly touches the Vast Wilds Continent across the Jade Strait, and that frontier is where humans and beasts bleed each other.
name: Morning Star Continent
summary: The human heartland: great river plains, cloud-wrapped sect peaks and more kingdoms than anyone has counted. Most lives start here.
top: Body Integration (the Ancestor Emperor, unseen and rumored dying)
truth: The three spirit veins under Jing Capital are being drained to keep the Ancestor Emperor alive, and the heartland's harvests are failing because of it.

lore: Entry is the Sword Stair: nine thousand nine hundred steps, each heavier than the last, climbed in front of the whole sect. Rank is decided by duels. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect calls itself the shield of the righteous and keeps a list of demonic cultivators it means to kill; the Night Banquet Sect's master has topped it for four hundred years.
name: Clear Heaven Sword Sect
summary: The Morning Star Continent's foremost sword sect, on seventy-two peaks in the north. Proud, rule-bound and very good at killing.
top: Void Refinement (the founding ancestor, silent in seclusion)
truth: The founding ancestor, a Void Refinement sword cultivator, is still in seclusion under the main peak. He stopped answering summons two hundred years ago, and the elders are afraid to look.

features.name: fields plowed with spears at hand

lore: The Gongsuns have held the march for nine generations and buried most of their sons on the wall. Every family owes one child to the garrison at sixteen. Rooted children are another matter: since the raids tripled, the Gongsuns hold a frontier charter, so the Registry's frontier tester comes at twelve, the age the march can put a child on the wall, and the garrison keeps every rooted child for its cadet school instead of sending them to the capital. Children here learn to read beast tracks before letters and to tell a raid horn from a hunt horn. A beast core turned in at a fort earns a bounty in rice or stones.
name: March of Pacified Borders
summary: The empire's frontier march, ruled by the Gongsun family of generals. Farmers plow with spears at hand, and every village has a watchtower and a beast-pit.

ties.why: Lady Gongsun sends cores and captives to Shared Roost for the weapons the capital stopped sending.
Our garrisons hold the wall's southern stretch, and every cadet learns it by patrolling it.
Stone Eyes is ours on every imperial map, yet its clans pay no tax and send no sons to the wall.
We hold the march for the dynasty, though the capital has stopped sending the weapons to do it.

truth: Lady Gongsun Wei, the general's widow, has been trading cores and captives to Shared Roost City to buy the weapons the capital stopped sending.

lore: Ships for the outer ocean leave from the Harbor of Stilled Waves, and every one pays twice: once to the empire and once to the sea clans' shark-folk factor, who keeps an office on the quay. Thunderwood, storm-pearls, lightning ink and puppets go out; sea silver and deep-sea herbs come in. Sailors swear the Rim's roar can be heard from the outer breakwater on windless nights.
name: Harbor of Stilled Waves
summary: The one safe harbor on the storm coast, behind a breakwater built by cultivators. The Azure Wave Palace's toll office and the empire's customs house face each other across the quay.

lore: The range is the reason the east coast feels like another country: three passes cross it, all taxed. Its western slopes feed the heartland rivers; its eastern slopes drop straight to the sea. Mines, forges and hermit caves dot its length, and fire-backed rock lizards bask on its warm cliffs. Every earthquake, villagers say the turtle turned over in its sleep.
name: Turtle-Spine Mountains
summary: The volcanic range down the Morning Star Continent's east side, separating the heartland plains from the outer coast. Legend says it is the shell ridge of a sleeping turtle.

lore: Every household in the Kingdom of a Hundred Herbs owes the Apricot Grove Valley a quota of herbs, and every quota is a little higher than last year's. The king is an Apricot Grove Valley outer disciple's nephew. Children learn herb lore at five, identify a hundred plants by smell at ten and can recite their family's debt at twelve. Rooted children are sent to the valley as apprentices, never to the Registry, and the empire looks away because it needs the Apricot Grove Valley's pills.
name: Kingdom of a Hundred Herbs
summary: A tenant kingdom that grows herbs for the Apricot Grove Valley on contracts its grandparents signed. Its fields are healthy, its people well fed, and nobody is allowed to leave the debt.

lore: White Sands grows spirit palms whose nuts feed beasts, gathers sea-turtle eggs and pays the Registry tester to visit every twelve years. Its queen is ninety and has outlived three heirs. Pirate raids take a few children every year, and the fleet comes too late. A hidden cove holds a wrecked Ascent Age ship in the dunes, which local children play in and adults avoid.
name: Kingdom of White Sands
summary: A sleepy coastal kingdom of dunes, palm groves and turtle beaches, ruled by an old mortal queen. Pirates take its children; nobody else remembers it exists.
truth: The wreck's hold is sealed and still warm.

lore: Across the [[Jade Strait]] lies beast country, and at low tide the island chain is a road in both directions, though walking it island to island is a season's travel at the least. Spirit beasts work north along the chain to raid herds and villages; human sects go over to hunt cores, eggs and herbs; half-bloods and smugglers pass goods island by island, by night, toward [[Shared Roost City]]. The empire holds the coast with fortress towns and conscript garrisons, and pays for every beast core brought in. The karst is honeycombed with caves where raiders, smugglers and beasts all hide. Raids have tripled in five years, and the beasts coming over are older.
name: The Border Wilds
summary: Karst hills on the Morning Star Continent's southwest coast where the island chain to Vast Wilds begins. Beasts raid, smugglers cross at low tide and every family owes a child to the wall.

ties.why: Walkers, poachers and smugglers leave our coast down the chain, and cores come back up it.

truth: The Beast Court is not sending the raids. Old beasts are waking in the Vast Wilds Continent's mountains and driving the young ones north across the strait.

lore: The rot spreads by spores that cling to cloth and skin, and the Apricot Grove Valley has ordered a cordon around the gardens. Inside, the blight has bred strange herbs, black lingzhi and weeping ginseng that alchemists will pay for and that may be poison. Herb thieves go in masked and come out coughing.
name: The Sick Gardens
summary: The blighted terraces and lingzhi caves of the Kingdom of Lingzhi Gardens, where black rot spreads to anything living. Mutant herbs grow in the rot.

lore: The Grain-Barge Mouth stands where the Grand Canal meets the [[Imperial River]], half a year west of the capital by barge. Bargemen's guilds, granary clerks and the Registry's holding pens share its waterfront. A Heavenly Scale Pavilion branch here changes spirit stones and writes grain futures, and the bathhouses sell forged test slips at three low-grade stones apiece. Gangs of qi-laborers who failed the Registry fight for loading rights at night.
name: Grain-Barge Mouth
summary: The canal port where grain barges from the whole heartland unload for the Jing Capital. Its granaries are the largest in the world and, this year, half empty.

lore: Prince Rui reached Core Formation at forty and wants the throne before his uncles can agree on anyone else. His kingdom is orchards, horse farms and a spear academy that takes any rooted youth who passes the Registry and fails the palace cut. He hires rogue cultivators by the season, buys formation flags from anyone, and pays a bounty for proof of his cousins' crimes. Mortals here eat better than anywhere else in the domain, because the prince quietly stopped sending his grain quota to the capital.
name: Kingdom of Lasting Peace
summary: The fief of Prince Rui, the Ancestor Emperor's ninth-generation grandson, a spear prodigy who drills his household guard as if the succession war started yesterday.
truth: The prince's 'grain shortfall' is stockpiled in a cave granary under his horse farms, enough to feed an army for two years.

lore: The South of the Tides is the empire's sea gate: grain, iron and silk go out to the [[Thousand Isles]], and pearls, sea silver and island herbs come back. Every voyage pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s toll and risks the pirate lords, which keeps the war junks of the southern fleet busy and the merchant houses rich. The fleet also ferries troops and supplies west to the Jade Strait frontier. Since the harvests failed, grain exports are banned, so the grain goes out at night instead.
name: South of the Tides
summary: The Morning Star Continent's southern tip, facing the Thousand Isles across open sea. The empire's southern fleet anchors here, and so does most of the continent's legal trade with the islands.
truth: The fleet's commander is Prince Rui's man. If the succession comes to war, the southern fleet will decide who controls the sea road to the frontier.

lore: Inside is a shallow drowned world of coral forests and tide pools full of spirit shellfish, pearls and water herbs. The cave floods on the third evening, and those still inside wait a year. Salt lords and the Tide-Watching Pavilion sell guides and tide tables; the Azure Wave Palace's shark-folk watch the cave mouth and take a share of whatever comes out.
name: Tidal Realm
summary: A shard world whose gate sits in a sea cave that is dry only at the lowest tide of the year. It stays open for three days, and only those below Foundation can pass.

lore: The bay is full of salvage: cargo, artifacts, ship's spirit stones and the bones of their owners. Iron-jawed reef eels nest in the hulls, ghost lights lead divers astray in Ghost Month, and the Kingdom of Surf Rocks's wreckers kill rival salvagers on sight. A Thousand Isles treasure ship went down here forty years ago, and its pirate owners still send divers.
name: Bay of Sunken Ships
summary: A reef-choked bay where a thousand years of wrecks lie stacked in shallow water. Reef eels, ghost lights and wreckers all hunt there.

lore: The Wind-Riding Gate teaches flight before fighting: disciples ride spirit kites in the dust storms until they can ride the wind alone. The sect holds the imperial courier contract for the north, carrying sealed letters faster than horses. It recruits light, quick children from the cave villages and trains them to read the sky. Its couriers know everyone's secrets and are paid not to.
name: Wind-Riding Gate
summary: A Wind Dao sect on the plateau's edge whose disciples fly on kites and gusts. The empire's fastest couriers wear its badge.

lore: The Turtle-Spine Mountains run hot here. Fire veins feed forges that supply half of the Morning Star Continent's artifact refiners, imperial convicts dig spirit ore in penal pits, and the [[Imperial River]] and the [[Flood River]] both rise on its slopes. Last spring a mid-grade vein surfaced in a collapsed valley, and every clan, sect and desperate miner in the east came running. The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] claims all new veins, the Blazing Furnace Sect claims everything in its forges' sight, and the claim-jumpers claim whatever they can hold until morning.
name: The Red Rocks
summary: Volcanic highlands along the Morning Star Continent's eastern spine: mines, forges, convict pits and a new spirit vein that broke the surface last year and started a stampede.
truth: The new vein is not natural. It is the core of an Ascent Age fire array waking with the tide, and the whole range is its wall.

lore: The City of First Sun trades salt, eastern silk and thunderwood for sea silver, deep-sea pearls and whatever the Thousand Isles are selling. The Azure Wave Palace's factor keeps a pavilion on the water, and no ship leaves without his seal. The city is the Dawn League's purse, and the imperial governor knows it. Sailors say the Morning Star rises here first, which is how Morning Star got its name.
name: City of First Sun
summary: The east's great port, where the sun rises first and ships leave for the outer ocean. Its quay has a toll office for the sea clans and a gallows for smugglers.

lore: Mist from the inner sea condenses on the ridge and keeps the valley wet. Wild herbs here are hundreds of years old, and the Apricot Grove Valley's ridge patrols arrest anyone picking them without a permit. Medicinal snakes and blue-tailed herb foxes live in the cliffs. The western slope looks out over the inner sea.
name: Jade Screen Ridge
summary: A green ridge that shields Apricot Grove Valley from the sea winds. Wild herbs grow on its slopes, and the Apricot Grove Valley's patrols guard the passes.

lore: The Cinnabar Hill Sect teaches alchemy through the Fire Dao and refuses to grow its own herbs anymore, buying everything from outside the Apricot Grove Valley's network: Vast Wilds smugglers, shard-realm teams, the marsh. It recruits alchemy talents the Apricot Grove Valley rejected, and it pays bounties for proof of the blight. Its Nascent Soul master has sworn to burn the apricot forest if the proof comes.
name: Cinnabar Hill Sect
summary: The Apricot Grove Valley's last rival in alchemy, on a red hill east of the valley. Its gardens are dying, its masters are furious and its pills are still very good.
truth: The Cinnabar Hill Sect's master is buying blight samples from the Netherworm Stockade to make a blight of his own.

lore: The Imperial Geomancy Office keeps a hall by the wells and logs the mist's height each dawn. Apprentice geomancers can be hired cheaply to read graves and fields, and the office sells its old logs to anyone with a court seal. Pilgrims drink the well water for long life. This year the mist barely clears the well lips, and the office has stopped letting outsiders look.
name: Earth Dragon Wells
summary: Nine ancient wells on the plain east of the Jing Capital where vein qi seeps up as warm mist. Geomancers have read the capital's veins here for two thousand years.
truth: Anyone who compares the logs will see the mist has fallen by half in three centuries, starting the year the Ancestor Emperor withdrew.

lore: The eastern kingdoms were old when the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] conquered them, and behind the mountains they still behave as if the conquest were temporary. They pay tax late, test children for the Registry with suspicious results, and trade with the outer sea on their own terms with the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s toll collectors. The harvest failures in the heartland have raised the grain levy on the east twice in two years. Now the eastern kings meet in secret, and the empire has started stationing spear cultivators at the passes.
name: The Eastern Corner
summary: The Morning Star Continent's outer east coast behind the Turtle-Spine passes: old kingdoms, salt pans and ports that see the sun first, and that remember being free.
truth: The Dawn League has been offered help by the Night Banquet. The price is the passes, and the League's elder council is about to say yes.

lore: Inside is a battlefield from the Ascent Age, frozen at the moment a sword array broke: shards of immortal swords stuck in floating stone, and sword-phantoms that still fight each other. A single shard can be refined into a Core Formation flying sword. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect controls the gate and sells forty places to outsiders by auction. The next opening is in eleven years, and the auction has already begun.
name: Realm of Broken Edges
summary: A shard world whose gate opens on the sixty-ninth peak for one month every thirty years. Only cultivators below Core Formation can enter.

features.name: the patrol walk along the top
the old sections faced with cart-sized skulls
bone heaps waiting to be built in

lore: Each garrison adds the bones of the beasts it kills, and the oldest sections are faced with skulls the size of carts. Beast spirits haunt it in the seventh month, and ghost-hunters and bone-collectors come then. Old bones from the wall are a refining material for beast-taming whistles and Slaughter Dao artifacts, and stealing them is a hanging offense. The [[March of Pacified Borders]] garrisons the southern stretch, and its cadets learn the wall by patrolling it.
name: The Wall of Piled Bones
summary: A wall of earth and beast bones along the coastal hills, built over a thousand years of raids. On Ghost Month nights the bones howl.

ties.why: The Gongsun garrisons man the southern stretch and add their kills to the bones.

lore: The dike runs for hundreds of li along the inner coast, and its lanterns burn at night with a pale qi flame. Formation masters study its arrays, which no living sect can reproduce, and thieves pry out its stones for their array cores. Prying out a stone is a capital crime under a law nobody has enforced in centuries, until this year.
name: Demon-Warding Dike
summary: A seawall three thousand years old, built in the Outer Demon War with warding arrays in every stone. Most of Morning Star thinks it is a relic.

lore: The pirate lord Red-Sleeve Gao holds the ruins with a few hundred raiders, a captured war junk and a formation that turns the harbor into a maze of fog. The fleet has attacked twice and lost twice. Captives are held in the old customs cellars until ransomed or sold. Gao pays well for information about convoys.
name: Dead Harbor
summary: A port sacked by Thousand Isles pirates fifty years ago and never rebuilt. A pirate lord uses its ruins as a mainland base.

lore: Inside is a sky of endless wind and floating rocks, where wind-crystal clusters grow on the windward faces. A crystal can carry a Wind Dao cultivator to Foundation. The gate stays open twenty days, and the storm outside kills as many applicants as the realm does. The Wind-Riding Gate sells guided entry; the cave villages sell it cheaper and guide worse.
name: Realm of the Wind Cave
summary: A shard world whose gate opens in a loess wind cave during the autumn dust storms every nine years. Only cultivators below Foundation can pass.

lore: In the Beneath the Peaks the empire's law runs up the valleys and stops where the terraces end; above them, the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] and its vassal sects rule from peaks you can see from every paddy. The Registry tests children at six. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect's recruiters come at nine with the Sword Stair trial, and they do not ask whether a child is registered. Villages hide their best children in hay carts, smugglers guide them up the mountain roads, and imperial bounty hunters wait at the passes. The upper terraces still yield; the lower ones, on imperial land, have started to fail.
name: Beneath the Peaks
summary: Terraced foothills between the capital plain and the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's peaks, where sect mountains rise straight out of the rice fields and two masters claim every rooted child.
truth: The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has quietly doubled its recruiting since its founder fell silent. The sect masters want more swords before anyone tests them.

lore: The Wave-Quelling Gate recruits sailors' children and drills them on decks until they can fight in a storm. Its three spirit ships patrol the coast, and its bounties are posted in every port. It holds an imperial commission and a quiet arrangement with two pirate lords, whose rivals it hunts with real zeal. It hires outside cultivators for raids on pirate nests.
name: Wave-Quelling Gate
summary: An orthodox sect of pirate hunters who fight from spirit ships with spear and Water Dao. They collect imperial bounties and pirate bribes with the same hand.

lore: Anything banned anywhere in the Morning Star Continent is sold here: stolen sect manuals, Registry slips, demonic techniques, Gu, beast cores from protected species and people. Prices are in spirit stones or favors, and favors are worse. The Night Banquet runs the market and guarantees its peace; fighting aboard means being served at the next banquet. Lantern tokens sell in the City of Pecks and Bushels and Blackwater for a mid-grade stone.
name: Floating Lantern Market
summary: A black market built on boats that drifts through the marsh and moors somewhere different every night. You find it with a lantern token, or it finds you.

lore: High Meadows is a few thousand herders, a monastery-turned-palace and a chieftain who calls himself king when the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's envoys are not listening. Its people trade yak butter, frost-lotus and glacier ice to the Zhu clan's Cold Forge. Children grow up in felt tents, herd on the ice edge and dream of the Sword Stair. This year the glacier dropped a river onto the lower meadows overnight, and the herders found Ascent Age stonework under the retreating ice.
name: Kingdom of High Meadows
summary: A high-valley kingdom of yak herders under the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's glaciers. Its meadows are greener every year because the ice above them is melting.

lore: The Tide-Watching Pavilion teaches the Water and Wind Daos through observation: disciples spend years on the sea wall counting waves before they learn a technique. The pavilion predicts storms, sea-clan migrations and the tide's surges, and sells its tables to captains, farmers and other sects. It has served the eastern kings for centuries and despises the Armillary Pavilion for charging more for less.
name: Tide-Watching Pavilion
summary: A sect of sea diviners who read tides, winds and the pull of the Mirror. Every captain on the east coast buys their charts.
truth: The tide tables have stopped matching the sea. As the Mirror swells, its pull lifts the outer ocean a little higher every year, and the pavilion's tables were built for a world that is gone.

lore: The Granary ships two barges of grain north for every one it keeps, and for three years it has not had two to spare. Vassal kings hide granaries from the [[Great Jing Dynasty]]'s auditors, spirit-farming sects blame the [[Apricot Grove Valley]]'s blight, and ash locusts that eat qi out of the stalks have appeared where the soil went thin. Buyers from the [[Night Banquet Sect]] markets move north along the river buying indentures from starving families. A cultivator who can grow anything, guard anything or find out where the grain is going will never lack work here.
name: The Granary
summary: The southern river plains that feed the empire, along the middle the Flood River. The harvests are failing, the quotas are not, and the roads south are full of families walking toward the marsh.
truth: The thinning spreads south from the Jing Capital along the old vein courses. The Granary's soil is fine; the qi under it is being pulled north.

lore: The villagers of Huaixia have prayed to the tree for centuries; ten years ago it answered. Its roots reach deep enough to feel the capital's veins, and it trades leaves that clear the mind, seeds and old memories of the land for help. Lately it asks every cultivator the same question: where is the water going? Woodcutters with court permits have twice come to fell it for palace timber and twice been strangled by its roots.
name: Spirit of the Old Scholar Tree
summary: A scholar tree three thousand years old that woke with the tide and is now dying of thirst beside a dry village well. It bargains with cultivators for answers.
truth: The tree can feel the drain flowing toward the palace and could lead anyone to the array's outer nodes. It has not found anyone it trusts.

lore: The Wall-Warden clan, the Shens, were charged three thousand years ago to keep the western wall manned, and they have, through famines and mockery. Every child learns to light the warding lanterns and recite the wall's array script. The empire pays a small stipend and laughs at the Shens. This year the Seal Watch sent an inspector for the first time in a thousand years, checked every lantern and left without a word.
name: Kingdom of the Old Ramparts
summary: A poor, proud kingdom strung along a seawall from the Outer Demon War, ruled by the hereditary wall-wardens who still keep its arrays lit.

lore: The Sea Gate's harbor is chained at night and patrolled by war junks. Its customs house taxes everything and seizes grain, which then reappears in warehouses on the far quay. Thousand Isles traders keep a walled compound by the docks, and the Azure Wave Palace's factor keeps a pavilion over the water. A cultivator with a sword and a clean record can sign onto a convoy for fifty low-grade stones a voyage.
name: The Sea Gate
summary: The empire's southern port and fleet base, a city of masts, customs houses and sailors' quarters at the tip of the Morning Star Continent.

lore: The weavers spin silk from the threads of deep-sea mussels and weave it underwater at night. Their robes are sought by every sect in the Morning Star Continent. Most members have a shark-folk grandmother and hide it; the gills close if they never swim. The guild trades quietly with [[Shared Roost City]] and smuggles half-blood children out of human villages that discover them.
name: Sea-Silk Workshop
summary: A weavers' guild of hidden half-bloods with shark-folk blood. Their sea silk turns blades and never gets wet.
truth: The guild pays the Azure Wave Palace with information about the coast, not silk.

lore: King Qian came from a shipping house and still runs the kingdom like one: offices instead of courts, contracts instead of oaths. Children of Calm Seas go to sea at twelve as deck boys or to the counting houses as clerks. The kingdom pays cultivators well to guard ships and better to recover stolen cargo. It is now quietly running grain to the Thousand Isles at triple price, and the crew members who object have stopped coming home.
name: Kingdom of Calm Seas
summary: A merchant kingdom whose king owns three hundred ships. It is loyal to the throne because the throne's navy keeps the pirates off its cargo.

lore: Cold Ford is iron, fish and ferries. Scavenger crews winter here and sell salvage in spring; iron-sand barges load for the forges; Floating Peak exiles cross on the ferries. The Soul-Calling Sect keeps a hall where the bereaved can speak to the drowned. It is the cheapest port on the inner coast to hire a crew, because the crews are the worst.
name: The Cold Ford
summary: A ferry port at the Snow River's mouth where ships leave for the Shattered Sea's northern islands and the long run up the Floating Peak Continent's coast. The harbor freezes every winter.

lore: The Zhu clan has forged for the Clear Heaven Sword Sect for six thousand years and trains its children in Metal and Fire Daos from the cradle. It takes outside apprentices with good fire roots and binds them for thirty years. The clan's Cold Forge quenches blades in glacier meltwater mixed with sword intent, and nobody has copied the method. The Zhus despise artifact refiners who use fire alone, and say so.
name: Zhu Clan of the Cold Forge
summary: The hereditary swordsmiths of the Clear Heaven Sword Sect, who forge spirit steel in forges cooled by glacier ice. A Zhu sword is worth more than a mortal town.
truth: The glacier the Cold Forge depends on is melting as the tide rises. The clan has twenty years of ice left and has told nobody.

lore: Every child in the Kingdom of the Held Pearl dives from the age of six, and the strongest swimmers go to the queen's shoals. Spirit pearls are sorted by grade at the palace and sold to alchemists and refiners. A tenth goes to the sea clans by treaty. Rooted divers learn Water Dao from the queen herself, which is why the Registry finds so few roots here. Pearl thieves are tied to a reef at low tide.
name: Kingdom of the Held Pearl
summary: A pearl-diving kingdom ruled by the Pearl Queen, a Foundation diver who can stay under for an hour. Its divers are the best on the coast and the shortest-lived.

lore: Blackwater is where pirate ships unload slaves, plunder and stolen sect treasures, and where marsh buyers pay in clean stones. It is officially a fishing village. Its harbor master is a Night Banquet outer disciple, its tavern keepers are appraisers, and its fences will buy anything, including people. Imperial raids arrive a day after the warning does.
name: Blackwater Port
summary: A port at the edge of the marsh where Thousand Isles pirates sell their loot. No questions, no Registry and no records.

features.name: the gate cave in the karst
a ruined village of the one people
herb meadows under a green sky

lore: Inside is a green world where beasts and humans once lived as one people, with ruined villages, bloodline altars and herbs that awaken dormant bloodlines. Half-bloods go in to learn what they are; tamers go in to strengthen their bonds; pure humans who try the gate are thrown back with broken bones. The Night Bridge Society guards the cave and charges entry. It last opened five years ago.
name: Realm of Mingled Blood
summary: A shard world whose gate opens in a karst cave every seven years. It admits only those below Foundation who carry beast blood, or a tamer bonded to a beast.

ties.why: The Night Bridge Society guards the gate cave and takes a toll from all who enter.

lore: The Flood River's floods lay down the silt that makes the southern plains rich, and its barges carry their grain north to the canal. Below the City of Pecks and Bushels it slows into the marsh, where channels split and rejoin and river pirates know every one. Flood-dragon carp, river otter clans and black-shell turtles live in its lower reaches. This year's flood came late and thin.
name: The Flood River
