summary: The river of the south, from the Turtle-Spine Mountains through the granary plains into the Ink Marsh and out to sea at Nine Bends. It floods every summer and feeds half the empire.

lore: Everything in the Imperial Domain points at the [[Jing Capital]]: the canals, the roads, the grain barges and the children. The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] tests every six-year-old at the county registry, and good roots go to the capital in sealed carts. The Ancestor Emperor has not been seen in three centuries, so the princes court cultivators openly and pay well for anyone who can win a duel or lose a witness. For three years the paddies nearest the capital have come up thin, and the court blames blight carried in from the [[Apricot Grove Valley]].
name: The Imperial Domain
summary: The Great Jing Dynasty's home domain around the Jing Capital: canal-laced plains, registry towns and princes' estates, where every child is tested for a spirit root at six.
top: Body Integration (the Ancestor Emperor, unseen and rumored dying)
truth: The dead fields form rings around the Jing Capital that match the palace array's draw. Court astrologers who noticed were posted to the frontier; two never arrived.

lore: Dug by a million laborers and a thousand cultivators over sixty years, the canal is the empire's artery. Barges move in convoys of a hundred under canal guard escort, and lock-keepers are imperial officials who sell priority. With the harvests failing, the barges run light and the bandits have grown bold enough to rob convoys at the locks. Convoy guards are hired at the City of Pecks and Bushels for a low-grade stone a day.
name: The Imperial Canal
summary: The Grand Canal that carries the south's grain from the Flood River to the Imperial River and on to the Jing Capital. Forty locks, a canal guard, and bandits at every one.

lore: Yellow Cliffs grows millet on terraces and sends its sons to the imperial cavalry, because the cavalry pays in silver. Its king is a retired cavalry general who rules like a quartermaster. Children grow up in cave homes, ride before they walk and wrap their faces against the dust. Rooted children are prized by the Registry, which sends them to the horse-archer academies.
name: Kingdom of Yellow Cliffs
summary: A loess kingdom of cave villages along the Snow River gorge. Poor, tough and famous for producing the empire's best cavalry.

lore: The realm is a hall of endless tables laid with spirit foods: every dish raises cultivation, and every dish takes something back, a year of life, a memory, a name. Only those below Core Formation can pass the gate, which stays open nine nights. The Night Banquet invites promising young cultivators of other sects, all expenses paid. Some come back stronger. Some come back strange.
name: Realm of the Phantom Feast
summary: A shard world that opens on the new moon of the seventh month in a sunken pavilion in the marsh. Inside, a banquet is always being served.
truth: The sect's founder found this realm, ate at its table for nine nights and came out with the Banquet's devouring method.

lore: The Apricot Grove Valley's pill halls take up a whole street, with prices posted daily and a Heavenly Scale Pavilion banker at each counter. The rest of the city is clinics, herb markets, inns for patients and the families of patients, and appraisers who test pills for fakes. Beast emissaries in human form walk its streets under the valley's protection, and attacking one is the one crime the Apricot Grove Valley punishes itself.
name: City of Returning Spring
summary: The pill market at the mouth of Apricot Grove Valley, where the Apricot Grove Valley sells its pills and the sick of all Morning Star come to wait.

lore: Earth-fire bubbles up through a hundred vents, and fire spirits born from it attack anything with qi. Fire essence condensed on the vent lips is the key ingredient for Fire Dao breakthroughs and sells for mid-grade stones. Mortals need masks; Qi Condensation cultivators need luck. The valley floor is littered with refiners' tools and bones.
name: Fire Prison Valley
summary: A valley of vents and lava pools where fire spirits drift like smoke and the air kills a mortal in ten breaths. The Blazing Furnace Sect harvests fire essence here.

lore: The Gate of Fine Grain teaches the Wood and Earth Daos through farming: disciples learn to read soil, call rain and graft spirit herbs before they learn a single attack. It recruits farm children with good roots and sells its seed strains everywhere. Now its elders blame the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] for a blight they cannot cure, and its young disciples are being hired out as field hands to anyone who pays the sect, including people who should not have them.
name: Gate of Fine Grain
summary: A spirit-farming sect that bred half the spirit rice strains grown in the Morning Star Continent. Its fields have failed, and it is selling its disciples' contracts to stay solvent.
truth: Half of the Gate of Fine Grain's failure really is the Apricot Grove Valley blight, planted ten years ago. The other half is the drain. The elders cannot tell the two apart, and that is the problem.

lore: The Sword Domain belongs to the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]], and the sect does not pretend otherwise: its peaks are the region's government, its duel rankings its law and its vassal kingdoms its farms. Applicants from all over Morning Star climb the Sword Stair each spring. Four elders sent to the [[Seal Watch]] were due home last year and have not come, and the sect has stopped saying when they will. Spies from the [[Night Banquet Sect]] are caught on the lower peaks every season, more of them each year.
name: The Sword Domain
summary: The Clear Heaven Sword Sect's seventy-two peaks at the Morning Star Continent's northern tip, facing the Floating Peak Continent across the strait. Every road here ends at a sword.
top: Void Refinement (the founder in seclusion; Qingxiao's masters at Deity Transformation)
truth: The main peak's sword hum, which every disciple hears in meditation, faded two hundred years ago. The elders replaced it with an array that imitates it.

lore: Ten thousand swords stand in the snow, each over a grave. Walking among them is a test of Sword Dao: those who endure the intent come out with insight, those who don't come out in pieces. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect lets its disciples in on oath and outsiders never. Thieves still try for the swords of fallen elders, which can be worth a sect's ransom.
name: Valley of the Sword Graves
summary: The valley where the Clear Heaven Sword Sect buries the swords of its dead. Their intent lingers and cuts anyone who walks in without the strength to bear it.
truth: Some graves are empty. The Clear Heaven Sword Sect buries the swords of disciples it executed in secret beside the honored dead.

lore: Fishermen steer wide of the caves, and coast law forbids even pointing at them. Jiao eggshells and shed scales wash up nearby and sell for fortunes to refiners, who pay beachcombers not to ask where they came from. The young jiao are said to be worth a Core Formation breakthrough each. The sea clans have punished one village for a single stolen scale.
name: The Jiao Nest
summary: Sea caves where a jiao of the sea clans' court raises its young. Any human who enters dies, and their village pays for it.

lore: Boundary Head Town is where Beneath the Peaks trades: cinnabar and talismans going down, rice and iron coming up. A Registry checkpoint searches every cart heading uphill, a Clear Heaven Sword Sect recruiting hall sits across the square, and the Mountain Road Gang owns the noodle shop between them. Duels in the square are legal if both parties are cultivators and the magistrate is paid. Talisman seconds from the [[Vermilion Talisman Sect]] sell here for a few low-grade stones.
name: Boundary Head Town
summary: The market town where the imperial road ends and the mountain paths begin. Registry officers, sect recruiters and smugglers all drink in the same three teahouses.

lore: The Command patrols the southern sea lanes, escorts convoys to the Thousand Isles and ferries troops to the Jade Strait. Its marines are Registry conscripts who drew sea duty, and its spear-and-water drills are brutal. It pays bounties for pirates, buys pearls cheap from captured smugglers and hires outside cultivators as convoy guards. Admiral Hou, a Nascent Soul, answers to the throne on paper and to Prince Rui in letters.
name: Sea-Pacifying Command
summary: The Great Jing's southern fleet: war junks with array-armored hulls, conscripted cultivator marines and an admiral with ambitions.

lore: The Capital Prefecture has no king; a Grain Intendant rules it for the throne and answers for every missing bushel and every untested child. Children here grow up on millet porridge, march drills and stories of village boys who tested well and came home in silver armor. Families with a rooted child are paid a bounty of ten low-grade spirit stones; families caught hiding one lose their land. The black trade in clean test results runs through the bathhouses of the Grain-Barge Mouth.
name: Capital Prefecture
summary: The crown's own prefecture around the Jing Capital: three million farmers, a registry office in every market town and the palace lights on the horizon every night.

lore: The Guard trains the empire's finest rooted conscripts in the imperial spear method and the Metal and Slaughter Daos, then posts them to the palace, the princes and the frontier. A Guard captain outranks a provincial governor. Its commander, a Nascent Soul, swears loyalty only to the Ancestor Emperor, whom she has never seen. Its junior officers drink in factions and duel at night, and the princes pay their debts.
name: Golden Spear Guard
summary: The imperial clan's own spear guard, picked from the Registry's best roots. Every prince wants it, and it has started to split along their lines.
truth: The commander has received orders under the Ancestor Emperor's seal for forty years. Lately the brushwork has changed.

lore: The nine strike-points are scorched into glass. Sitting between them during a storm is the fastest way to grasp Lightning Dao and the fastest way to die. The Thunder-Drawing Sect owns the headland and charges entry. Glass from the strike-points is an artifact refining material for lightning weapons.
name: Terrace of Nine Thunders
summary: A bare headland where lightning strikes nine times in every storm, always in the same nine places. Cultivators come to watch it and comprehend the Lightning Dao.
truth: The nine points form a fragment of an Ascent Age tribulation array. Someone could finish it.

lore: Nine Bends is nominally an imperial prefecture. In practice, the river pirates who know the channels decide which barges reach the sea, and Governor Pei decides which pirates he arrests. Children here learn the channels by heart and learn early which boats not to look at. Grain barges from upriver come in light this year, and smuggled cargo going out goes heavier.
name: Kingdom of Nine Bends
summary: The delta kingdom at the Flood River's mouth: a maze of channels, river pirates and an imperial governor who has not seen his salary in years and does not need it.

lore: The Brotherhood smuggles food, medicine and cultivation manuals into the pits and smuggles people out. Its members are miners, escaped convicts and a few disgraced cultivators who learned Earth Dao underground. It wants the Convict Prefecture emptied and the Kangs dead. It pays in ore, recruits anyone the overseers have whipped, and is already planning to use the vein rush as cover.
name: Miners' Brotherhood
summary: A secret society of miners and convicts planning to break the penal pits open. Its oath is sworn on a lump of ore.

lore: Ash locusts came out of the dead soil two years ago: gray insects that strip qi instead of leaves. A swarm can empty a Qi Condensation cultivator's dantian in minutes. Their wings are a talisman ink ingredient and sell well in the City of Pecks and Bushels, so desperate hunters go in with nets and fire. The swarms are spreading toward the [[Kingdom of Wheat Waves]].
name: The Withered Plain
summary: Twenty thousand li of dead fields west of the Flood River, where ash locusts swarm and drain the qi out of anything that stands still.
truth: The locusts are hatching from soil emptied of qi. Wherever the drain runs deepest, they appear first.

lore: The Abbey has logged the Stump's hum and the Mirror's width every night for two thousand years. It teaches divination, star-reading and a slow Time Dao method that ages its masters gracefully. Kings buy horoscopes; sects buy dates for breakthroughs; the Armillary Pavilion buys the logs and pretends not to need them. Its novices are orphans of the coast with good eyes and no families to miss them.
name: Heaven-Peeping Abbey
summary: Astrologer-priests who watch the Stump and the Mirror from a cliff observatory, and sell fortunes to kings and sects.
truth: The logs show the Stump's hum rising with the tide, faster each decade. The abbot sent the figures to the Armillary Pavilion and has been paid every year since to stop publishing them.

lore: The Kingdom of Blue Stone's blue whetstone takes an edge on spirit steel, and every stone is cut for the Clear Heaven Sword Sect. The king, a Foundation outer disciple named Fang Ru, settles disputes by duel and lets any subject challenge a magistrate. Children work the quarries from ten and spar with wooden swords at night. Rooted children go up the mountain at nine with no Registry paperwork, which makes the Kingdom of Blue Stone the empire's least favorite place.
name: Kingdom of Blue Stone
summary: A quarry kingdom under the eastern peaks that cuts the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's whetstones and sword-steps. Its king is a Clear Heaven Sword Sect outer disciple and rules like one.
truth: Fang Ru was sent down from the inner sect for a crime the sect never names. He has been writing to the Night Banquet.

lore: The wolves den where lightning strikes most, and their fur stores enough charge to stop a heart. The wolf king lets logging crews into the groves in exchange for salt and the bodies of poachers. Beast tamers prize thunder-wolf pups above any other beast in the north, and poachers who take them start feuds that last generations. The king speaks in a growl that sounds like words to anyone with good ears.
name: Thunder Wolf Clan
summary: Packs of thunder-wolves in the burned pine groves, led by a Core Formation wolf king who has learned to bargain with the loggers instead of eating them.
truth: Beast Court envoys have offered the king a seat at the Court's lowest table if his packs drive the loggers out of the groves for good. He has not decided.

lore: The Jiao clan buys every thunder-struck pine in the Thunder Cliffs and carves it into puppets animated by lightning arrays. Its best puppets fight at Core Formation and sell to princes and sects across the Morning Star Continent. Outsiders can apprentice for ten years of service. The clan hates the Thousand Puppet Gate, whose corpse puppets it calls 'grave meat on strings', and refuses to sell to anyone who buys from it.
name: Jiao Clan of Thunderwood
summary: A clan of puppeteers who carve fighting puppets from lightning-struck pine. Their puppets move faster than a Foundation cultivator can draw a sword.
truth: The Jiao patriarch has bought one of the Gate's immortal-corpse puppets in secret to study it. It watches him when he works.

lore: Storms off the outer ocean break on the Thunder Cliffs's cliffs all year, and lightning strikes the headlands so often that the pines grow scarred and the rocks are magnetized. It is poor country for farming and rich country for anyone who can use lightning: talisman makers buy thunder-struck wood, puppeteers carve it, and lightning cultivators come to be struck on purpose. The coast pays toll to the [[Azure Wave Palace]] for every boat that fishes past the reefs. The empire's writ is thin here; the Registry tester comes by ship, when the weather allows.
name: Thunder Cliffs
summary: The Morning Star Continent's northeastern corner: storm-pine forests on sea cliffs facing the Shoreless Sea, where thunderstorms come ashore three days in four.
truth: The storms have doubled in ten years. Something far out toward the Rim is drawing them, and the lightning sect's elders have felt it calling.

lore: Rifts come in on the tide, hang above the sand for hours and fade. Things come through them too: driftwood from other continents, ancient coins, once a live sea serpent. Space Dao cultivators meditate on the rifts at a safe distance; scavengers wait to grab whatever falls out. Nobody walks the beach at night.
name: Rift Beach
summary: A beach where spatial rifts from the Shattered Sea wash ashore after storms, drifting like jellyfish. Touch one and you are elsewhere, or in pieces.
truth: One rift in ten opens toward the Scar. What comes through those does not wash back out.

lore: The Registry keeps a jade slip for every rooted child in a hundred kingdoms and sends testers on a six-year circuit with a root-reading mirror. Top roots go to the palace academies, middling ones to the army, poor ones to the arsenals and granaries as qi laborers. Sect recruiters who take a registered child are outlaws in the Great Jing Dynasty. The Registry pays informers, hires bounty cultivators to track runaways, and quietly sells its rejects' slips to the highest bidder.
name: Court of the Spirit Registry
summary: The imperial bureau that tests, registers and conscripts every spirit-rooted child in the Great Jing Dynasty's lands. Its gray-robed testers are the most hated officials on the continent.
truth: Since the harvests failed the Registry has been ordered to send every root above middling straight to the palace, unrecorded. None of those children have been assigned anywhere.

lore: Families from the dead plains arrive daily with nothing. The Temple of Alms-Food runs a kitchen; imperial officers run a census to find rooted children; marsh buyers run indenture contracts. Gangs run the water. A cultivator can hire a hundred laborers here for a sack of rice, or adopt a rooted orphan before the Registry does.
name: Camp of the Displaced
summary: A sprawling refugee camp on the marsh's northern edge, a hundred thousand famine families strong. Night Banquet buyers walk its lanes with full purses.

lore: Reed Flowers fishes, cuts reeds and paddles everywhere. Its king writes poetry and signs whatever the chamberlain puts in front of him. The kingdom is safe: no pirates, no bandits, no imperial auditors, because nobody wants to offend the sect. Every autumn twenty young people go to the banquet halls as servants, and most come back in a year with gifts and silences. Children grow up among herons, leeches and stories about the ones who did not.
name: Kingdom of Reed Flowers
summary: A stilt-village kingdom in the reeds, ruled by a gentle mortal king and his Night Banquet chamberlain. Each autumn it sends twenty youths to serve at the banquets.
truth: The ones who come back are not all the ones who left. A few are Banquet disciples wearing their faces, and they go on to serve in noble houses across the Morning Star Continent.

lore: The Kingdom of Wheat Waves was the poorest vassal before the harvests failed, and now it is lawless. The Barefoot Banner has opened the royal granaries and hangs tax collectors, and its leader is a Qi Condensation hedge cultivator who claims Heaven has withdrawn its mandate from the Jing. The empire has sent a punitive column. Both sides are hiring, and so are the slavers following the column.
name: Kingdom of Wheat Waves
summary: A dry wheat kingdom on the plain's eastern edge, in open famine. Its king fled to the Jing Capital, and a peasant army calling itself the Barefoot Banner holds the granaries.
truth: The Banner's leader hums a tune nobody taught him, and his followers have started humming it too.

lore: Inside is an endless autumn of wild spirit grain guarded by straw-golem scarecrows and harvest mice the size of dogs. Seeds brought out sprout in any soil, and with the harvests failing, the court has promised a minor title for every hundred catties of seed. The princes each field their own teams of young cultivators, and the teams fight inside. The gate next opens in two years.
name: Realm of Grain in Ear
summary: A farming shard world whose gate opens in a wheat field east of the Jing Capital for forty days every twelve years. Only cultivators below Foundation can pass.
truth: Straw golems that are smashed reform in the shape of whoever smashed them.

lore: The Imperial Stables run the pastures as a prefecture, and every herder family is bound to the herds by law. Wind-maned horses can run a thousand li a day and sell for a mid-grade stone each, so thieves come from everywhere, including the princes' own households. Children herd foals and learn horse medicine before letters. A herder who raises a champion is freed with his family.
name: Imperial Horse Pastures
summary: The empire's stud farms on the high plateau, where wind-maned spirit horses are bred for princes and cavalry. Horse thieves hang from every gate.
truth: Prince Rui's agents have been buying the best foals through false sales. The Stables' master knows and has been paid to know.

features.name: stone pillars that shift in the illusion

lore: The Golden Python's grandson, a Nascent Soul serpent, crossed the strait six years ago and took the stone forest as its hunting ground. Its illusions make travelers walk in circles until they starve. Its shed skins are worth a fortune, and its den is said to hold the treasures of everyone it has eaten. Three imperial expeditions have gone in.
name: Soul-Lost Stone Forest
summary: A maze of stone pillars where a great python from the Vast Wilds Continent has made its den. Its illusions turn the forest into a trap no map survives.

ties.why: The serpent of the stone forest is the Golden Python's grandson, and his den answers to the lair.

lore: The Stockade breeds Gu in jars sunk in marsh mud, crossing Vast Wilds strains with marsh leeches and corpse worms. Its masters teach Gu raising to anyone who survives a year of feeding the jars, and their curses kill from twenty li, given a hair or a name. They buy eggs from frontier smugglers at any price and are terrified of the Jar-Mothers ever finding out where their strains came from.
name: Netherworm Stockade
summary: Demonic Gu raisers on a mud island in the marsh, who buy Gu eggs smuggled from the Vast Wilds Continent and sell curses to the Night Banquet's guests.
truth: Three of their strains were stolen from a Jar-Mother village. The thief is the Stockade's master, and the Jar-Mothers already know.

lore: The oysters feed on qi from a vein under the seabed, and a hundred-year pearl can be ground into Foundation pills. The Kingdom of the Held Pearl holds the shoals by treaty with the sea clans and must leave a third of the beds untouched. Poachers come at night in black boats. The giant spirit clams in the deepest beds have taken more divers than the pirates.
name: Bright Pearl Shoals
summary: Spirit-oyster beds in shallow, warm water where the best pearls on the coast grow. Divers, pirates and sea-clan wardens all claim them.

lore: The Ink Marsh is the [[Night Banquet Sect]]'s country. Its stilt kingdoms are ruled by puppets, its channels by smugglers and its nights by the sect's banquets, held each new moon in a hall nobody finds twice. Black markets float through the reeds selling stolen manuals, Gu, slaves and secrets from every court. The famine has filled the marsh's edges with refugees, and the sect's buyers pick through them. The marsh is spreading north a few li each year, and the land it takes does not come back.
name: The Ink Marsh
summary: The black-water marshes of the Flood River delta, seat of the Night Banquet Sect. Every forbidden thing in the Morning Star Continent is for sale here, usually after dark.
truth: The marsh grows wherever the Banquet Master's aura settles. That cultivation has outgrown Nascent Soul, and the land is the first thing that cannot hide it.

features.name: ranch corrals of thunder-horned deer and scale-horses

lore: The Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches raise thunder-horned deer, scale-horses and war hounds from eggs and cubs bought from smugglers. The empire buys every mount at a good price, and the herder families are rich, armed and hunted. Beast Court agents, half-bloods in its pay and now and then an old beast, cross the strait to kill tamers and free their beasts. Children are bonded to a hatchling at seven and grow up with it.
name: Kingdom of Spirit Herders
summary: A kingdom of beast tamers who raise war mounts for the empire from eggs smuggled out of the Vast Wilds Continent. The Beast Court has put a price on every one of them.

ties.why: The Gate spits on us as collaborators and seizes any bonded beast that strays near its hall.
Our hatchlings come over the strait in Night Bridge crates, and we pay whatever they ask.
The Court has priced every tamer's head and sends agents over the strait to collect.
The frontier command buys every war mount we raise, at a good price.

truth: The kingdom's best stallion bloodline comes from a beast that wandered over the strait on its own and asked to stay. It speaks, though it has never shown a realm that should allow it, and has asked them to keep that quiet.

lore: Each step is a farm worked by one family for generations, watered by a vein that runs down the mountain. The top hundred steps belong to the Clear Heaven Sword Sect and grow Cloud-Silk rice that sells for ten low-grade stones a catty. The bottom steps grow mortal rice for the empire's tax. Spirit farmers come to study the terraces' irrigation arrays, which nobody has been able to copy.
name: Cloud-Climbing Terraces
summary: Spirit-rice terraces climbing a whole mountainside to the gates of the sect peaks. The upper steps glow green; the lower steps, on imperial land, are turning gray.
truth: The vein feeding the lower steps has started running backward, downhill toward the Jing Capital.

lore: The Society teaches water-breathing arts, appraisal and formation breaking, and outfits crews for months-long dives among the shattered islands. It buys anything brought up, sells to the Heavenly Scale Pavilion and the marsh, and runs the coast's best appraisal hall. New divers sign a ten-year contract and get a tenth of what they find. The Seal Watch has forbidden them to sail inside the marker buoys, and the Society has lost two crews who tried.
name: Abyss-Diving Society
summary: A scavenger sect based on the inner coast that dives the drowned valleys of the Shattered Sea for Ascent Age ruins. Half its members die rich, the other half just die.
truth: The last crew back brought up a jade token that hums in time with the Stump. The Society's master has hidden it and is selling dive rights to the spot.

lore: The Kingdom by the Bridge's king is a mortal of an old house who keeps power by never choosing a side. Imperial spearmen guard the south end of the Ninefold Bridge and the Clear Heaven Sword Sect outer disciples guard the north end, and neither may cross armed. Children grow up fishing off the bridge piers and watching cultivators duel in the river mist. A rooted child born here is a diplomatic incident, and families sometimes sell the news to both sides.
name: Kingdom by the Bridge
summary: A river kingdom built around a great stone bridge over the Snow River. It pays tax to the throne, tithe to the Clear Heaven Sword Sect and bribes to everyone else.
truth: The king's eldest daughter tested as a heaven-grade root. He hid it, and now both sides know.

lore: Three Passes lives on tolls. Its ruling family, the Lis, are Core Formation cultivators who have served the throne loyally for six hundred years because loyalty pays. Every caravan, conscript column and tax cart crosses their gates. The Dawn League needs the passes to rebel; the empire needs them to stop it; the Lis have taken gifts from both and promised nothing.
name: Kingdom of Three Passes
summary: The kingdom that holds the three passes over the Turtle-Spine Mountains, and with them the only roads between the east and the empire.
truth: The Li patriarch's grandson was conscripted by the Registry eight years ago and has not been heard from. The patriarch blames the throne.

lore: The Gang charges a family a year's harvest to take a child uphill, and it knows every goat trail and every bribable patrol. Its leaders are failed the Clear Heaven Sword Sect applicants with Foundation cultivation and no love for either master. It also runs forged Registry slips, contraband talismans and runaway soldiers. General Yan Ku has hanged forty of its guides this year.
name: Mountain Road Gang
summary: Smugglers who guide rooted children past imperial checkpoints to the Sword Stair for a fee. Most arrive; some are sold elsewhere.
truth: One in ten children never reaches the Stair. They go south down the river to the marsh buyers, and the Gang tells the families they failed the climb.

lore: The City of Pecks and Bushels sends its grain east to the [[Flood River]], where the barges gather for the trip north. Its grain exchange is the busiest market in the south, and its streets are full of refugees, speculators, imperial auditors and buyers for the marsh. Rooms are cheap, information is not, and a hired guard for a grain barge earns thirty low-grade stones a trip if the barge arrives.
name: City of Pecks and Bushels
summary: The river city where the south's grain is weighed, taxed and gambled on. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion sets the price at dawn, and by noon people are fighting over it.

lore: King Dou, a retired pirate hunter, rules from a fort on a headland and pays a bounty for pirate heads in salt. Watchtowers line the coast with signal fires, and the militia drills monthly. Children learn to shoot before they can write and to hide in cellars when the bells ring. The kingdom hires cultivators every autumn and is always short of them.
name: Kingdom of Stone Forts
summary: A coastal kingdom where every village is a walled fort and every adult keeps a crossbow, because the pirates come every autumn.
truth: King Dou sells captured pirates to the Convict Prefecture as miners instead of hanging them. Three of his recent captures were pirate lords' sons, sent to recruit in the pits.

lore: Corpse qi pools in the black water and draws blood-leeches by the million. A swarm can bleed a horse in a minute. Their engorged bodies sell to demonic alchemists, and leech-catchers wade in on stilts. Some of the dead in the fen still walk at night in Ghost Month.
name: The Man-Eating Fen
summary: A fen of sinkholes and blood-leech swarms where the marsh swallows bodies whole. The Night Banquet leaves its leftovers here.

lore: The temple feeds anyone who asks, and asks only that they listen to a sermon and leave their name in the merit ledger. Its monks cultivate karma and the vajra body, heal for free and refuse to fight unless a mortal is attacked in front of them. Rooted children fed at its kitchens often take vows, which puts them beyond the Registry's reach. The abbot, a Nascent Soul monk from the [[Thousand Lamps Temple]], has been offered land by three princes.
name: Temple of Alms-Food
summary: A Buddhist temple founded by monks from the Myriad Sands Continent, now running famine kitchens across the south. Converts arrive by the thousand, and the court is starting to worry.
truth: The abbot has read the drain in the earth and knows who causes it. He keeps silent because the court has promised the temple a hundred thousand acres when the famine ends.

features.name: a sinkhole rim with terraces down the walls

lore: Stone Eyes is named for the round sinkholes that dot its hills, each with a village around the rim and terraces down the walls. Its people farm in the sinkholes, keep bats for guano and guide smugglers through caves no map shows. The empire counts it as part of the march; the cave clans pay no tax and give no soldiers. Children grow up knowing which neighbors have scales under their sleeves and never saying so.
name: Kingdom of Stone Eyes
summary: Sinkhole villages in the karst, ruled by a council of cave clans. Half-blood families hide here, and nobody asks what is in the lower caves.

ties.why: We guide the Society's runners through the lower caves for a share, and never ask what is in the crates.
The march calls us its own and wants our taxes and our sons; it gets neither.

features.name: the bounty office, paying for cores by grade
the reef road below the walls at low tide

lore: The City of the Guarded Mouth holds the narrow coast where the chain begins, with a garrison of ten thousand and a bounty office that pays for cores by grade. Its markets sell beast parts, smuggled Vast Wilds herbs and frontier saber steel. Every sect with a frontier interest keeps a hall here. At low tide, the reef road appears below the walls.
name: City of the Guarded Mouth
summary: The fortress city at the head of the island chain, the empire's frontier headquarters. Its walls are faced with the skulls of beasts that tried them.

ties.why: The Gate leads our raids across the chain and fills our bounty office with cores.
Our cavalry rides Spirit Herder mounts, and we buy every one they raise.

lore: The princes were buried with their spears, and the spears woke. Grave robbers still try for the jade armor and spear manuals inside, because one manual can make a family. The frost on the hill never melts, even in summer. The imperial clan is buried here, so trespass is treason, and the guards at the gate are bribable only on Ghost Month nights.
name: The Frost Mausoleums
summary: The sealed tombs of the dynasty's early princes on a frost-rimed hill north of the Jing Capital. Spear-spirits patrol the avenues and kill anyone without a clan token.
truth: The mausoleum's guardian array runs off the same veins as the palace. Since the drain began, the spear-spirits have been starving, and they have started to wander off the hill.

lore: Dawnlight's queen is a Foundation cultivator of the Yu family, which ruled the whole east before the conquest. Each morning at sunrise the court bows to the sea, an old rite the Jing banned and the Yus never stopped. Children here learn that the Jing are a passing weather and that the first light of the world touches their beaches. The queen leads the Dawn League and is quietly buying spears.
name: Kingdom of Dawnlight
summary: A far eastern kingdom of the Morning Star Continent, whose royal house is older than the Jing and keeps the crown it was forbidden to wear.

lore: Dust storms come off the plateau every spring and bury whole villages, and its people live in cave homes cut into the yellow cliffs. The empire breeds its spirit horses here, the [[Snow River]] carries meltwater and sword-steel silt to a cold delta, and the Morning Star Continent's largest battlefield from the [[Hundred Sects War]] lies unburied on the high plain, where it has been haunted for twelve thousand years. Ghost cultivators keep the dead in place for a fee the empire pays reluctantly. Millet still grows, but the plateau's springs are sinking.
name: The North Wind
summary: A windswept loess plateau in the Morning Star Continent's northwest, cut by the Snow River's gorge. Cave villages, imperial horse pastures and the oldest battlefield on the continent.
truth: The ghosts on the battlefield have started marching in formation toward the coast every Ghost Month, as if called to a wall.

lore: The League began as a drinking society of eastern princes and is now a conspiracy with treasury, couriers and a Nascent Soul elder on its council. It hides rooted children from the Registry, runs salt to fund itself and recruits cultivators with grudges against the empire. Members know each other by a rising-sun token cut in half. Its plan needs the passes, a navy and a reason; the famine levy may provide the reason.
name: The Dawn League
summary: A secret alliance of eastern kings and cultivator houses sworn to break the east away from the Great Jing Dynasty.

lore: The Kingdom of Pine Shade's king is a logging boss's grandson with a crown from the Jing court and a debt to the Jiao puppet clan. Lightning-struck pine sells by the inch, so logging crews go out in storms on purpose, and the kingdom buries a few every season. Children grow up in the smell of pitch and learn to climb before they walk. Thunder-wolves den in the burned groves, and their pelts hold a static charge for years.
name: Kingdom of Pine Shade
summary: A forest kingdom of loggers and charcoal burners under the Snow Blade Ridge, whose thunder-struck pines are worth more than gold to puppeteers.

lore: King Hao of the Kingdom of the Grain Plain is a decent mortal with a bad hand: his yields have fallen a third, his quota has not moved, and the auditors arrive in autumn. He has started hiring cultivators to guard secret granaries and to scare off the Night Banquet's indenture buyers, and he pays in land titles rather than stones. Children here grow up in the paddies, learn to swim before they walk, and know the Registry tester by the color of his robe.
name: Kingdom of the Grain Plain
summary: The largest vassal of the south: endless paddies, a mortal king who owes the throne a quota he cannot meet, and a Registry office he pays to look the other way.
truth: King Hao's court geomancer has found that the soil's qi runs north like water down a drain, and is too frightened to tell him why.

lore: The Kingdom of Pool Creek grows spirit lotus in three hundred ponds, and the seed pods sell to alchemists for a low-grade stone apiece. The Bai family are Foundation cultivators of the Water Dao who treat the villages as tenants and pick their servants from rooted children before the Registry arrives. The ponds are still healthy, which makes the Kingdom of Pool Creek the envy of the plain and a target. A family of ash-scaled pond eels has started taking villagers at dusk.
name: Kingdom of Pool Creek
summary: A small lake kingdom of lotus farmers and fishing villages, ruled by the Bai cultivator family from an island manor in its biggest pool.
truth: The Bais bribe the Registry with one rooted child in three to keep the other two. They do not choose randomly.

lore: The Kingdom of Surf Rocks's lords are three mortal families and one Foundation cultivator, Old Ma, who sits on the reef rock and takes a cut of every wreck. Children learn to dive for wreck salvage at eight and to read storms before they can count. The kingdom pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s shark-folk collectors a tenth of its catch, and anyone who takes a sea-clan child in a net is drowned by their neighbors before the sea clans can come for the village.
name: Kingdom of Surf Rocks
summary: A kingdom of fishing coves and wreckers' villages on the storm coast, ruled by sea lords who light false beacons on bad nights.
truth: Old Ma has been luring the Azure Wave Palace's own toll ships onto the reefs, and blaming the storms.

lore: A Dao stele on the cliff edge, carved by an unknown hand, describes falling water without end. Cultivators of Water and Space come to meditate on it. The cliff is also where eastern kings swear oaths, because nothing said facing the Rim can be taken back, or so they say.
name: Rim-Gazing Cliff
summary: A sheer sea cliff where, on the clearest winter mornings, a white line shows on the eastern horizon. Scholars call it a mirage; sailors call it the edge of the world.
truth: The stele's carver was an Ascent Age master who walked out along the falling water, as the old texts claim, and came back. The worn last line tells how.

lore: The Coin Treasure Trading House issues letters of credit the Heavenly Scale Pavilion will honor, which makes it the second most important bank in the south. It runs ships to the Thousand Isles and caravans to the frontier, hires appraisers and guards by the hundred and has a standing arrangement with half the pirate lords. Its young masters are cultivators of middling talent and expensive habits.
name: Coin Treasure Trading House
summary: The largest merchant house in the southern Morning Star Continent, with branches in Ten Thousand Sails and Shared Roost City. It banks, ships, insures and smuggles, in roughly that order.
truth: The Coin Treasure Trading House insures grain ships, then sells their routes to pirates. It profits twice and has done so for forty years.

lore: The Kangs are a Foundation clan of Earth and Metal cultivators who hold the kingdom from the throne by contract: so much copper and spirit iron a year, no questions asked. Miners are paid in scrip only Kang shops accept. Children work the sorting tables from seven, and rooted ones are sold to the Blazing Furnace Sect before the Registry hears of them. A cave-in last month buried three hundred miners, and the Kangs have not dug.
name: Kingdom of Copper Ridge
summary: A mining kingdom ruled by the Kang family of mine-masters, who own every shaft, every forge and most of the people.
truth: The cave-in was deliberate. The buried shaft broke into an Ascent Age gallery, and the Kangs wanted no witnesses.

features.name: the drill yard, where rank is counted in cores

lore: The Beast-Butcher Gate teaches Saber and Slaughter Daos and recruits frontier orphans who have already lost someone to beasts. Disciples earn rank by cores taken. The sect sells cores to the Apricot Grove Valley, hides to the Zhu clan's rivals and meat to anyone, and leads the empire's punitive raids across the island chain. It despises beast tamers as collaborators and half-bloods as vermin.
name: Beast-Butcher Gate
summary: A frontier sect of saber cultivators who raid across the strait for beast cores. Brutal, rich and the beasts' favorite target.

ties.why: We raid across the strait for their cores, and their young come back over it for our disciples.
The herders raise beasts for coin and call it taming; we take their mounts at our gates and their riders for collaborators.
Apricot Grove buys every beast core we bring home, at a price we never argue.
We keep a hall in the city and lead its punitive raids down the chain; the bounty office pays us first.

truth: The sect's Nascent Soul master killed a young Beast Court prince fifty years ago. The prince's mother has finally woken from seclusion.

lore: Everyone on this coast has seen the [[Ladder Stump]] and has an opinion about it. Fishermen read weather from its shadow, astrologers read fate from its hum, and scavenger crews sail west toward it to dive the drowned ruins of the [[Shattered Sea]]. The coast still has seawalls from the Outer Demon War, kept by families who were told to watch the west and never stop. Lately the Stump hums on nights when the Mirror is not overhead, spatial rifts wash up on the beaches after storms, and elders sent to the [[Seal Watch]] are not coming home.
name: Ladder-Gazing Coast
summary: The Morning Star Continent's inner coast at the mouth of the Imperial River, facing the Shattered Sea. On clear nights the Heaven Ladder's stump stands on the horizon, a black line against the Mirror.
truth: Those who sit on the beach long enough start to hear the hum as a song. Some fishing villages have been singing along for a year.

lore: The Kingdom Facing the Peaks lives off the four-month strait crossing: ships, pilots, inns and a customs house that taxes both the Clear Heaven Sword Sect and the Floating Peak clans. Its harbor quarter is full of Floating Peak exiles, children of the [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] born without their bloodline and sent down to serve, who fled across the water instead. They teach formation basics for a meal and resent everyone. The Kingdom Facing the Peaks children learn to swim in cold water, read the strait currents and spot floating peaks by their shadows.
name: Kingdom Facing the Peaks
summary: A strait kingdom of ferry towns and fishing villages on the northern coast, where on some clear mornings a stray floating peak, drifted far out over the strait, stands on the horizon.
truth: One exile is not bloodless: his bloodline was sealed at birth by a rival clan. The Conclave has learned of it and wants him back, quietly.

lore: Evening Glow handles the heartland's trade with the Shattered Sea islands: grain and iron out, salvage and sea herbs in. Its salvage market is the best place in the Morning Star Continent to buy a broken Ascent Age artifact and the worst place to be sure of what it is. Abyss-Diving Society halls line the waterfront, and Floating Peak exiles sell formation services in its alleys. Sunsets here turn the harbor red behind the Stump's silhouette.
name: City of Evening Glow
summary: The great port at the Imperial River's mouth, where river barges meet sea junks and scavenger crews sail west toward the Stump.

lore: Bones and broken weapons cover the plain under a thin skin of dust. Ghosts of whole sects still fight their last battles on it, worst in the seventh month. Appraisers and grave-diggers go in for ancient artifacts, manuals and the jade tokens of dead sects, and ghost cultivators go in to harvest yin. Anyone who dies there joins the war.
name: Plain of Ten Thousand Graves
summary: The high-plain battlefield of the War of a Hundred Sects, never buried. Twelve thousand years of ghosts, broken artifacts and spirit-vein scars.

lore: Every spring the town fills with youths, their families and the people who prey on them. Bookmakers take bets on who will reach which step; healers set bones for those who fall; swordsmiths sell 'Stair-proven' blades. Failed climbers who reached the five-thousandth step are hired as guards across the Morning Star Continent. Sect recruiters from smaller sword schools wait at the bottom with offers for the ones who fail.
name: Sword-Asking Town
summary: The town at the foot of the Sword Stair, where thousands of hopefuls wait each spring to climb. Swordsmiths, healers and bookmakers live off them.

lore: A sentence to the Convict Prefecture is a sentence to dig spirit ore until you die or pay. Overseers are Foundation cultivators with suppression collars for unruly convicts; the warden is a peak Foundation officer who sells early release. Children born in the pits belong to the prefecture. Cultivators who lose a duel to the wrong prince sometimes end up here, which means some of the convicts are dangerous.
name: Convict Prefecture
summary: The empire's penal prefecture: forty mining pits worked by convicts, failed conscripts and debtors under imperial overseers with whips that cut qi.
truth: The warden has been writing off living convicts as dead and selling them south to the marsh buyers.

lore: Prospectors, claim-jumpers, refiners, gamblers and imperial surveyors crowd a valley that smokes day and night. Spirit ore changes hands raw at a third of the city price, claims are sold three times over, and the imperial surveyor's stamp costs more than the claim. The Blazing Furnace Sect, the Kangs and two Night Banquet fronts each hold a hill. Good pay for guards, appraisers and anyone who can tell real ore from painted rock.
name: New Vein Market
summary: A boomtown of tents and claim stakes around the newly surfaced vein, a year old and already ten thousand strong. Law is whoever holds the hill.

lore: Setting Sun is ruled by King Wen, a mortal scholar and amateur astrologer who pays the Heaven-Peeping Abbey to interpret his dreams. Its delta rice still yields well, so imperial grain auditors arrive twice a year and leave with more each time. Children here fish, row and climb the seawall at dusk to watch the Stump take the sun. The Registry office in the capital is one of the most corrupt in the empire and sells exemptions openly.
name: Kingdom of the Setting Sun
summary: The delta kingdom at the mouth of the Imperial River, rich in rice, fish and river trade, where every evening the sun sets behind the Stump.

lore: Members carry a gourd on a staff and go where the famine and the raids are. They teach acupuncture, herb lore and the Life Dao at roadside camps, and their students become village doctors across the Morning Star Continent. The Apricot Grove Valley tolerates them as long as they sell no pills. They know which villages are sick before anyone else does.
name: Society of the Hanging Gourd
summary: Wandering healers, mostly the Apricot Grove Valley dropouts, who treat the poor for free and teach medicine to anyone. The valley calls them charlatans and uses them as cheap labor.
truth: The Society's doctors have mapped the blight's spread across three regions. Their map points back to the valley.

lore: Its water is cold enough to numb a mortal in minutes and, swordsmiths swear, carries sword intent from the peaks. The upper river is the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's, the middle river is the empire's, and the delta belongs to whoever is dredging it this season. Gorge barges haul iron sand and millet, and the river's ice in winter is a highway for sledges.
name: Snow River
summary: The great river of the north, from the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's glaciers past the terraced foothills and through the loess gorges to a cold delta on the inner sea.

lore: Every peak on the ridge has a Clear Heaven Sword Sect hall, a vassal sect or a hermit on it. Snow apes and frost cranes nest on the highest slopes, and their cores are prized for Ice and Wind Dao pills. The few passes are customs posts. The ridge's meltwater is said to carry sword intent, and swordsmiths downstream quench blades in it.
name: Snow Blade Ridge
summary: The snow-covered range across the Morning Star Continent's north on which Clear Heaven Sword Sect's seventy-two peaks stand. Its passes are guarded and its glaciers feed the Snow River.

lore: Misty Waves dredges iron sand from the delta for forges, fishes the cold inner sea and runs ships north toward the Floating Peak Continent's western coasts. The Ruan family are Foundation cultivators of the Water Dao who sell iron to both the Zhu clan and the Blazing Furnace Sect and play them against each other. Children here dredge, row and know the fog by smell. Sword-steel silt sometimes carries flecks of real sword intent, and finding one can make a family.
name: Kingdom of Misty Waves
summary: A cold delta kingdom at the Snow River's mouth, ruled by the Ruan cultivator family. Its silt is full of iron from the north, and its fog never quite lifts.

lore: The Kingdom of Salt Pans's pans produce a third of the Morning Star Continent's salt, and the empire takes half of it in tax. Salt lords, mortal families with cultivator guards, run the pans and the smuggling both. Spirit salt crystallizes in a few pans after storms and sells to alchemists. Children rake salt barefoot and grow up knowing which patrols can be bribed. A salt lord's son who reaches Qi Condensation is married off to a cultivator house before he can blink.
name: Kingdom of Salt Pans
summary: A kingdom of salt pans and salt lords on the flat southeastern shore. Imperial salt tax is the law; salt smuggling is the economy.

lore: The Blazing Furnace Sect teaches the Fire and Metal Daos at the anvil: disciples stoke vent-forges for three years before they may strike. The sect takes apprentices with fire roots from any family, sells weapons to anyone and hires out refiners to repair sect treasures. Its rivalry with the Zhu Clan of the Cold Forge is three thousand years old and mostly settled by forging contests, sometimes by murder. Its claim teams at the new vein shoot first.
name: Blazing Furnace Sect
summary: Artifact refiners who forge inside a live volcanic vent. They make the best fire weapons in the Morning Star Continent, and they mean to own the new vein.

lore: These hills belong to whoever buys their herbs, and the [[Apricot Grove Valley]] buys them all. Tenant kingdoms grow herbs on the Apricot Grove Valley contracts, rival gardens wither under blight nobody can explain, and patients arrive from every corner of the Morning Star Continent, and from beyond it: beast emissaries in human shape come up from the strait for medicine, under the Apricot Grove Valley's protection. The empire blames the famine on the Apricot Grove Valley's blight and the valley denies it, and both are partly right. Herb thieves, alchemists and sick people all come here, and the valley profits from each.
name: The Medicine Ridges
summary: Green hills on the Morning Star Continent's western side around Apricot Grove Valley: herb gardens, apricot forests and kingdoms that owe the Apricot Grove Valley everything, including their debts.
top: Void Refinement (the Valley Master, by rumor older than the trees)
truth: The blight the Apricot Grove Valley seeds in rival gardens has started jumping to its own tenants' fields, and the valley's healers cannot cure what their elders made.

features.name: a tide pool island on the chain

lore: The Society knows the tides, the reefs and which islands have something living on them this month. Most of its runners are Qi Condensation or Foundation half-bloods who know one stretch by heart, and each crew waits on its own tide, so a cargo takes about half a year to pass end to end; only the Core Formation leaders fly the whole chain, in about a month. It runs half-bloods out of human villages, beast eggs to the Kingdom of Spirit Herders's ranches, Gu to the marsh and Vast Wilds herbs to anyone. Its leaders are half-bloods with beast senses and long grudges. It pays tribute to nobody and has informers in every fort. Passage costs five low-grade stones, or a favor.
name: Night Bridge Society
summary: Half-blood smugglers who run the island chain in relays, one crew to a stretch, passing people, Gu eggs, beast cubs and herbs from island to island at low tide between the Morning Star Continent and Shared Roost City.

ties.why: The ranches pay well for every egg and cub we carry over at low tide.
Everything we run along the chain ends at Shared Roost, the only market that takes it all.
The cave clans guide our cargo through caves no map shows, for a share and no questions.
We hold the cave where the gate opens and charge every blood that goes in.

lore: The Thunder-Drawing Sect recruits from storm survivors: anyone struck by lightning and still alive gets an invitation. Its method tempers meridians with lightning, fast and brutal, and its disciples reach Foundation years ahead of most sects. It sells lightning-charged talisman ink, trains tribulation survival for a fee and treats the Clear Heaven Sword Sect as an old rival. Its Nascent Soul master has not left the cliff in ten years.
name: Thunder-Drawing Sect
summary: A lightning sect on the highest sea cliff, whose disciples draw thunderbolts into their bodies to temper them. One in five does not survive the first year.
truth: The master can hear a voice in the storms from the east. He believes it is his Dao calling him to the Rim.

lore: Half of the Morning Star Continent's trade rides the Imperial River, and the Grand Canal joins it at the Grain-Barge Mouth to carry the south's grain to the capital. Imperial toll stations every hundred li tax barges, and the river guard is a posting for princes' sons. Spirit carp in its middle reaches leap the Jing Capital weir each spring, and catching one is a festival. This year the water runs low and warm past the capital, and the carp have not come.
name: The Imperial River
summary: The great river of the heartland, from the Turtle-Spine Mountains west past the walls of the Jing Capital to the delta at Evening Glow on the inner sea.
truth: The river's qi drops sharply as it passes the Jing Capital and recovers a hundred li downstream. Fishermen have noticed; officials have not written it down.

lore: The Imperial Grain Prefecture grows Jade Pearl rice for the palace kitchens, and its farmers are serfs of the Imperial Household. The Lu family, a Foundation clan of spirit farmers, has run it for nine generations and is now being audited for the shortfall. Rumor says the Lus will hang a village headman to satisfy the auditors. Anyone who can make the paddies yield again, or find out why they will not, will have the Household's ear.
name: Imperial Grain Prefecture
summary: The palace's private spirit-rice county, terraced around a low-grade vein. For three years its harvest has fallen by a tenth each season.
truth: The vein under the Imperial Grain Prefecture is a capillary of the Jing Capital veins. It is not failing. It is being pulled.

lore: The Kingdom of Cloud Stockades has no king, no roads a cart can use and no Registry office; the testers come once every few years if the passes are open. Its people herd goats, gather wild herbs and hunt cloud-leopards with crossbows. Every nine years the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's recruiters walk through, and every child dreams of the Sword Stair. The elders keep a cave of old manuals left by a cultivator who died here, and nobody in the valleys can read the script.
name: Kingdom of Cloud Stockades
summary: Forty stockaded villages in high valleys under the peaks, ruled by a council of elders and visited by the outside world once a season. The backwater every hero claims to come from.
truth: The manuals are a Dim Age Wind Dao method, complete through Core Formation.

lore: The sect has lived at the battlefield's edge for four thousand years, cultivating yin from its ghosts and keeping them penned with banners. The empire pays it to stop the dead from walking south, and orthodox sects hold their noses and let it. It teaches the Ghost and Death Daos, talks to the dead for a fee and recruits children who see things others don't. Its strength peaks in the seventh month.
name: Soul-Calling Sect
summary: Ghost cultivators who keep the dead of the old battlefield in place, sell seances to the bereaved and raise ghost soldiers for anyone who pays.
truth: The sect's banners can no longer turn the dead. They are being pulled toward the coast by something stronger, and the sect is pretending it planned the marches.

lore: The Northern Garrison Prefecture exists to stop the flow of rooted children uphill. General Yan Ku, a Core Formation spear cultivator who failed the Sword Stair as a boy, commands six thousand soldiers and the Registry's northern office. Families here serve in the garrison by law, and children learn drill before letters. The general pays well for smugglers' heads and better for proof that a Clear Heaven Sword Sect disciple took a registered child.
name: Northern Garrison Prefecture
summary: A military prefecture of the empire at the foot of the hills, garrisoned by conscripted spear cultivators and run by a general who hates the Clear Heaven Sword Sect.

lore: The pagoda was built with the Armillary Pavilion's help two thousand years ago, and its array still holds a circle of calm water around the cape. Formation masters study it from outside; only imperial engineers may enter. When the stones run late, wrecks follow. The keeper's office now spends more on stones than it gets, and the pagoda has gone dark twice this year.
name: Sea-Calming Pagoda
summary: A nine-story lighthouse pagoda on the southern cape whose array calms storms within sight of its lamp. It burns a spirit stone every night.

lore: Lingzhi Gardens grew mushrooms for the Cinnabar Hill Sect for eight hundred years and refused every offer the Apricot Grove Valley made. Ten years ago a black rot took the caves, then the terraces. The king sold his crown jewels to buy cures that did not work. Children here grow up poor and hating the valley, and the youths who can fight hire on as herb thieves.
name: Kingdom of Lingzhi Gardens
summary: Once the richest herb gardens outside the Apricot Grove Valley's control, now a kingdom of dead terraces and angry people. Its lingzhi caves went black in a single summer.
truth: The Apricot Grove Valley's blight was carried into the caves by a gardener the valley bought. He still works for the king.

lore: The Vermilion Talisman Sect disciples learn calligraphy before cultivation and spend their first three years grinding cinnabar. The sect teaches the Fire and Lightning Daos through talisman script, and its exploding talismans are standard issue in the imperial army. It is a Clear Heaven Sword Sect vassal on paper and a supplier to everyone in practice. Its outer disciples sell seconds in Boundary Head Town at a third of the price, some of which work.
name: Vermilion Talisman Sect
summary: A talisman sect on a cinnabar peak above the terraces. It mines its own ink, recruits farm children and sells talismans to the empire and the Clear Heaven Sword Sect alike.
truth: The Vermilion Talisman Sect's cinnabar seam runs into the root of the Clear Heaven Sword Sect's main peak. The miners have started hearing a sword hum in the rock, very faintly.

lore: The Pearl Shore looks south and east toward the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s waters and the [[Thousand Isles]], and both look back. Pirate lords raid for slaves and grain, shark-folk collectors take toll on every catch, and pearl divers bring up spirit pearls that pay for both. Imperial pirate-hunters collect bounties and bribes in equal measure. Half-bloods with sea-clan blood live quietly in the coves, and the marsh's black markets begin at its western edge.
name: The Pearl Shore
summary: A coast of headlands, coves and pearl shoals facing the Thousand Isles and the sea clans' waters. Pirates raid it, pearl divers work it and every village is a fort.
truth: A jiao of the Azure Wave Palace's court nests its young in a sea cave off this coast. If one is ever taken, the sea clans will come ashore.

lore: Laver's people farm seaweed on ropes across the flats and dry it on their roofs. There is no king, only a Tide Warden elected by the villages. They keep a shrine facing the Stump and leave a bowl of rice for it every new moon. A Qi Condensation hedge cultivator is the strongest person in the kingdom, and outsiders come only to buy laver or hide.
name: Kingdom of Laver
summary: A tide-flat kingdom of seaweed farmers so poor the Registry rarely bothers testing them. They have watched the Stump every night for a thousand years.
truth: The villagers have started humming a tune nobody taught them, all at the same hour of the night.

lore: A beast's core holds its cultivation, so humans hunt beasts for cores and beasts hunt humans for revenge. They rule the Vast Wilds Continent and the deep places of every continent.
name: Spirit Beasts
summary: Beasts that woke to qi. They grow slowly, live long, and from Nascent Soul on can take human form.

lore: Ghosts grow by gathering yin and resentment. A ghost that keeps its mind for a thousand years becomes a power; the Pale Sovereign has kept hers for sixty-six thousand.
name: Ghosts
summary: Souls that never moved on. Most are mindless; the old ones of the Long Dusk Continent keep courts, laws and grudges older than any sect.

lore: Humans call them beasts and beasts call them human. Most hide what they are; the rest live in Shared Roost City or die young.
name: Half-bloods
summary: Children of humans and spirit beasts or sea clans. Strong bloodlines and no home.

lore: Humans hold the Morning Star Continent, the Floating Peak Continent and the Myriad Sands Continent outright and cling to the edges of the other three continents. They live short lives and make up for it in numbers and ambition.
name: Humans
summary: The most numerous race and the most divided. Most cultivators are human, and so are most of their victims.

lore: They came through Heaven's Scar twice. Survivors describe them as hunger with a shape, and say the worst ones speak in your own voice.
name: Outer Demons
summary: Predators from the Void Sea that possess, devour and corrupt. Every child is told they are gone.
truth: They are not gone. A few slipped out during the war and wear human faces. The Void Choir hears the rest singing through the seal.

lore: An old enough spirit herb grows legs and runs. An old enough tree grows a mind and holds a grudge for centuries.
name: Spirit Plants
summary: Herbs and trees that woke. Most are prey for alchemists; the ones in the Evergreen Deep fight back.

lore: The sea clans were here before the land, or so they say. Every ship on the outer ocean sails by the Azure Wave Palace's leave, and every human port pays toll in one form or another.
name: Sea Clans
summary: Jiao flood dragons, shark-folk, turtle sages and the things of the deep trenches. They hold the Shoreless Sea.

lore: The Safe Passage lord is a Nascent Soul water cultivator with flawless manners. His islands are paved, his mortals are fed, and his captains' children are tutored in three scripts. Other lords call him lucky. He funds the League's treasury and votes for whatever keeps the League from looking too closely at anything.
name: Safe Passage Stockade
summary: The richest pirate lordship in the isles, whose sixty sails raid as far as the Floating Peak Continent and have not lost a hull to the sea in forty years.
truth: He is the Sea Sovereign's chief tributary in the League, and his ships are how the [[Azure Wave Palace]] means to carry the dragon pearl home once someone steals it from the [[Floating Peak Continent]].

lore: Scavengers may dive for a fee paid to the queen's clerks. The upper hulls are stripped; the lower ones hold sealed holds, drowned crews and the occasional ghost that wants its cargo delivered. An appraiser can make a career here learning the ship-marks of every navy and sect in the world. The water is so thick with rotting spirit wood that it glows faint green at night.
name: Tomb of a Hundred Ships
summary: A lagoon where the pirates sink the ships they cannot sell. Hulls lie twenty deep, and the oldest are warships from the Outer Demon War with cargo nobody bothered to take.
top: Foundation Establishment (ghosts in the lower hulls)
truth: The bottom hull is a supply ship of the Scar's defenders, sunk in the Outer Demon War. Its hold is still sealed, and it still hums.

lore: A turtle clerk assesses toll by the cargo's weight and the crew's cultivation; a Foundation passenger costs more than a hold of rice. Payment is in spirit stones, pearls or service. Ships that pay fly a white scale pennant and are left alone as far as the [[Rim]] mist. The post is commanded by a white jiao, the Sovereign's grand-nephew, who is bored, ambitious and known to start fights for entertainment.
name: White Scale Barrier
summary: The sea clans' toll post on the Toll Line: a ring of coral towers round a lagoon, where every ship bound past the Morning Star Continent's outer coast stops to pay.
truth: The white jiao wants a war to make his name. He pays poachers to raid his own nursery reefs so he can blame Jing fishermen.

lore: The White Fang lord is a Core Formation saber cultivator who took the title by killing a Beast Court envoy, and his hall is roofed with the envoy's hide. His islands are a frontier town of raiders, tanners, core-cutters and tamers' agents; children learn to skin before they can swim and to grade a core by its smell. Mortal fishing villages tithe to him for protection, which mostly means the beasts come for him first.
name: White Fang Stockade
summary: A pirate lordship of beast-raiders on a ring of jungle islands. Its lord pays bounties for cores by grade and sells cubs to tamers by the cage.
truth: He survives by selling the Beast Court the camps of rival raiders.

lore: A fast ship reaches the [[Vast Wilds Continent]]'s coast from here in two days. Raiders slip up estuaries, take cores, eggs and cubs, and sell them in the isles to tamers and alchemists from every continent. The [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]] answers with flights of storm birds, the odd sea serpent, and every few decades something much worse. Half-blood crews from [[Shared Roost City]] sign on as trackers, because they can smell a lair and pass for either side.
name: Raider Isles
summary: The western isles nearest the Vast Wilds Continent, where pirate crews raid beast lairs on the jungle coast for cores and cubs, and the Beast Court raids them back.
truth: The Beast Court's Storm Roc lets the raiders operate. Nearly every cub they take comes from the White Ape King's lineages.

lore: A claim is a carved marker stone and a line in the registry; the registrars are neutral, underpaid and bribed by everyone. Disputes go to the ring: one champion a side, below Core Formation, to first blood or worse. The market sells talisman fragments, bronze, old jade slips and sifted beach sand by the sack, which now and then holds a spirit stone. Sects scout the ring for fighters.
name: Marker-Stone Town
summary: The isles' claims town, where scavenger sects register their stakes, sell salvage and settle disputes in a duel ring paved with Ascent Age flagstones.

lore: In summer it is a lane of icebergs and fog, worked by sealers and by the [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders who wait in the fog for the Floating Peak Continent's grain ships. In winters cold enough an ice bridge forms, and the [[Iron Bone Tribes]] have crossed it four times in recorded history to raid the Floating Peak Continent's lowlands. The Floating Peak Continent's lowland lords keep fire arrays along the shore to break the ice, and the tribes' shamans curse them for it.
name: Ice Bridge Sea
summary: The cold strait between the Floating Peak Continent and the Black Frost Continent. In hard winters it freezes from shore to shore, and the Iron Bone khans ride across.
truth: The last two winters came within days of a full bridge, and the tribes are choosing a Great Khan.

lore: Sailors who reach the mist see blue terraces going down into darkness, lit from below by something that is not the sun. Ice from the lower steps never melts and is prized for Ice Dao weapons; a sliver sells for a high-grade stone. Every expedition to cut it has lost people to the cold, the fall, or the shapes seen moving on the lower steps. The Black Frost Continent's shamans call it the back door and will not sail within sight of it.
name: The Ice Stair
summary: Where the polar sea pours over the Rim and freezes on the way down: terraces of ice a thousand li wide descending into the void. Things climb it.
truth: Outer demons climb it whenever the tide runs high. Most freeze on the upper steps. The ones that don't come ashore wearing whalers' faces.

lore: A bead wraps a diver in air and a ward against the deep: a Low-grade bead lasts an hour at fifty fathoms, a High-grade one a day at three hundred. The bead-makers here are the best water-art refiners in the Shattered Sea and kill to keep their recipes. Appraisers grade salvage on the dock before it dries, and grade it low. The Gate of Sinking and Rising collects one part in five of everything landed, and the [[Corpse-Diver School]] undercuts everyone from the next island over.
name: Market of Water-Parting Beads
summary: A stilt town over the shallowest valley, where divers rent water-parting beads by the hour, sell what they bring up and drink away what they don't.

lore: The Hall teaches formations the hard way: apprentices redraw seal script on the forts' outer walls while the walls are live, and a wrong stroke burns off fingers. It examines candidates every spring in the [[Harbor of the Changing Watch]]; anyone with a steady hand and a Qi Condensation base may sit. Its graduates are the best seal-script masters alive. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] has tried for three thousand years to buy the Hall's methods and been refused every time; the Hall's masters call the Armillary Pavilion's arrays toll booths.
name: Hall of Array Mending
summary: The formation masters who maintain the seal's outer arrays under contract to the Seal Watch. They take apprentices from any sect, and few apprentices ever go home.
truth: The Hall's master has worked out that the outer arrays now carry load meant for the center. He told the Warden, and the Warden ordered him to tell no one else.

lore: Immortal jade cannot be cut by anything below Nascent Soul, so scavengers work the cracks and sell the dust to refiners at a mid-grade stone a jin. Inside are flooded halls whose bodies have not rotted. The [[Court of No Light]] sends ghost clerks to register each corpse; the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] sends crews to steal them. Whoever is caught by the other side is added to the count.
name: Reef of Broken Jade
summary: A slab of the fallen span nine li long, jutting from the sea along the fall line. Its halls are flooded, its jade is immortal, and two courts say its dead belong to them.
truth: One sealed hall still answers to Upper Realm tokens, like parts of the [[Fallen Ladder]], and last winter it opened briefly for someone.

lore: Tidal races here can roll a ship end over end, and the safe hours are posted in every harbor on both coasts. The [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] keeps a chained floating rock over the narrows and charges ships for passing beneath it; the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] calls that piracy and sends warships through at the wrong hour to prove it. It is also the shortest sea road from the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s waters to the Floating Peaks, and both coasts have begun counting sea-clan scouts.
name: Tide Gate Strait
summary: The strait between the Morning Star Continent and the Floating Peak Continent, where the tide pours between the inner and outer seas twice a day like a river in flood.

lore: The Pavilion of the Rising Tide teaches the Water and Wind Daos through the tides: disciples meditate in the surf and rise a rank for every tide-race won against the current. Its escorts guard convoys through the isles for a twentieth of the cargo, and a convoy that declines is usually robbed within the week. It recruits at the Kingdom of Hazy Waters auctions and pays the best prices for spirit-root children. Its patriarch hates the [[Raider Isles]] raiders for drawing the Beast Court's anger onto the isles.
name: Pavilion of the Rising Tide
summary: The largest sect of the central isles: water and storm cultivators who teach tide-reading, sell escort fleets and sit on the League council.
truth: The patriarch pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]] for his escort routes, which is why his convoys never lose a hull to sea beasts.

lore: The valleys sank whole when the central continent broke, so halls, gardens and treasuries sit under fifty to three hundred fathoms of clear water. Divers buy water-parting beads in the [[Market of Water-Parting Beads]] and go down on the bead's clock: when it dims, you rise or drown. The shallows were stripped ten thousand years ago; the rich ruins, like the furnaces of the [[Valley of the Pill Furnaces]], are deep, sealed and still guarded by Ascent Age arrays. The [[Gate of Sinking and Rising]] sells the licenses, and most of what comes up goes to the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] buyers bound for [[Fallen Star City]].
name: Sea of Sunken Valleys
summary: Clear water over the drowned valleys of the old central continent. Ascent Age towns lie intact on the bottom, and divers from every continent come to loot them.
truth: The Heavenly Scale Pavilion buyers on the docks fix salvage prices together, and the Pavilion holds the notes on half the bead-makers in the Market of Water-Parting Beads.

lore: The Whale-Spear Gate teaches the Spear and Ice Daos and a cold-blooded body art for working wet in winter wind. Disciples hunt from floes with harpoons tempered in whale blood and sell cores to refiners at the [[Frost Fair]]. It recruits whaling children by the throw: put an iron harpoon through a seal's skull at forty paces and you are in. It is at war with the whale-riding sea clans, who sink its boats, and pays the [[Eternal Night Palace]] to be left alone on land.
name: Whale-Spear Gate
summary: A sect of whale hunters who cultivate the Spear Dao on the ice. A disciple's rank is the size of the largest whale they have helped kill.
truth: Its elders have seen what climbs the [[Ice Stair]]. They chip the frozen ones out of the upper steps and sell them to the [[Eternal Night Palace]], which wants an outer demon's cultivation method.

lore: Diviners sell forecasts of the next lull by the hour, and the good ones are richer than the captains. Betting houses take wagers on which ships come out the far side. Cargo spoils, crews desert, and moneylenders buy holds cheap from desperate captains. Divination students apprentice with the forecasters, who test them by asking for the next lull's hour; three wrong answers and you are sent home.
name: Harbor of Waiting Winds
summary: The harbor on the storm belt's eastern edge where ships wait, sometimes for months, for the lull. A city of gamblers, weather-readers and captains going broke.
truth: The best forecaster in the harbor does not read the sky. She bribes an elder of the [[Abbey of Drawn Lightning]], whose rods feel the drum in the eye before every lull.

lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables list the date; the condition is not in the tables. The gate admits only cultivators holding a pill furnace with a live fire in it, so alchemists hire divers to escort them down and keep the furnace dry in a bubble ward. Inside is a dry library of jade slips on fire control and formulas lost since the Severance, kept by furnace golems that test visitors by making them refine. Bad pills are punished. A Nascent Soul aura cracks the gate. The next opening is five years off.
name: Realm of the Pill Scriptures
summary: The drowned alchemy sect's library shard. Its gate on the valley's lowest terrace opens for ten days every twenty-four years, only to those below Nascent Soul carrying a lit furnace.
truth: The golems copy what visitors refine. The library has been learning the Sealed Era's alchemy for three thousand years, and some of its newer slips are better than anything outside.

lore: Over two hundred furnaces stand on stone terraces at ninety fathoms. The cold ones were looted down to the bricks; the warm ones are sealed, and divers who pry at them come up boiled. Ash scraped from their outer walls steadies a pill's fire and sells for its weight in low-grade stones. The [[Apricot Grove Valley]] alchemists pay divers to bring the ash up and, quietly, to report on the seals.
name: Valley of the Pill Furnaces
summary: A drowned valley lined with the pill furnaces of an Ascent Age alchemy sect. Sixty-six thousand years underwater, some of them are still warm.
truth: The warm furnaces are still refining. They have tended the same batch since the Severance, and it is nearly done.

lore: The anchor is a black pillar bound with nine bronze bands; within forty li of it, space behaves. The town sells rift wards, crystal tongs, cold-proof furs and bunks priced by distance from the pillar. The Pavilion That Holds the Void buys crystal at the quay, and so do smugglers who pay a little more and ask nothing. Every season some crew comes back one member short, or one extra.
name: Town of Fixed Space
summary: The one island on the fall line where rifts never open, held still by an Ascent Age anchor stone. Crystal hunters sleep, trade and bury each other here.
truth: The bands are failing. Four have cracked since the tide turned, the last this decade, and the town council has agreed not to count them aloud.

lore: The landing is a raft of white-lacquered boats lashed together, staffed by ghost clerks with nets and ledgers. Families pay to have a drowned relative searched for in the registers, and pay more to have one released before shipping. Living workers are hired to haul the nets, because ghost clerks cannot haul nets; the pay is days of lifespan returned. Shark-folk patrols circle it constantly.
name: Soul-Ferry Landing
