summary: The Court of No Light's floating customs house, where drowned souls are netted from the current, registered and shipped to the Pale City. The living may land with a pass.
truth: The clerks enter one soul in twenty as lost to the sea and sell it to a broker who sets it into the cores of the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] puppets. This is why some of the Gate's puppets are not empty.

lore: The line runs between two reef pillars, one carved with the Jing seal and one with the Sovereign's, and a ship that crosses without paying is fair game. Jing fishing towns live off the shoals inside it; the richest shoals lie outside. Sea-clan young hatch on the outer reefs each spring, and poachers sell their scales to alchemists for ten times the price of fish. Every few years a poachers' port burns: the Jing call it a raid, and the sea clans call it law.
name: Ocean of the Dividing Line
summary: The waters off the Morning Star Continent's outer coast, cut by the Toll Line: inside it, the Great Jing's fishing fleets; outside, the sea clans' toll and law.
truth: The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] court wants a sea war. War would let it conscript the coast's fishing families, who hide the last untested spirit-root children in the empire.

lore: The Gate of Sinking and Rising teaches turtle breath, the Water Dao and a body art that hardens the chest against the deep. Its divers map the valleys and sell licenses by the season; an unlicensed diver is tied to a stone and allowed to keep whatever he finds at the bottom. It recruits the dock children who stay under longest in the summer contest. It is at war with the [[Corpse-Diver School]], whose corpse divers need no beads and no licenses.
name: Gate of Sinking and Rising
summary: The diving sect that rules the drowned valleys: it sells the dive licenses, keeps the claim maps and teaches breath arts nobody else can match.
truth: The claim maps are wrong on purpose. The Gate of Sinking and Rising's elders keep the richest valleys off them and drown anyone who finds one.

lore: Each buoy carries a plate of seal script and a bell that rings when anything with qi crosses the line, so the forts know where to aim. Buoy-tenders row the line in pairs to scrape weed and replace chain; it is the best-paid safe job in the Shattered Sea until a bell rings next to you. Broken plates sell in [[Ten Thousand Sails]] as protective charms for a mid-grade stone, and the Watch treats taking one as an attack on the seal.
name: Chain of Floating Bells
summary: The marker line around the Scar: three thousand six hundred bronze buoys chained in a ring twenty-two thousand li from the Stump, each hung with a bell. The Watch sinks anything that crosses.
truth: The buoys are the outermost ring of the seal array, not markers. For eleven years the northern bells have rung on still nights with nothing crossing, and always from the inside.

lore: The imperial seals on the chests still hold, and anyone who breaks one is entered in the Jing registry as a thief of the throne, with a bounty that never lapses. Raiders dive the wreck anyway and melt what they find. Jing patrols sweep the reef on every pass. An appraiser can tell a coin's mint and year from its rim, and so can the registrars, which is how most divers get caught.
name: Graveyard of the Tax Barges
summary: A reef where a Great Jing tax fleet carrying a year of southern revenue broke up in a typhoon two hundred years ago. The empire still claims every coin.

lore: The archive is carved into the shell of its eldest sage, a turtle the size of a hill who has not moved in nine thousand years. Its scholars write law on shells: what a ship owes, what a poacher owes, which human ports are in debt. Their faction holds the Sovereign back from war. Humans may petition the archive to lower a toll or settle a blood debt; it takes years and costs more than the debt, but it is the only appeal there is.
name: Turtle Archive
summary: The turtle sages of the Azure Wave Palace's court, who keep the sea's law, set its tolls and remember every debt owed to the sea clans for fifty thousand years.
truth: The eldest sage is brother to the [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]]'s Old Tortoise. Through the two of them, the sea and the land beasts have been talking for a century, and the subject is humans.

lore: Every autumn the great whales pass south along this coast from the polar sea toward their calving grounds, and every spring they come back. The [[Kingdom of Whale Oil]] whalers wait for them, and so do the monks of the [[Sea Lotus Temple]], who pay to have harpooned whales cut free. Under the narrows runs a trench where the inkfolk keep [[Inkwell City]] and sell the best talisman ink in the world. The sea clans count every whale that does not come back.
name: Sea of Passing Whales
summary: The narrows between the Myriad Sands Continent's outer coast and the Rim, where the whale road runs so close to shore that a monk on the cliffs can count the pods.
truth: The whale road is narrowing. Each year the pods swim closer to the coast, as if something were pushing them away from the Rim.

lore: When a whaler has a whale on the line, a monk rows out with spirit stones and pays its price to have it cut free. Whalers have learned to harpoon more whales. The temple teaches the vajra body and a chant that calms sea beasts, and takes in the orphans of drowned whalers, who make devout and very strong monks. Sea-clan pilgrims come to its lower caves to hear the sutras, and a few shark-folk have taken vows.
name: Sea Lotus Temple
summary: A daughter temple of the Thousand Lamps Temple on a sea cliff above the whale road. Its monks ransom harpooned whales and preach to anything that surfaces.
truth: The temple tags ransomed whales with prayer beads and sells their tracks to a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] whaling consortium. Compassion here has a price list too.

lore: The mirage hangs over open water a day's sail from [[Ten Thousand Sails]]; boats row into it and do not come out the other side. Inside is an empty Ascent Age market town on a ring of islets, its stalls still stocked with goods that have half-rotted into spirit materials, and its tide pools full of pearl clams the size of carts. A Foundation aura dispels the mirage, so island sects send their youngest disciples, who fight each other harder than anything inside.
name: Realm of the Sea Mirage
summary: A shard world that shows itself as a mirage city above the Confluence Isles every three years at the spring equinox. For seven days its gate is real, and only Qi Condensation cultivators can pass.
truth: The market is not empty. Its shopkeepers are still there, a half-step out of phase, and they remember every customer who did not pay.

lore: The Kingdom of the Pearl Crescent queens rule by the pearl ledger: every pearl brought up is weighed at the palace, and a tenth goes to the crown. Black pearls that glow in the dark are shark-folk tears; touching one is death, and the queen's executioners carry it out before the sea clans can. The kingdom farms spirit pearls in caged beds, the best eye-brightening pill ingredient in the isles. Spirit-root children are bought by League sects; the rest dive until their ears bleed.
name: Kingdom of the Pearl Crescent
summary: A mortal kingdom of pearl divers on a crescent of reef islands, where every child learns to dive before reading, and learns which pearls must never be touched.
truth: The queens have married shark-folk for twelve generations. The royal children are half-bloods, and the sea spares the kingdom for their sake.

lore: The crack runs a hundred li, and no rope has found its bottom. Bodies float up from it with their dantians emptied and no wound on them. The Gate of Sinking and Rising marks it on every map with a black ring. Core Formation divers go anyway, because the ruins on its lip are the best preserved in the sea and their arrays still glow.
name: Black Throat Abyss
summary: Where the deepest drowned valley drops into a crack in the sea floor. Divers who go near it come back without their cores, or don't come back.
truth: An Ascent Age master sleeps sealed in a cave abode on the crack's wall. His arrays are drawing qi from divers to wake him, and he is close. He sealed himself at Body Integration.

lore: The court has spent three centuries building tribulation arrays here: coral pillars, buried pearls and the bones of nine jiao who failed before. Thunder with nowhere to go strikes the cliff on its own every few days. Scavengers who sneak in after the pearls are found turned to glass. When the Sovereign finally rises, everything within a thousand li will lie under his tribulation clouds.
name: Cliff of the Dragon's Becoming
summary: A cliff on the trench's lip, blasted bare, where the Sovereign has prepared the ground for his dragon tribulation. Leftover thunder strikes anything that enters.
truth: The arrays are built for a tribulation he cannot survive without the pearl. If age or war forces him to rise early, he dies, and the court splits between generals and sages.

lore: Each continent's ships moor in a separate basin so their crews never meet off duty. The Merit Office trades Watch tokens for pills, manuals and passage, and rotation disciples sell spare rations on the quay. The [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] swordsmen and the [[Eternal Night Palace]] blood cultivators eat in one canteen under one rule: a fight costs both sides their term's merit. Qi Condensation laborers sign three-year contracts at a low-grade stone a day plus board, double what a kingdom pays a cultivator guard.
name: Harbor of the Changing Watch
summary: The Seal Watch's supply harbor on a cracked jade terrace that was once a stair of the Ladder. Every rotation, grain barge, convict and volunteer lands here.
truth: Forged Watch tokens from [[Ten Thousand Sails]] circulate on the quay. The Merit Office lets them, because anyone desperate enough to buy a forgery is worth following, and some of them lead to the [[Void Choir]].

lore: Ships cross by compass and sound, ringing bells every hundred breaths. Ghost pilots from [[Long Dusk Continent]] offer to guide them through for a price in days of lifespan, and they are the only pilots who never get lost. The Heavenly Scale Pavilion cargo bound for the [[Pale City]] comes this way, and so do the pirates who know it. The fog has thickened every year for a century, and the strait's fishing villages are moving away.
name: Yellow Fog Sea
summary: The strait between the Myriad Sands Continent and the Long Dusk Continent, where dust blown off the Sand Sea meets the Long Dusk Continent's dusk and makes a yellow fog that never lifts.
truth: The fog thickens because the Sand Sea is spreading west, faster than anyone in Myriad Sands admits.

lore: The Ash Lord's family was executed when a Jing prince wanted their spirit vein, and he has burned eleven Jing coastal towns since, always ones that prince owns. His people are runaway conscripts, escaped bondservants and their children, who grow up knowing the imperial registry as the thing that takes you away. He splits plunder evenly and hangs anyone who sells a captive to the Night Banquet, which makes him unusual on these reefs.
name: Stockade of Ashes
summary: The strongest raider lordship on the black reefs, ruled by a Core Formation fire cultivator who was once a Jing magistrate's son.
truth: The prince quietly funds his raids. Every burned town drives the Ancestor Emperor's other heirs to beg that prince for protection.

lore: Every current in the archipelago passes through here, and so does every ship. [[Ten Thousand Sails]] sells anything, and its array platform is the only the Heavenly Circuit hub at sea. The [[Thousand Isles League]] meets here when an outsider threatens the isles and otherwise lets its members rob one another. Island sects hire out as escorts, the yards build spirit ships for half the world's navies, and children with spirit roots are auctioned at the spring tests. The [[Great Jing Dynasty]] is said to be building a fleet to end all of it.
name: Confluence Isles
summary: The crowded heart of the Thousand Isles, where four currents meet: Ten Thousand Sails's harbor, the League's hall, and a hundred islands that live off both.
top: Deity Transformation (the Isles League's three island masters)
truth: The League's current speaker pays the [[Azure Wave Palace]], and the agenda of its next meeting was written in the Sea Sovereign's court.

lore: The islet is a single prison tower inside a ring of silencing arrays. Guards wear wax in their ears and talk by hand. The Watch says everyone inside is touched by the [[Void Choir]]; families who come asking are handed an urn. Fishermen say that on still nights the whole tower hums the same tune, in harmony.
name: Islet of Sealed Voices
summary: A rock outside the buoy line where the Seal Watch keeps anyone caught humming a tune nobody taught them. No ship stops there, and no prisoner has ever been released.
truth: Fewer than half the prisoners are Choir. The rest saw something on duty they were told never to speak of, and spoke.

lore: Each sword marks the grave of the cultivator who carried it, and many still hum with their owner's intent. A Sword Dao cultivator who sits among them can feel the old sect's forms; one who pulls a sword must win a duel with what is left of its owner. The lower slopes hold the sect's herb terraces, which is why the [[Hall of Seed-Seekers]] wants it.
name: Peak of Sword Graves
summary: An island that was the peak of an Ascent Age sword sect, where ten thousand swords stand planted in the slopes as grave markers. Two scavenger sects have fought over it for ninety years.

lore: The jiao was an Azure Wave Palace toll-collector that sank fishing fleets over unpaid toll; nineteen pirate captains burned it with fire ships two thousand years ago and founded the League on its bones. Oaths sworn on the skull are binding, and a lord who breaks one is said to drown within the year. The marrow was sold long ago, but the ribs still hum with water qi, and Water Dao cultivators meditate between them.
name: Islet of the Jiao's Bones
summary: An islet made of the ribs of a flood dragon the League's founders killed. Every lord who joins the League swears on its skull.
truth: The jiao's soul is still in the skull. It hears every oath and reports it to the Sea Sovereign, which is how he knows which League lords to buy.

lore: The [[Azure Wave Palace]] stands on a ridge at the trench's lip, and the [[City of Pearl Light]] glows in the wall below it. Humans come only as envoys, hostages, tribute or invited scholars. The court is split: the [[Iron Gill Host]] generals want war with the [[Floating Peak Continent]] for the dragon pearl now, and the [[Turtle Archive]] sages say a Sovereign who starts a war on land before his tribulation dies in it. Tribute ships from the [[Isles of the Following Current]] arrive at night and leave lighter.
name: Abyss of the Flood Dragon
summary: The Sea Sovereign's home waters: a deep blue basin over the trench where the Azure Wave Palace stands, patrolled by shark-folk and closed to any ship without a toll pass.
top: Body Integration (the Sea Sovereign, one pearl short of a true dragon)
truth: The Sovereign has chosen theft over war. He is quietly shopping among human sects for thieves who can walk into the Floating Peaks.

lore: The Town That Meets the Clouds hangs a few hundred feet above the waves and strains at its chains, so its harbor is rebuilt every decade. The market sells pristine Ascent Age fragments, sky-crane eggs, wind-cured cloud moss for alchemy, and maps of the upper shards, half of them lies. There are no walls, only the drop. Debts are settled at the edge, in front of witnesses.
name: Town That Meets the Clouds
summary: A market town on the broad back of a low shard, reached by chain lifts from a floating harbor below. Everything sold here came down from higher up.

lore: Whalers from the Black Frost Continent's northern coast haul up here in the third month and leave before the first snow. The town renders blubber into lamp oil, cuts spirit bone for refiners and sells kun-whale cores when someone lands one, which happens every few years and makes a crew rich for life. The sea clans call each kill murder and send a reckoning every few summers. Anyone still in town when the sun sets for the winter is not found in spring.
name: Whale-Rib Town
summary: A summer whaling town built inside the ribs of a whale that died on the ice a thousand years ago. In winter it is left to the dark and whatever walks on the ice.
truth: Last spring two whalers who stayed the winter walked back into town. Their families took them home and have let no one see them since.

lore: The Harpoon Throne passes to whichever royal child kills the largest whale in their eighteenth year. Children learn the oar before they walk and the harpoon at ten; spirit-root children train in the royal harpoon hall and become the kingdom's only cultivators above Qi Condensation. It sells oil, spirit bone and ambergris to the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]], which also holds its debts. The Sea Lotus monks' ransom money is now a third of its income.
name: Kingdom of Whale Oil
summary: A whaling kingdom on the islands off the Myriad Sands Continent's outer coast. Its oil lights half the lamps in the Myriad Sands Continent, including, quietly, the life lamps of the Thousand Lamps Temple.
truth: The [[Thousand Lamps Temple]] is its largest oil buyer, through a merchant front, and has privately asked it not to stop whaling.

lore: The storm never stops, but it breathes: every forty-nine days it slackens for about a day, and the ships waiting in the [[Harbor of Waiting Winds]] race through. Those who cannot wait hug the [[Black Frost Continent]]'s south coast and pay the [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders instead. Lightning here is dense enough to temper a body, and talismans drawn under it hold twice the charge. The [[Abbey of Drawn Lightning]] owns the reefs where it strikes most. In the middle lies a calm eye, the [[Isle of the Thunder Drum]], that nobody living has reached.
name: Ocean of Mad Winds
summary: A belt of permanent storm across the northern Shattered Sea. Ships between the Floating Peak Continent and Myriad Sands cross it in a lull or go the long way past the Black Frost Continent's raiders.
truth: The lulls are getting shorter and less regular, and the abbey has stopped publishing its count of them.

lore: The skull alone is a hill. Spirit marrow seeps from the bones into the water, so the reef teems with fish, crabs and the things that eat them, and sea-clan and human divers fight over the marrow channels. Ambergris from the gut washes up after storms and sells as incense for its weight in mid-grade stones. The Sea Lotus monks hold a funeral here every year; the whalers hold an auction the same week.
name: Isle of the Kun's Grave
summary: The carcass of a kun whale that died two thousand years ago, grown over with reef until it became an island. Its bones still seep qi, and everything in the sea comes to feed.

lore: The old kun has taken human form once in living memory, to walk into Whale-Rib Town and eat its headman. His pods, a few hundred whales and the sea-clan riders who herd them, feed in the krill blooms from the fourth month to the eighth, then swim south down the whale road. The riders trade with anyone who does not hunt and sell whale song sealed in shells, which calms beasts and is worth a fortune to tamers.
name: Court of the Old Kun
summary: The summer domain of an ancient kun whale, a Nascent Soul beast lord whose pods gather under the ice each year. In his waters, whaling is war.
truth: He feeds near the Ice Stair on purpose. Whatever climbs it, he eats, and he is the only reason the climbers are few.

lore: A ring of lightning walls the eye, so it can only be approached in a lull, and lulls end without warning. Through a spyglass the island shows a bronze drum the size of a hill under a roof of black tile. The [[Abbey of Drawn Lightning]] calls the eye holy ground and forbids attempts. A reward posted in the [[Harbor of Waiting Winds]] for a rubbing of the drum's inscription stands at three high-grade stones.
name: Isle of the Thunder Drum
summary: The calm eye of the storm belt: a circle of still water around an island no one has reached alive in living memory. Every forty-nine days a drumbeat from it carries a thousand li.
truth: The drum is the heart of a storm wall raised around the Scar in the First Sealing, and the belt is its last working arc. Each beat answers a pulse from the Scar, and the beats are coming closer together.

lore: Ghost Way cultivators meditate on its rim, because the yin is the densest in the Shoreless Sea, and those who misjudge it join it. A living person who falls in is not drowned so much as outnumbered. In Ghost Month it rises into a waterspout that reaches the clouds, and on those nights the [[Nether Shard]] is said to show in the water instead of the sky.
name: The Cold Whirl
summary: Where the outer sea's currents meet and sink: a slow whirlpool of grey water thick with souls, cold enough to frost a ship's sails in summer.
truth: It drains toward the Nether Shard. Every Ghost Month a few thousand souls go down it, registered by neither court.

lore: The Kingdom of Two Waters kings are Jing vassals by registry and sea-clan clients by toll, and have lasted nine hundred years by being too useful to crush. Children learn two scripts and two sets of manners. Spirit-root children are supposed to be reported to the Jing registrars; the kings hide one in three and send them to sea-clan tutors instead. The current king is sixteen, and both sides have a candidate for his regent.
name: Kingdom of Two Waters
summary: A kingdom of fishing islands astride the Toll Line that pays tribute to both the Great Jing and the Azure Wave Palace, and spies on each for the other.

lore: Rifts here last from a breath to a season. Small ones are a nuisance; large ones open onto the void sea, and the cold pouring out freezes rigging solid. Rift edges leave void crystal, which every storage ring and bag needs, so crystal hunters swarm the field and race the closings. The [[Pavilion That Holds the Void]] reads the rifts and buys the crystal. Debris from the span lies along the line, and the [[Court of No Light]] claims every body in it, as it does in the [[Fallen Ladder]].
name: Sea of Torn Sky
summary: The path the Ladder's upper span tore as it fell toward the Long Dusk Continent. Space along it never healed: rifts open in the air and on the water, and close on whatever is halfway through.
truth: Not every rift opens onto empty void. Twice this century something has come through a large one, and the [[Seal Watch]] burned the nearby islands and called it a fire.

lore: For half the year the sun never rises here, and the Rim's roar carries across the ice for days. In the brief summer the great whales come up the western whale road to feed on krill blooms along the ice edge, and whalers and sea clans follow them. The whalers work out of the [[Whale-Rib Town]] and hunt under the eye of the [[Court of the Old Kun]]. The Seal Watch guards the frozen host on the [[Demon-Sealing Glacier]] to the south. Nobody guards the Rim.
name: Drift-Ice Sea
summary: The polar sea north of the Black Frost Continent, where pack ice drifts toward the Rim and the falling ocean freezes on its way down into a stair of ice.
truth: The frozen host faces south because it came from the north. It climbed the [[Ice Stair]] while the war raged at the Scar, and the stair is still a door.

lore: A good spirit ship takes three years and a Core Formation refiner's attention, and costs as much as a small kingdom's treasury. The docks take apprentice refiners and array masters on ten-year bonds; those who survive the bond are hired anywhere. Keels are the bones of jiao and great whales, which is why the docks pay hunters well, and why the [[Azure Wave Palace]] considers every launch a corpse wearing sails.
name: Keel Docks
summary: The shipyards beside Ten Thousand Sails where spirit ships are built for anyone who pays: keels of sea-beast bone, hulls of ironwood, sails woven with wind arrays.
truth: The yards are laying a hundred hulls for a buyer paying through the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]]. It is the Great Jing's admiralty, and the fleet is meant for these isles.

lore: The islands have moved: Rekindling charts put them three hundred li further east. Neither the [[Beast Court of Ten Thousand Mountains]] nor the [[Court of No Light]] claims them, which tells sailors all they need. Ships that anchor too long report the ground breathing. Everyone fights over the strait's real cargo instead: immortal corpses from the Long Dusk Continent's coast, smuggled to the [[Jar-Mother Clans]] of the Vast Wilds Continent, who pay well for flesh that never rots.
name: Strait of the Sleeping Beast
summary: The strait between the Long Dusk Continent and the Vast Wilds Continent, crossed by a chain of long, ridged, warm islands that sailors swear is the spine of something asleep.
truth: It is an Ascent Age sea beast, one of those the tide is waking, and it rolled over in its sleep last spring.

lore: The stacks are the broken teeth of mountains on the old continent's southern rim. Channels between them shift as arches fall, and only local pilots know which are open this year. The haven preys on the southern route between the [[Morning Star Continent]], the [[Long Dusk Continent]] and the [[Myriad Sands Continent]], which every captain takes to avoid both the Scar and the storm belt. Its pirates answer to the queen of the [[Iron Bridge Stockade]], and her law is stricter than [[Ten Thousand Sails]]'s, which is to say it exists.
name: Sea of Maze Pillars
summary: A maze of sea stacks and fallen arches south of the Stump, where the inner sea's pirates hide their ships, their money and their prisoners.

lore: It happened twenty years ago; at low tide you can see the masts. The holds are full of plunder from a raid on the [[Morning Star Continent]]'s coast, and none of it has come up: divers who touch the cargo feel hands close round their ankles. League lords call it a curse. The lord's widow offers half the cargo to whoever brings back his body.
name: Bay of the Silent Sinking
summary: A shallow bay where a pirate lord's whole fleet of thirty ships sank in a dead calm in one night, every hull intact and every sailor still at his post.
truth: He had stopped paying the [[Azure Wave Palace]]. His crews' souls serve in the Sovereign's court now, and the hands on the divers' ankles are theirs, begging to be taken up.

lore: Inkfolk ink holds qi better than cinnabar: a talisman drawn in it keeps its charge for a century. They sell it by the drop at a raft market above the trench and take payment in spirit stones, books and secrets. Down in the trench the city is lit by their own skin, which changes color as they speak. They answer to the [[Azure Wave Palace]] in theory and to nobody in practice. Talisman makers from every continent apprentice here for the ink trade alone.
name: Inkwell City
summary: A city of the inkfolk, cuttlefish sea clans who live in a trench under the whale road and sell the best spirit ink in the world to talisman makers.
truth: Their best ink is not theirs. It is milked from something much larger at the trench bottom, and keeping it calm is getting harder.

lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables put the next opening in the coming autumn. The gate is a ring of white stone on the underside of a shard, so entrants climb down to it on ropes; a Core Formation aura cracks it. Inside are cloud meadows and crane herds bred from the mounts of Ascent Age immortals. An egg sells for a mid-grade stone in the [[Town That Meets the Clouds]], a tamed adult for ten. Cranes defend their nests in flocks, and the meadows have edges.
name: Realm of the Crane Pastures
summary: A shard world whose gate hangs under a floating shard and opens for thirty days every nine years. Only cultivators below Core Formation can pass; inside, Ascent Age cranes still graze.
truth: The herds are not wild. Something still whistles them home at dusk, and it has noticed the egg thieves.

lore: The Pavilion That Holds the Void teaches the Space Dao, rift-reading and the refining of storage artifacts, and its ring-smiths are the best artifact refiners in the Shattered Sea. Crystal hunters sell to it because nobody pays better. It tests children for spatial sense: blindfolded, a candidate must find a coin hidden in a fold of space. It is locked in a bitter quarrel with the [[Armillary Pavilion]], which wants its rift charts and calls its rings unlicensed.
name: Pavilion That Holds the Void
summary: Space Dao specialists who predict rift openings and turn void crystal into storage rings. Most rings sold anywhere in the world started here.
truth: Its forecasts come from an outer demon it keeps caged in nested space, which feels the void sea pressing on the world.

lore: Every tenth child born in the Kingdom of Calm Waves is sent at seven to serve in the Azure Wave Palace court; some come home at seventy, rich and strange. The rest grow up safe, fed and governed by sea law: no nets in the breeding months, no killing anything with scales. Kings are crowned by a jiao and buried at sea. The Kingdom of Calm Waves-born servants are the only humans the court trusts, so every sect that wants a spy below the sea tries to buy one.
name: Kingdom of Calm Waves
summary: The only human kingdom inside the Sovereign's waters: a ring of atolls that pays tribute in children and has not seen a storm, a pirate or a war in two thousand years.
truth: Each Kingdom of Calm Waves servant carries a sea-clan sigil under the tongue. Whoever buys one buys the Sovereign an ear.

lore: Cores are graded on the quay by color and weight, and a Core Formation beast's core sells for more than the ship that brought it. Half-bloods from Shared Roost City work as appraisers because they can smell a fake; Jar-Mother agents buy venom glands and say nothing. The stink carries ten li downwind, which makes the harbor easy for the Beast Court to find. Twice a century something huge comes out of the sea and eats it, and the next tide of hunters rebuilds.
name: Beast-Cutters' Harbor
summary: The isles' core market: a harbor of butchers, appraisers and buyers' agents where a beast's core, gall, hide and young are sold by the pound.

lore: Ships that go in lose time as well as space: crews come out with beards grown or wounds still fresh. The best void crystal on the fall line forms here, fist-sized, and one buys a Foundation Pill. The cold from the large rifts kills more hunters than the closings do. Time Dao cultivators come to study the slips in time, and a few stay longer than they meant to.
name: Abyss of a Thousand Gaps
summary: The densest stretch of the rift field, where the span's heaviest section struck the sea. Rifts open every hour, and the large ones open onto the void.
truth: Something on the far side holds the large rifts open a few breaths longer every year.

lore: Watch recruits swear their oath with a palm on the blank. Pilgrims from every continent come to touch it, and some leave sure they almost remembered something. Carving anything into the blank is punished by drowning; three scholars have tried in the last century, each certain they had recovered the name, and each carved a different one. Core Formation cultivators meditate before it to steady their hearts against inner demons.
name: Stele of the Missing Name
summary: The founding stele of the Seal Watch, raised at the Second Sealing. It lists every founder but one, and the blank where her name should be is worn smooth by hands.
truth: Every name carved so far was wrong. The right one would unpay the price of the seal, and the Pale Sovereign of the [[Court of No Light]] knows exactly what that would cost.

lore: The school buys drowned bodies from fishing villages, and from anyone else who can supply them, and refines them into diving puppets that work the deep for a month at a time. It sells salvage under the Gate of Sinking and Rising's prices and teaches puppetry, corpse refining and the Death Dao to anyone who pays tuition. Its puppets are crude beside the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]]'s, and the Gate sells it the cores that run them. The Gate of Sinking and Rising has burned its island twice; twice it moved.
name: Corpse-Diver School
summary: Demonic puppeteers who send refined corpses down to loot the drowned valleys. Corpses need no beads, no license and no share, which is why the Gate of Sinking and Rising wants them dead.
truth: Its best puppet came up from the [[Black Throat Abyss]] holding something and has refused every command since. The master keeps it chained in his cellar and is afraid to unmake it.

lore: The Sect of Gleaned Relics teaches appraisal before fighting: a novice must date a potsherd to the right millennium before learning a sword form. It sends its finds to the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] first, which keeps the swords and returns a stipend. It recruits from the beach sifters by watching which children find things. It despises the [[Hall of Seed-Seekers]] as the Apricot Grove Valley's gardeners and has fought it over the [[Peak of Sword Graves]] claim for ninety years.
name: Sect of Gleaned Relics
summary: The largest scavenger sect in the isles, sponsored by the Clear Heaven Sword Sect. It digs old sword graves and trains the best relic appraisers in the Shattered Sea.
truth: The Clear Heaven Sword Sect has told the Sect of Gleaned Relics to find one sword above all others, and not to draw it if they do.

lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables give the date to the hour, and sailors know before that, when the Rim's roar changes pitch. The bridge is falling water bent into a road by the shard's pull, and a Nascent Soul's weight breaks it. The shard is cold, bright and full of Ascent Age ruins that have never been looted, because anyone still on it when the bridge drops is carried off into the void. The last crossing was twenty-nine years ago.
name: Realm of the Water Bridge
summary: Every thirty-three years a shard world swings so close past the Rim here that the falling ocean bends into a bridge to it. For nine days, anyone below Nascent Soul can walk across.
truth: The old texts about Ascent Age masters walking out along the falling water describe this. The shard was a waystation, and its far side faces the void sea, not Severed Heaven.

lore: These are the isles nearest the [[Azure Wave Palace]]'s waters, and their pirate lords are the richest in the League: they raid far, never lose ships to storms or serpents, and always seem to know where the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] patrols are. A current runs through them to the open sea that carries a ship two days' sail in one. The pearl beds are the best in the archipelago, and divers from poorer islands learn quickly which pearls are taken and which are left.
name: Isles of the Following Current
summary: The eastern isles facing the open Shoreless Sea: rich, quiet and strangely safe. Sea beasts here leave ships alone, and nobody asks why.
truth: Every lord here pays the Sea Sovereign, and turtle sages below steer the current that names the isles. A lord who stops paying finds out when the current turns.

lore: Its admiral, a Nascent Soul spear cultivator of the imperial clan, is assembling a hundred war junks for the Pacification of the Isles, which the court has announced every decade for a century. Five years' service earns a pardon in the registry, so the garrison is full of runaways the empire caught. Garrison and raiders trade at night through a sea cave that nobody officially knows about.
name: Fort That Quells the Sea
summary: The Great Jing's forward naval fort on a northern reef, from which its punitive fleets sail. Raiders have burned it three times, and it was rebuilt larger each time.
truth: The quartermaster sells patrol schedules to the raiders, and the admiral lets him. Every raid justifies a bigger fleet.

lore: Whoever holds the chains holds the cheapest road between the inner sea and the Myriad Sands Continent's outer coast. Four powers have raised them in the last thousand years. Today the [[Eternal Night Palace]] holds the northern windlass forts and a consortium backed by the [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] holds the southern ones, and ships pay both. Currents in the narrows are vicious, and the bottom is a field of wrecks from the last time the two sides tried to cut each other's chains.
name: Locked Gate Strait
summary: The best-guarded strait between any two continents, between the Black Frost Continent and the Myriad Sands Continent. Islets string the narrows, and whoever fortifies them can close it with chain booms.

lore: Wounded raiders soak in the springs at a low-grade stone a night, and the town's healers sell medicines compounded from the sulfur crust; there is no faster place in the isles to learn field medicine. The captive market opens at dusk: spirit-root children go to island sects, the rest to plantations, and the leftovers to quiet buyers with banquet invitations. Two raider lords have died arguing over the Mid-grade fire vein under the springs.
name: Hot Spring Town
summary: The raiders' harbor town, built around volcanic springs that close a sword wound overnight. Its back streets hold the captive market.

lore: Every island was a mountain sect's peak, and its broken halls turn up talismans, bronze and bones after every storm. Scavenger sects register claims in the [[Marker-Stone Town]] and fight over the rest. The Morning Star Continent's great sects sponsor scavengers as proxies, so a beach brawl here can end as a debt between the [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] and the [[Apricot Grove Valley]]. Mortal sifters work the beaches for coppers a day and the chance of a spirit stone in the sand; the sects recruit the lucky ones.
name: Sand-Sifting Isles
summary: A chain of islands that were once the peaks of the central continent's eastern ranges. Scavenger sects each hold a peak and sift its ruins, its beaches and each other.
truth: The registry keeps two ledgers. Every rich claim in the isles has been sold twice, and the registrars decide which sale is real by who pays last.

lore: The Iron Bridge queen, a Nascent Soul water cultivator who widowed herself, rules by ledger: every prize is logged, every share paid on time, and a captain who cheats is hung by the ankles from a bridge until the tide decides. Children grow up running the chain bridges, and the quick ones become pilots. Mortals here eat well, pay a tenth and never leave. Her nephews are already quarrelling over who inherits the ledger.
name: Iron Bridge Stockade
summary: The pirate queen's realm: three hundred sea stacks linked by iron chain bridges, forty thousand people and one law, which is hers.
truth: She pays the [[Seal Watch]] in information, reporting every ship that drifts toward the buoys, and in return no Watch elder has ever come to clean out the stacks.

lore: Iron Gill warriors cultivate the Water and Slaughter Daos and fight with tridents and teeth; a general's rank is the number of hulls he has opened. They enforce the tolls in all the Sovereign's waters and hunt poachers down in their own ports, sometimes years later. Their chief, a Nascent Soul shark lord, leads the faction that wants war with Floating Peak now. They despise the turtle sages as cowards and the [[Thousand Isles League]] as thieves who have been allowed to live.
name: Iron Gill Host
summary: The shark-folk war host of the Azure Wave Palace: the Sovereign's generals, his toll enforcers and the hands that drag unpaying ships under.
truth: The chief general keeps a spy among the vault guards on the Floating Peaks, and has not told the Sovereign.

lore: Inside a ring of bell buoys lies the [[Heaven's Scar]], and in its middle the [[Ladder Stump]] rises from the water, ringed by forts. Just outside the buoys sits the seat of the [[Seal Watch]]. Everything arrives by ship, because transfer arrays scramble near the Scar. The Watch hires porters, cooks and buoy-tenders at Qi Condensation and pays in merit tokens that buy pills and manuals no market sells; Core Formation elders serve terms for their sects. Since the garrison was doubled, nobody has been granted leave, and the ships home sail half empty.
name: Sea of the Ladder's Root
summary: The black, glass-calm water around the Heaven Ladder's stump: the Scar, the Seal Watch's fortress ring, and the only harbor where orthodox and demonic disciples queue at the same gate.
top: Void Refinement (the Warden; something sealed below is higher)
truth: Elders whose terms have ended are still on the walls. Their sects keep receiving letters in their handwriting, written by the Watch's scribes.

lore: The master is a gentle old scholar who never leaves the reef and never seems to age. The academy teaches the Water Dao, the eighteen tolls of the Shoreless Sea, the etiquette for addressing a jiao, and the sea clans' script. Captains who want to pay toll and survive the conversation hire its graduates. It takes ten students a year, chosen by an essay on the law of the sea.
name: Academy of the Listening Deep
summary: A quiet academy on a reef that teaches water arts, navigation and sea-clan law to island children. Its graduates make the best toll negotiators in the isles.
top: Nascent Soul (the master, a turtle sage in human form)
truth: The master is a turtle sage of the [[Turtle Archive]] in human form, and the academy is how the Sovereign chooses which island lords to buy next.

lore: Folk belief holds that a water ghost is freed when it drowns a living soul to take its place. The Society runs that as a business: its ghosts keep a strict queue, and a captain who pays toll in grave goods at the right buoy is passed by. Unpaid ships lose a sailor a night. Its living members, mostly Ghost Way cultivators, sell protection, broker substitutes from prisons and slave markets and teach the Death Dao. The Court of No Light calls them unregistered.
name: Society of Substitutes
summary: Drowned ghosts who can only move on by drowning someone in their place. They have organized, keep a waiting list and take bribes to pass a ship by.
truth: Substitution frees no one. The drowned soul goes into a court's ledger either way. The founder knows; the queue is simply the most profitable lie on the sea.

lore: The vortex drains into something under the sea floor. Wreckage from it surfaces in the [[Sea of Sunken Valleys]] months later, scoured clean and smelling of lightning. Divers with strong water arts have ridden the current down and come back with Ascent Age bronze; most do not come back. Water Dao cultivators meditate on the outer current lashed to a mast, and some come away with a comprehension.
name: Ship-Swallowing Vortex
summary: A whirlpool forty li across on the belt's western side that has never closed. Ships caught in its outer current circle for days before they go down.
truth: It is the storm wall's intake. Everything it swallows is carried down to cool the drum, and the chamber around the drum is full of ships.

lore: Currents from the whole outer sea meet here, carrying wreckage and the souls of the drowned. The [[Court of No Light]] says every soul that dies within sight of the Long Dusk Continent's shadow is its subject; the [[Azure Wave Palace]] says whatever drowns belongs to the sea. Ghost clerks in paper boats and shark-folk patrols meet on the water and argue jurisdiction over each corpse. The living sail through fast, with coins to throw overboard.
name: Sea of Lost Souls
summary: The grey waters south of Long Dusk where the drowned of six continents drift in on converging currents. The Court of No Light and the Azure Wave Palace both claim them.
truth: The two courts settled the dispute in secret centuries ago and split the souls between them. The arguing on the water is theater to keep human sects out of the trade.

lore: Qi near its crown is richer than any vein in the Shattered Sea, and Core Formation cultivators climb it to break bottlenecks. The daily lightning hunts whoever on the summit has the most cultivation, like a tribulation, and it has killed eleven Nascent Souls. The halls on its crown are sealed with characters no scholar can read. On clear nights the Mirror above it looks close enough to touch.
name: Heaven-Gazing Shard
summary: The highest of the hanging shards, now above the clouds, where the air is too thin for mortals and lightning strikes the summit every day out of a clear sky.
truth: It will touch the world barrier within a century, long before the Floating Peak Continent's peaks. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] keeps a hidden post on its underside to record exactly what happens when it does.

lore: Raiders from these reefs hit Jing salt towns and rice barges and take spirit-root children before the empire's registrars can. The [[Night Banquet Sect]] buys the ones nobody else wants. Jing punitive fleets come every few years, burn whatever stands above the tide line and leave; the raiders are back within the month. The reefs are volcanic and riddled with hot springs where wounded raiders soak.
name: Black Rock Isles
summary: Black basalt reefs a day's sail from the Morning Star Continent's southern coast: the raiders' anchorage for strikes on the Great Jing's shore, and the Jing navy's favorite target.
truth: Jing registrars on the coast sell the raiders lists of villages with untested spirit-root children, and take a share of every sale.

lore: The Tethering Gate disciples cultivate the Wind and Earth Daos for climbing and forge chain from black iron and beast tendon, which makes its smiths decent artifact refiners. Recruitment is a climb: any child who reaches the first shard up a chain without help is taken in. The Gate fights a quiet war with sky pirates who cut chains to drop shards on rival claims. Its master wants a chain on the [[Heaven-Gazing Shard]] before the [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] gets one there.
name: Tethering Gate
summary: The scavenger sect that chained the lower shards to anchors on the sea floor. It owns every chain, charges toll to climb them and decides who salvages what.
truth: Its anchor fees are paid in secret by the [[Armillary Pavilion]], which wants the shards held at fixed heights as relay posts for a new Ladder.

lore: The shards float on the same rich qi that holds the [[Floating Peak Continent]]'s peaks aloft, so their qi is the richest in the Shattered Sea and their Ascent Age halls have never been under water. Getting up is the problem: by kite, by crane, or by a chain someone else owns. The [[Tethering Gate]] has tethered the lower shards to anchors on the sea floor and charges toll to climb. Rockfall from the shards sinks a ship a month. The [[Conclave of Nine Clans]] calls the shards lost kin of its own peaks and sends hunters after any bloodline relic found on them.
name: Sea of Hanging Isles
summary: Chunks of the old central continent hanging in the air over the sea, some a few hundred feet up, some above the clouds. A few creep higher every year, and their chains must be lengthened.
truth: The shards that rise are the ones with intact Ascent Age halls. They are not drifting; something on the Mirror's side is pulling them home.

lore: The Hall teaches spirit farming, the Wood Dao and vault-breaking. Seeds sixty-six thousand years old sometimes sprout in its terraced gardens, and one living strain can make an alchemy hall's century. The [[Apricot Grove Valley]] buys first and pays well. Recruits are handed a dead seed; the ones it sprouts for stay. It claims the [[Peak of Sword Graves]] because the sword sect's herb terraces lie under the graves.
name: Hall of Seed-Seekers
summary: A scavenger sect sponsored by the Apricot Grove Valley that digs Ascent Age seed vaults for herbs extinct since the Severance, and replants them.
truth: The Apricot Grove Valley uses the Hall's revived strains to breed the blights it seeds in rival gardens. The Hall's master knows and takes the money.

lore: The Kingdom of Hazy Waters house has reigned nine hundred years by never being worth replacing. Its people pilot, caulk, cook and smuggle for Ten Thousand Sails; a child's first job is diving for coins dropped under the moorings. Spirit-root children are auctioned to island sects at the spring tests, and the crown takes the price. The crown prince wants to stop paying the League and has been meeting the [[Great Jing Dynasty]] envoys about it.
name: Kingdom of Hazy Waters
summary: A mortal kingdom of eighty islands on the approaches to Ten Thousand Sails. Its kings collect harbor dues for the League and are allowed to keep a tenth.
truth: The [[Pavilion of the Rising Tide]] rigs the spring auctions. The crown is paid a fixed fee, and the best children never reach the block.

lore: Night Oar boats are low, black and silent, rowed by Qi Condensation fishermen with hush talismans on the oarlocks. The gang buys from anyone and sells to the best price, and teaches its rowers enough water arts to swim home when the boat goes down. Its boss is a Core Formation former Jing customs officer who knows every patrol on both sides. The fishing towns hate it, because they are the ones that burn when it fails.
name: Night Oar Gang
summary: The poachers of the Toll Line: night rowers who take sea-clan hatchlings from the outer reefs and sell them to alchemists who pay without asking.
truth: Its biggest buyer is the [[Apricot Grove Valley]], through three layers of middlemen. The white jiao at the [[White Scale Barrier]] knows, and is saving the name for when he needs a war.

lore: The Armillary Pavilion's tables list it as a minor herb shard and say nothing of the people. They speak an Ascent Age dialect, farm terraces around a dead transfer array and believe the world outside ended. They trade spirit rice and old manuals for salt and iron, and kill anyone who tries to take their children back through the gate. A Foundation aura cracks its edges, so sects send their best Qi Condensation disciples. The next opening is next spring.
name: Realm of the Left-Behind
summary: A stable rift that opens for twenty days every seven years into a shard world still peopled by descendants of Severance survivors. Only cultivators below Foundation can pass.
truth: They have waited sixty-six thousand years for the array to be repaired, and they still keep its keys. It once linked to the Heaven Ladder.

lore: The fleet was carrying refugees from the burning continents when it sank, and the admiral has kept everyone aboard ever since: sailors still stand watch, children still go to deck school, and the purser still pays wages. Living ships it meets are hailed and asked for papers from a war that ended three thousand years ago. Those who play along can trade for antique spirit stones and Rekindling manuals; those who don't are boarded.
name: Kingdom of Yin Sails
summary: A fleet of four hundred ships drowned in one storm during the Outer Demon War, still sailing in formation under its admiral: a fief of the dead with its own law.
truth: The admiral refuses to register with the Court of No Light. The moment the fleet is registered, its souls belong to the Pale Sovereign, and he promised them they would stay together.

lore: The abbey teaches the Lightning and Wind Daos and a body art that requires being struck: novices begin on the lowest rod with a copper chain round one ankle. It makes the best thunder talisman paper in the world, charged under the storm for a year, and sells sealed jars of storm qi to refiners. It recruits from wrecks: children pulled alive out of the belt are held to be chosen by thunder. It hates the [[Eternal Night Palace]] raiders who steal its jars and blames them for every novice lost.
name: Abbey of Drawn Lightning
summary: A storm-cultivating abbey on a reef of iron lightning rods inside the belt. Its disciples bathe in lightning and sell the storm by the jar.
truth: The rods are draining the drum in the eye. The abbot knows the storm is part of a seal, and has decided the abbey's growth matters more.

lore: Pilot families sound the channels every spring after the winter falls and keep the maps in their heads; writing one down is death under guild law. Pilots read stone the way geomancers read land and can tell which arch will fall within the year. Merchant captains pay them to go through instead of around, which is either a bargain or an ambush. The guild teaches Earth and Water sense to its children and adopts orphans with good ears.
name: Pilots' Guild
summary: The pilots of the stacks, who alone know which channels are open this year. They serve the queen, but they are paid by the voyage, and anyone can hire them.
truth: The guild knows which stacks will fall next, and is waiting for the one above the queen's hall.

lore: Hatchling scale ground fine clears blocked meridians, so alchemists pay well and do not ask. Poachers come at night in small boats with shuttered lanterns. The reef is guarded by hatchling mothers who will chase a boat into a harbor, and by Iron Gill patrols who will chase it into a city. Fishermen inside the line hear the mothers singing in spring and keep their children indoors.
name: Reef of Young Scales
summary: The spawning reefs just outside the Toll Line where sea-clan young hatch each spring. Their scales fetch ten times any fish, and taking them is death.

lore: It happened three hundred years ago. Forty ships still lie in the fingers with their holds full of caged cubs that drowned. Salvagers come for the cores in the wrecks; sometimes the Court leaves a sentinel in the palm, and sometimes it doesn't. Raiders sail past it bareheaded. A Fist Dao cultivator who meditates inside the print can feel the shape of the blow.
name: Ape's Palm Reef
summary: A reef in the shape of a giant handprint, left when the Beast Court's White Ape King struck the sea and sank a whole raiding fleet with one blow.

lore: The Sea-Taming Sect teaches taming by blood contract and the Wood and Water arts that keep a bonded beast healthy. Its serpents tow the fastest ships in the isles, and its gulls carry letters to [[Ten Thousand Sails]] in a day. Every apprentice is handed a cub and told their rank depends on what it grows into. The Beast Court calls the sect slavers and has posted a price: one tamer's core for every beast they free.
name: Sea-Taming Sect
summary: Beast tamers who raise sea serpents, war crabs and storm gulls in a lagoon, and buy the raiders' cubs to break them.

lore: Ransoms are posted on boards by realm: a Qi Condensation disciple of a known sect is a hundred low-grade stones, a Foundation elder one mid-grade, a Core Formation elder whatever the sect can bear. Captives not ransomed by the new moon go to the second board. Fences appraise everything low on purpose. Agents of the [[Night Banquet Sect]] keep a permanent table beside the second board.
name: Ledger Harbor
summary: The haven's market harbor, where the queen's clerks divide plunder, fences buy anything, and captives are ransomed at posted prices.

lore: The City of Pearl Light's streets are terraces in the trench wall, and its light comes from pearls the shark-folk weep and set in the stone. Its market sells dragon silk that sheds water, coral and kelp pills, and air pearls that let a human breathe for a month. Spirit kelp farms line the upper terraces. A human visitor must be sponsored by a sea-clan household, which answers for every insult. Shark-folk weavers will trade silk for human poetry, the one thing they think humans make well.
name: City of Pearl Light
summary: A shark-folk city cut into the trench wall below the Azure Wave Palace, lit by the pearls in its stones. Humans may enter with an air pearl and a sponsor.
truth: The pearl walls are a ledger. Each pearl was wept for a shark-folk killed by humans, and the generals mean to collect on all of them.

lore: Founded at the Second Sealing, the Seal Watch answers to no sect. Every great power sends elders to serve a term, and refusing is the one thing all the others will punish. Its fortress rings the Ladder Stump, and a second fortress watches the Demon-Sealing Glacier. Seal Watch elders are forbidden to speak of what they see on duty.
name: Seal Watch
summary: The garrison that guards Heaven's Scar and the Frozen Host, staffed by every great power in rotation. The one place where orthodox and demonic stand on the same wall.
truth: The seal is failing faster than the Seal Watch reports. It has doubled its garrison and stopped granting leave.

lore: Some shard worlds are minor worlds caught by Severed Heaven's pull. Many are pieces of the central continent flung out when the Ladder broke. The Armillary Pavilion publishes tables of their openings: one herb-rich shard opens every sixty years and admits only cultivators below Foundation, because a stronger aura would crack its gate.
name: The Shard Worlds
summary: The small thousand worlds that circle Severed Heaven. Their orbits bring them close on fixed cycles, and when they pass near, their gates open as secret realms.
truth: A few shards still hold descendants of Severance survivors, cut off for sixty-six thousand years.

lore: Travelers arriving by array step out above the clouds onto a bronze terrace the size of a town, under a sky so close the Mirror looks near enough to touch.
name: Star Dial
summary: The Armillary Pavilion's observatory on the highest floating peak in the world, and the center of the Heavenly Circuit.

lore: Scavenger sects live on the islands and dive for ruins from the Age of the Ascent in the drowned valleys. Spatial rifts open and close without warning. No great power holds the Shattered Sea; the Seal Watch holds its center, and nobody argues with the Seal Watch.
name: Shattered Sea
summary: Where the central continent stood before the Severance: broken islands, floating shards and storms around the Ladder Stump.
truth: A few of the floating shards are slowly rising toward the Mirror.

lore: The sea around the Ladder Stump is glass-calm and black, and divine sense slides off it. The Seal Watch sinks anything that sails inside the marker buoys.
name: Heaven's Scar
summary: The sealed tear in the world barrier beneath the Ladder Stump. Outer demons have come through it twice.
truth: The seal is the Nameless Sealer. Her cultivation has held Heaven's Scar shut for 3,127 years, and the rising tide is pulling it open faster than she can mend it.

lore: On clear nights it is visible from the inner coast of every continent, a black line against the Mirror. The Seal Watch's fortress rings its base. The Ladder Stump hums when the Mirror is overhead.
name: The Ladder Stump
summary: What is left of the Heaven Ladder: a pillar as wide as a kingdom, rising from the Shattered Sea and ending in broken jade above the clouds.
truth: Armillary Pavilion survey teams have climbed it in secret. The top is not broken. It was cut clean.

lore: Island sects cultivate water and storm arts, pirate lords raid every coast, and free ports buy anything without asking where it came from.
name: Thousand Isles
summary: An archipelago in the Shoreless Sea between the Morning Star Continent and the Vast Wilds Continent: closer to ten thousand islands than a thousand, and every one has a lord.
top: Deity Transformation (the Isles League's three island masters)

lore: A body that once held immortal qi never rots. The Gate digs them out of the Fallen Ladder, refines them into puppets that fight at their old realm, and sells them to anyone who pays. The Court of No Light calls this theft of its subjects and is at war with the Gate in all but name. Nobody makes better puppets.
name: Thousand Puppet Gate
summary: Demonic corpse refiners who mine the Fallen Ladder's tombs for immortal bodies and turn them into puppets.
truth: Some of their best puppets are not empty. The Gate's master does not know. The fullest of them holds the soul of a Body Integration immortal from the Age of the Ascent, awake and patient.

lore: From Fallen Star City, the Heavenly Scale Pavilion runs branches in every great city on every continent. Its one law is written over every door: no blood on the scale. Fight inside a hall of the Heavenly Scale Pavilion and every branch in the world will refuse you, forever. It lends to empires, bankrolls both sides of most wars, and sets the price of a Foundation Pill for the whole world each spring.
name: Heavenly Scale Pavilion
summary: The merchant house of the whole world. It runs the great auctions, changes spirit stones between grades and enforces contracts with karmic oaths.
top: Body Integration (the Founding Scale, never seen)
truth: The Heavenly Scale Pavilion holds the debts of four great powers. If it called them in at once, two would fall. Every karmic oath the Pavilion writes is sworn to the Founding Scale, a Body Integration merchant no living client has met. Two of its Scale-Keepers are at Void Refinement.

lore: Most people think the Void Choir is a story to frighten disciples. Its members hide in every sect and every city. Their sign is a cultivator humming a tune nobody taught them.
name: Void Choir
summary: A secret cult that hears the outer demons singing through the seal and wants to let them in.
truth: Some of its leaders are possessed by outer demons who slipped out during the war. They are patient.

lore: Great thousand worlds hang in the Void Sea like suns, each with a crowd of middle thousand worlds circling it, and each of those with its own swarm of small worlds. Nothing lives in the void that a sane cultivator wants to meet.
name: The Void Sea
summary: The endless dark between worlds. Worlds drift in it like islands, and the great ones' gravity gathers the smaller around them.
truth: Outer demons are the Void Sea's native life. They feed on worlds' qi and are drawn to anything that pierces a world barrier.

lore: Anything can be bought in Ten Thousand Sails, including people, and anything can be sold, including your name.
name: Ten Thousand Sails
summary: The free port of the Thousand Isles: no laws, no questions, and ten thousand sails in the harbor. A hub of the Heavenly Circuit.

lore:
Scholars call the world Severed Heaven, after the day its ladder to the Upper Realm broke. Maps carved before the break call it Tongtian, Heaven-Reaching. Most mortals never learn either name; to them it is simply all under heaven.

Six continents ring the Shattered Sea, where the Ladder Stump still rises from the water. Past them lies the Shoreless Sea, then the Rim, where the ocean pours over the world's edge into the void.

It is year 3,127 of the Sealed Era. Qi is the richest in sixty-six thousand years and still rising. Sects crowd every spirit vein, geniuses are born every generation, and everyone races to climb before the tide turns.
name: Severed Heaven
notes:
Scale: kingdom 5,000-15,000 li across; region 40,000-80,000 li; continent 200,000-300,000 li; world about 1,000,000 li (1 li = 0.5 km).
Travel per day: mortal 60 li, Qi Condensation 150, Foundation 1,000, Core Formation 2,000, Nascent Soul 8,000, Deity Transformation 50,000 and up.
How common each realm is: Deity Transformation, dozens per continent (every great power has several); Void Refinement, a few per continent, kept in seclusion as ancestors; Body Integration, about twenty in the world; Mahayana, fewer than ten, mostly hidden pillars behind great powers; Tribulation Transcendence, a handful, hiding from their last tribulation or waiting to ascend.
summary: A prosperous middle thousand world: a flat disc of land and sea about a million li across, drifting in the Void Sea around the great world mortals call the Mirror.
truth: The tide will peak in about two thousand years. The same pull that floods the world with qi is stretching the seal over Heaven's Scar, and the Seal Watch knows it is failing faster than it admits. A handful of Tribulation Transcenders are alive. Most hide from their last tribulation or wait for the tide's peak to ascend; the Nameless Sealer is bound inside the seal.

lore: Its name comes from the old saying that life has a shore and knowledge has none. Beyond the continents the water deepens into trenches no human has sounded, and the sea clans' cities glow at the bottom.
name: Shoreless Sea
summary: The outer ocean around the six continents. Sea clan territory: ships pay toll or vanish.
top: Body Integration (the Sea Sovereign, one pearl short of a true dragon)

lore: Apricot Grove Valley's founder healed the poor for free and asked only that each patient plant an apricot tree. The valley is now a forest of a million trees around the richest herb gardens on the continent. They heal all sides for a price, sell pills to empires and demonic sects alike, and their Alchemy Hall heads are courted like princes.
name: Apricot Grove Valley
summary: The greatest alchemy and medicine sect on the Morning Star Continent. Everyone needs them, so nobody touches them.

ties.why: The Butchers are our steadiest source of beast cores, and we pay them enough to keep it that way.

truth: Apricot Grove Valley keeps its grip on the herb trade by quietly seeding blight in rival gardens. The Valley Master calls it hygiene. The Valley Master is a Void Refinement alchemist who has outlived three dynasties by keeping all of them in his debt.

lore: Built on stilts over warm ground, the town has more herb sellers than houses. The great auction is held at first dawn, when the polar night ends and the year's herbs are cured, and its prices are quoted at the Frost Fair for the rest of the year. Appraisers grade herbs by age for a fee. Faking an herb's age is a hanging offense under market law, enforced by Cold Flame Valley's disciples. Alchemists rent furnace rooms by the day.
name: Hundred Herb Market
summary: The basin's market town, where Palace buyers, tribe traders and Frost Fair merchants bid for fire-and-ice herbs at the first-dawn auction.

lore: A body cultivator's bones outlast stone; a chief's thighbone can be used as a hammer. The tribes lay their dead here and never come back for them. Dawnless City refiners pay a mid-grade spirit stone for a Foundation body cultivator's skeleton, and bone thieves come every winter. A tribe that catches one breaks every bone in his body and leaves him here alive. The Eagle-Master tribe keeps watch from the cliffs, for a fee.
name: White Bone Flats
summary: The sky-burial ground of the Iron Bone Tribes, where the dead are left for eagles and wolves. The bones of a hundred generations of body cultivators whiten the flats.
truth: On still nights the bones shift a little toward Ancestor Mountain. The Bone Ancestor is drawing what is left of his descendants back to him.

lore: Inside the White Blind the wind never drops below a gale and you cannot see your own hand. Divine sense frays in it like rope. Caravans that cut through it between the Spine and the fortress lose a third of their animals; Qi Condensation cultivators who lose the rope freeze within a day. Ice Dao cultivators who survive a month inside come out with a cold in their meridians that never leaves, and sometimes with a breakthrough.
name: The White Blind
summary: A stretch of ice sheet west of the glacier where the blizzard never stops. The tribes say this is where the demons' bad dreams come out.

lore: The Lin dynasty rules by one rule: keep the walls white and the tribute ready. Every adult serves a month a year on the walls, and children learn the bell signals before their letters. The royal guard has a dozen Foundation cultivators trained by the North Wind Sword Gate. The kingdom ships ivory and furs through Stone Ship Harbor and imports the grain it cannot grow. Its treasury is empty: the last tribute was paid with a [[Heavenly Scale Pavilion]] loan, and the loan falls due the same winter the next Great Khan is expected.
name: Kingdom of White Walls
summary: The largest coastal kingdom, behind three rings of whitewashed walls. It has paid tribute to every Great Khan for three hundred years and is proud never to have fallen.
truth: Sea-Crossing Temple has quietly bought the loan. If the kingdom defaults, the monks own the walls.

lore: The camp sits in the open on the northern steppe for the whole polar night. Entrance is the Blizzard Run: a night walking naked in the storm, and whoever stops, dies. Those who finish are fed, beaten, and taught to break stone with their fists and take a sword cut on the forearm. The teachers rode with the last Great Khan; they despise qi cultivators and teach them twice as hard. A student who reaches Foundation Establishment in body gets a tribe name and a place in the next raid.
name: Blizzard Camp
summary: The Iron Bone Tribes' winter school of the Fist Dao, open to outsiders who survive the entrance. Most foreigners leave with broken hands; a few leave unbreakable.
truth: The camp's master is training a hundred outsiders, not tribesmen, as the Snow Wolf claimant's personal guard. He thinks a khan's guard should owe nothing to any tribe.

lore: The Bear King walks among humans as a huge, silent man in a sealskin coat and buys salt and honey at the Floe Market. His court is a dozen Core Formation bears and several hundred lesser ones. They hold the pack ice and the shore cliffs, hunt anyone who takes their cubs and leave alone those who leave them alone. Beast tamers prize white bear cubs above any mount on the continent. The Seal Tribe blames the bears for its missing hunters, and the Bear King has let it.
name: Court of the Northern Bears
summary: The white bears of the pack ice, ruled by a Nascent Soul bear king who has taken human form. They hunt seals, walrus and humans with equal interest.
truth: The Bear King knows what is taking the hunters, because it has taken bears too. He is afraid of it, and he has never been afraid of anything.

lore: In most winters the strait is open water and drifting floes. In a hard one the ice runs from this headland toward the Myriad Sands Continent's northern cliffs, a crossing only cultivators and spirit-beast riders survive. The last Great Khan's vanguard crossed here, and few came back. The fort is held by whichever kingdom paid the North Wind Sword Gate most recently, and the shrine is the temple's. Ice guides gather at the first freeze and sell their services by the day.
name: Ice Bridgehead
summary: The headland where, in the hardest winters, the sea ice reaches across the strait toward the Myriad Sands Continent. A fort and a shrine mark where raiders set out and refugees come home.

lore: Ice-Fisher camps move out onto the frozen bay at the first freeze and come ashore at the thaw. Their children learn to read ice by its color and its sound before they learn to swim, because swimming will not save them. They hunt seals at breathing holes and fish through the ice on lines a li long. The Iron Bone tribes despise them as fish-eaters and need them as guides. Their elders charge a low-grade spirit stone a day to guide a caravan across the ice.
name: Ice-Fisher Tribe
summary: Seal hunters and ice fishers who winter on the bay's western ice. They know where the sea ice is thin, and every caravan and every raid needs them.
truth: The last Great Khan died on the sea ice because an Ice-Fisher guide led his army onto a current lead. The tribe has never admitted it, and the Snow Wolf chief has started asking.

lore: Inside, the sun hangs at noon and never moves: a grass world full of sunfire grass, golden locust swarms and herds of fire-maned horses. The tribes send their youths in as a rite, and a youth who comes back with a sunfire horse is made a rider on the spot. Alchemists pay a low-grade spirit stone a stalk for sunfire grass, which keeps meridians warm through the polar night. A Foundation aura cracks the gate, and whoever is inside when it cracks stays until the next opening.
name: Realm of the Unsetting Sun
summary: A shard world that passes closest at midsummer every seven years and opens as a ring of light on the steppe for twelve days. Only cultivators below Foundation Establishment can enter.
truth: Time runs slower inside. The few who have been shut in through a closing came out seven years later having lived a single day.

lore: The Mu family moved into the Broken Tower two centuries ago, broke the guardian puppets that still walked its halls and found the lower floors full of formation plates. They sell plates, puppet parts and appraised relics through agents at the Frost Fair, and their tower is the only warm, walled place in the waste, so scavenger crews winter there and pay for it. Four Foundation cultivators and a hundred guards keep the tenth collected. Mu children learn appraisal before letters, and the family's young appraisers are the best on the continent.
name: Fief of the Broken Tower
summary: A cultivator family's fief inside a half-buried Ascent Age tower. The Mu family claims salvage rights on every ruin within three thousand li and takes a tenth.
truth: The Mu salvage decree is a forgery. The Palace knows, and lets it stand because the Mu send their best finds to the Night Sovereign every year.

lore: Forty years ago the lord was mauled by a white bear on the ice and carried home for dead. He recovered, lit the Long Lamp, and since then nobody in his fief has frozen or starved. His people are healthy, his granaries full, and he takes in anyone who reaches his gate. He rarely leaves his tower and has not visibly aged. His people hum a harvest song at work that nobody remembers learning. Seal Watch patrols have stopped there twice and reported nothing unusual.
name: Keep of the Long Lamp
summary: A small, prosperous frost fief whose lord keeps a great lamp burning on his tower through the whole polar night. Travelers lost on the ice steer for it.
truth: The lord died on the ice. The outer demon that escaped the Palace wears him now, feeds on travelers who steer for the lamp and keeps its own villagers fat and warm. The song is the Frozen Host's.

lore: When the great midwinter ebb pulls the fjord down, a stone arch rises from the water with a drowned island behind it: tide pools full of spirit pearls, crab-folk who fight with stolen harpoons and a shrine nobody has opened. A Foundation aura cracks the arch. The Whale Tooth kings sell passage to young cultivators for twenty low-grade spirit stones. The sea clans consider the island theirs and sometimes wait inside.
name: Midwinter Tide Realm
summary: A gate under a western fjord that rises above the water only at the lowest tide of midwinter, every third year, for three days. Only Qi Condensation cultivators can pass.

lore: The outer city has been picked over for centuries: tunnels through ice-choked streets, empty shops, a frozen guardian puppet that still twitches. The inner city is another matter. Its walls still run their formations, and anything that crosses them without the right token is cut apart by ice blades that form out of the air. Crews pay for maps, for tokens taken off earlier crews' bodies and for appraisers who can tell a working formation plate from a dead one. Thousand Puppet Gate buyers wait at the edge to buy whole puppets.
name: Slumbering City
summary: An Ascent Age city frozen whole into the permafrost. Its outer streets are tunnels that scavengers work; its inner city still runs its formations and kills.
truth: At the center, behind the last ward, an Ascent Age master sits frozen in meditation. He chose to sleep through the Ebb, and the rising tide is thawing him.

lore: The Lan family has ruled the Red Spring valleys for four hundred years by paying the Palace's blood tithe on time: a hundred youths every Long Night, drawn by lottery in the village squares. Families hide children with spirit roots in the steam caves, because the Palace takes the gifted first. The springs feed barley, black goats and the only orchards north of the strait. No child of a noble house has been drawn for nine years running, and the villages have begun to count.
name: Red Spring Fief
summary: Warm valleys on the south side of the ranges where red iron springs keep barley growing through the polar night. Its mortal lords pay the Eternal Night Palace in children.
truth: The lottery is rigged, and the Lan heir hates it. He has been smuggling hidden children south to the [[Sea-Crossing Temple]], and the Palace will notice the missing count by spring.

lore: The Gao kings have built ships for three hundred years, and their yards are the only ones north of the strait that can lay a keel for an ocean hull. The present king married a Floating Peak clanswoman born without her clan's bloodline and sent down from the floating peaks to serve; she is cleverer than he is, and the court knows it. Children grow up in the yards and timber camps. Those with spirit roots are sent to the Thunder-Feather Lodge for testing, and those who pass are never seen in the kingdom again.
name: Kingdom of Ship Timber
summary: A mortal coastal kingdom that cuts black pine masts and builds ships for the Floating Peak Continent and the Shattered Sea's scavenger sects. Its queen was born into one of the Floating Peak Continent's clans.

lore: Children here grow up barefoot in warm mud in the middle of the polar night, which no other child on the continent can say. Nine farm elders rule by harvest weight: the families who bring in the most herbs sit highest. They pay the Palace in herbs, the Musk Ox Tribe in grain and the Seal Watch in labor, and marry daughters into the tribes for grazing peace. A child who can tell a ten-year snow ginseng from a hundred-year one by smell is apprenticed to Cold Flame Valley, and the family's tithe is forgiven for a year.
name: Kingdom of Spring Gardens
summary: A mortal farming kingdom in the basin's warm south, ruled by a council of farm elders. It grows the only fresh greens on the continent and pays tithes to three masters.

lore: The Cornerstone Gang runs the Fair's smuggling, pickpockets and protection, and it helps rebuild the Fair every winter, which is where it got its name. Its real trade is the ice burial: a body set in the foundations as the water freezes, found in spring when nobody can say when it died. It is mortals and Qi Condensation cultivators with a few Foundation enforcers, and it recruits orphans off the docks. It pays the Palace's tax collectors more than the honest merchants do, and they leave it alone.
name: Cornerstone Gang
summary: A Frost Fair gang of smugglers and ice-burial killers. Pay them, and your problem ends up frozen into a foundation.
truth: Its boss failed the Palace's Ash Gate thirty years ago and swore to bury a Palace elder in the ice before he dies. He has finally found a client who will pay for it.

lore: The spring boils from below with a slow heartbeat, and its steam carries so much fire qi that a Qi Condensation cultivator who sits in it for a month can break through, if he survives the heat. The Palace, the Iron Bone tribes and Cold Flame Valley each hold a third of its shore under an agreement made sixty years ago, after a battle that boiled forty men alive. Fire Dao cultivators pay a low-grade spirit stone a day to sit at the edge. The water has dropped three feet this year.
name: Earth's Eye Spring
summary: A boiling spring a li across in the middle of the basin, over a mid-grade fire spirit vein. Three powers share it under an arrangement none of them likes.

lore: Every thaw uncovers something: a spearhead that still hums, a talisman case, a defender frozen with his hands up.
