Outer demons left no bodies, only black glass where they died, and Frost Fair appraisers pay well for glass and gear alike. The Left-Behind fief claims a tenth of every find and enforces it. Demon glass gives off a cold that keeps meat for a year, and a smell that draws ice wolves from fifty li.
name: Field of Broken Spears
summary: The Outer Demon War battlefield south of the glacier, where the northern line held for eleven years. Broken artifacts and frozen defenders still lie under the snow.
truth: Some of the black glass is not dead. It warms in the hand when someone nearby hums.

lore: The fjord's mouth is so narrow that one chain can close it, and the Sheer Cliff lords have lived behind that chain for four centuries, raiding everyone else's boats. They light false beacons on the outer cliffs to draw ships onto the rocks and keep whatever washes ashore. Their warriors climb sheer ice with hand-claws, and their children start by robbing gull nests. They hate the Whale Tooth kings and would love to watch the sea clans finish them.
name: Kingdom of the Sheer Cliffs
summary: A cliff-walled fjord kingdom of wreckers and pirates who prey on the Whale Tooth fleet and sell captives at Chain-Gate Harbor.
truth: Their queen has sent an envoy to the Cold Jiao Mansion offering to guide its hunters into the Whale Tooth fjord.

lore: Forty monks and a Nascent Soul abbot crossed from Myriad Sands two centuries ago and built a hospital before they built a hall. They teach medicine, the vajra body and patience. They will not kill, but they have broken the arms of three Palace slavers who came for their orphans. They ransom captives from the tribes with temple money and settle the freed on temple land, and raiders who wake in the temple's beds sometimes stay. The coastal kings love them and owe them, which is how the temple prefers it.
name: Sea-Crossing Temple
summary: The Thousand Lamps Temple's northern mission on the Sand-Gazing Shore. Its monks treat frostbite and raid wounds for anyone, preach to raiders and ransom captives.
truth: The temple has been buying the coastal kingdoms' debts through the Heavenly Scale Pavilion brokers for fifty years. Within a generation it will own the Sand-Gazing Shore without converting a single king.

lore: The ground is moss over hot mud, and new pools open under it every day. Steam leeches the length of an arm drink qi rather than blood, and ember toads spit burning slime. At the heart, where a cold spring rises among the hot ones, frostflame lotus grows thicker than anywhere else in the world. Pickers rope themselves together in lines of five, and a line that comes back with four is considered lucky.
name: Marsh of Boiling Springs
summary: The eastern marsh of the basin, where pools boil up without warning under a skin of moss. Frostflame lotus grows thick at its heart, guarded by ember toads and steam leeches.

lore: The columns are six-sided, packed like a honeycomb and broken off at every height, and in a north wind they sing a chord you feel in your teeth. Wind Dao cultivators sit among them to learn to hear qi move in air, and a few learn to ride the gusts between the pillars. Ice wolf packs den in the gaps. The Snow Wolf tribe takes pups here each spring and loses a rider or two to the mothers every year.
name: Forest of Wind Pillars
summary: A field of basalt columns on the tableland where the wind sings through ten thousand pillars. Wind Dao cultivators come to listen, and ice wolf packs den among the stones.

lore: In winter it is forty empty longhouses under the snow. When the pack ice breaks up in early summer it fills: seal oil, walrus and mammoth ivory, white bear pelts, glacier relics smuggled from the south and sea clan pearls change hands under the midnight sun. A sea clan envoy sits in a tide pool at the end of the pier and takes toll from every boat. Disputes go to the market's three elders: one human, one half-blood and one jiao.
name: Floe Market
summary: A summer trading post on the shore of the Utter North, where whalers, seal hunters, smugglers and sea clan envoys meet while the ice is out.

lore: The Dou family holds the fief by right of having killed the family that held it before, and sells to the Floating Peak Continent's artifact refiners through Harbor of Distant Peaks. Diggers thaw the permafrost with fire and dig out tusks, bones and now and then a whole frozen mammoth with its meat still red. A tusk from an Ascent Age mammoth king can hold a core worth more than the fief. The Giant-Blood tribe calls it grave robbing and has burned the diggings twice. Diggers are paid by the tusk, and most die of the cold or the herds.
name: Fief of Ancient Tusks
summary: A fief of fossil-ivory diggers who mine the permafrost for the tusks of mammoths dead seventy thousand years. Some of the old tusks still hold beast cores.

lore: Seal Tribe hunters can lie still on the ice by a breathing hole for a day and a night, and their children practice by lying still in the snow until a fox comes to sniff them. They trade oil, hides and walrus ivory at the Floe Market and pay the sea clans one seal in ten, left on the ice for the jiao. They fight the white bears for the same seals and lose a hunter or two each winter. In the last forty years they have lost eleven whole parties, each found as an empty camp. The young hunters have started to go armed against men.
name: Seal Tribe
summary: Seal hunters of the ice edge, who follow the pack ice out each winter. Their hunting parties are the ones disappearing.

lore: The Fu merchant kings have ruled for three hundred years by paying protection to the Palace and tribute to whichever khan is strongest, and by never building walls high enough to insult either. Children grow up as dock hands and ice-cutters. A child with a spirit root is sold at the Fair's root market to the highest sect bid, and the family eats well for ten years. The old king is dying, and his two sons have chosen patrons: the elder the Palace, the young Snow Wolf claimant.
name: Petrel Kingdom
summary: A mortal merchant kingdom on the east shore of Glass Bay that owns the Frost Fair's land side: wharves, warehouses and the summer town.
truth: The king is not dying of age. The elder son's Palace patron has been salting his bread with Blood Salt Lake salt, a pinch a day.

lore: When the sun sets for the half-year, the old kingdom's ghosts rise in their frozen capital: a king, his court, his tax collectors. Living settlers rent land from the dead by leaving lamps lit and a drop of blood at each threshold every month; those who refuse wake colder each morning until they do not wake. Children learn never to let a lamp go out. The ghost king judges disputes fairly and remembers everything. Ghost Way cultivators come to bargain for the court's lore, and the [[Court of No Light]] has sent an envoy to enter its dead in the registers.
name: Kingdom of Cold Souls
summary: A ghost fief on the northern barrens. A kingdom froze here in a single night during the Outer Demon War, and its dead still keep court through the polar night and fade in the midnight sun.
truth: The kingdom did not freeze by accident. Its king bargained with an outer demon for a cultivation method and paid with his people's warmth. His court has forgotten the bargain, and the Night Sovereign's envoys have started asking the ghost king to remember it.

lore: The Valley's founder learned to balance fire and ice herbs in one cauldron, and its pills are the only ones on the continent that treat frozen meridians and fire deviation alike. It brews tempering baths for the Iron Bone tribes, salves for the Seal Watch and, quietly, blood pills for the Palace. It recruits farm children with good noses and teaches alchemy, medicine and the Fire and Ice Daos. It wants the Earth's Eye Spring's vein for a new furnace hall, and hates the Palace's herb officers, who take the best roots before the auction.
name: Cold Flame Valley
summary: An alchemy and medicine sect in a steaming side valley of the basin. It makes fire-and-ice pills and the body-tempering baths the tribes buy by the barrel.

lore: Black Pine hunters ride spirit elk through timber too thick for horses and trap sable, lynx and ice marten for the fur trade. They temper their bodies like the steppe tribes but fight with axes, which the steppe tribes find embarrassing. Their children are given a sapling at birth and are buried under it. They tolerate loggers who cut where they say and kill those who do not, and the coastal kingdom's timber camps push further in every year. Their shamans tend the ancient pine and say it dreams in spring.
name: Black Pine Tribe
summary: A forest tribe of trappers and elk riders in the deep taiga. They are Iron Bone in name and nobody's in fact, and they worship the Pine of Ten Thousand Ages.

lore: Fire runs under the ice here. The Burning Spine's vents keep lakes open and passes warm through the polar night, and the Eternal Night Palace holds all but the Hearth Clan's. Its fiefs mine black iron with slaves taken on steppe raids and pay a blood tithe of youths each Long Night. In the first month of darkness anyone may climb to the Palace's Ash Gate; those who survive a season in its outer court become disciples, and the rest go to the mines. Elders buy each other's deaths through the Contract Hall in Dawnless City. Three elders have vanished in ten years, and the Palace has stopped claiming it ate them.
name: Obsidian Ranges
summary: The black volcanic ranges of the west, where lava glows through the polar night and the Eternal Night Palace rules from the heights. Black iron, obsidian, sulfur and slaves flow out of every pass.
top: Body Integration (the Night Sovereign, who never sleeps)
truth: The vanished elders were sent to the thaw works under the glacier. The Night Sovereign lets nobody who has seen a thawed demon come home.

lore: When the gate opens, the aurora pours down into the stone ring like water into a funnel, and anyone below Core Formation can walk into a shard world of blue ice and slow light. Inside are ice spirit veins lying open on the surface, aurora moths whose wing dust makes the finest talisman ink, and the ruins of a town. The Frozen Radiance Observatory announces the date a year ahead, and the Armillary Pavilion's tables agree to the day. The next opening is in two years.
name: Realm of Returning Light
summary: A gate in a ring of standing stones where the aurora touches the ground every nine years at the depth of the polar night. It stays open nine days, and a Core Formation aura cracks it.
truth: The town is still inhabited. Its people descend from Severance survivors, speak an Ascent Age dialect and kill outsiders on sight, because the last visitors took their children.

lore: Hearth Clan children are bathed in vent steam until their skin stops blistering, and their warriors can hold a coal until it goes out. They answer to neither the Palace nor the Iron Bone Tribes and live by guiding both through lava tubes that kill everyone else. They gather ember moss and fire salamander skins for Dawnless City. The Palace has asked twice to lease their three deepest vents, and twice the clan's old mother has refused.
name: Hearth Clan
summary: A mountain clan that lives in lava tubes in the eastern half of the Burning Spine, warm all year, with bodies tempered in volcanic heat.
truth: The Palace wants those vents to pipe fire under the glacier for its thaw works. A third refusal will be answered with an army, and the old mother knows it.

lore: Under the coastal dunes lie forests drowned a hundred thousand years ago, and their resin has turned to amber: honey-gold, sometimes holding insects, sometimes something larger. Array masters pay well for clear amber, which holds a formation for centuries, and the Armillary Pavilion's agents buy the best and set the price. The Shen amber-merchant family rules, with a Foundation cultivator heir who studies formations. Children dig the dunes for pocket money, and a child who finds spirit amber, with qi trapped inside, can clear a family's debts.
name: Amber Kingdom
summary: A small coastal kingdom that digs amber from buried ancient forests. The Floating Peak Continent's array masters buy it, because clear amber holds a formation better than jade.

lore: During the polar night the aurora hangs so low over these flats that it hums, and Ice Dao cultivators sit at the [[Forest of Frost Steles]] for weeks waiting for insight; some freeze where they sit. Wherever the ground heaves, Ascent Age walls and towers break through the permafrost, and scavenger crews from the Frost Fair camp here every summer and fight each other for the best ground. The richest is the Slumbering City, whose inner wards still kill Core Formation cultivators. Reindeer herders follow the lights and treat the scavengers like weather. The Eternal Night Palace claims the waste and enforces the claim about once a decade, brutally.
name: Aurora Waste
summary: The northwestern barrens between the Obsidian Ranges and the Rim coast, where the aurora hangs lowest and Ascent Age ruins break through the permafrost. Ice Dao cultivators come to watch the sky.
truth: The aurora is the world barrier glowing where it is thinnest, close to the Rim. It has doubled in brightness in a century as the tide stretches the barrier, and the steles have started to answer it.

lore: Inside the Silent Plain your footsteps make no sound and your shout does not reach your own ears. Hunters have always gone around it, though the trail around takes ten days longer. In the last forty years parties that went around have vanished too, and tracks have been found leading into the plain from both sides and none coming out. The seal hunters say something lives in the silence. The Seal Watch marked it forbidden after its second patrol.
name: Silent Plain
summary: A plain in the south of the Utter North where the wind stops and sound dies. People who cross it alone do not arrive, and lately neither do groups.
truth: It is where the escaped demon first fed. It eats voices first, so its prey cannot call for help, and it can speak in every voice it has eaten.

lore: The Hu dynasty won its crown with harpoons and keeps it the same way: the king throws the first iron of the spring hunt, and a king who misses is replaced by whoever does not. Children with spirit roots become harpooners, whose thrown iron can pierce a whale's skull. Oil, bone and ambergris go out through the Frost Fair and pay for grain. This winter one of their ships killed an ice jiao calf, and the Cold Jiao Mansion has demanded the captain, his family and the king's eldest son. The king has offered spirit stones instead.
name: Kingdom of the Whale Tooth
summary: A whaling kingdom in the largest fjord, ruled by harpooner kings. Its whale oil lights the polar night on half the continent.

lore: When the Ember Shard swings close, the volcano's throat fills with red light. Anyone below Core Formation can walk in; a Core aura cracks the gate and burns whoever wore it. Inside are black glass plains, fire spirit stones lying loose, salamanders the size of oxen and, in deep pockets, seeds of earth fire that refiners would kill for. The Palace auctions entry tokens in Dawnless City. The next opening is in four years, and tokens already sell for a mid-grade spirit stone.
name: Ember Realm
summary: The gate of a shard world of cooling lava, opening in the throat of a dead volcano every twelve years for thirty days. Only cultivators below Core Formation can pass.
truth: The shard is a piece of the central continent's old foundries, thrown out in the Severance. Somewhere inside is a forge that still remembers how the Ladder's jade was made.

lore: The Fair has moved south for as long as anyone remembers, and its old sites stay where they were: rings of piling, rotted platforms and sunken stalls, all locked in ice that never fully thaws. Spring scavengers find lost goods, spirit stones dropped through the cracks and, every year, at least one body frozen upright in a foundation. Ice-Fisher children dare each other to sleep there. The truce council investigates each body and has never named a killer.
name: The Old Fairs
summary: A line of abandoned Frost Fair foundations stretching up the bay, each frozen where it was left. Scavengers pick them over every spring and find someone frozen in the ice.
truth: The bodies are the Cornerstone Gang's work, paid for by whoever wants someone gone. The council knows, because two of its members are clients.

lore: Giant-Blood children look human until about fifteen, when the blood wakes in a month-long fever. Those who live grow a head taller every year until they stop at ten or twelve feet, with bones like iron and tempers to match. Most of the continent calls them half-beasts. The Iron Bone tribes call them cousins and want them as champions, and the Mammoth Tribe's chief has offered marriages. The elders refuse every alliance: they go where the herds go. Their young, who want glory, have started slipping away to the claimants' camps.
name: Giant-Blood Tribe
summary: A tribe of giant-blooded half-bloods who live with the mammoth herds. Grown, they stand twelve feet tall; one in five does not survive the fever that wakes the blood.

lore: The kingdom refused tribute, and the Khan made an example of it: walls broken, every adult killed, children taken north. Sixty years on the hills still weep at night, and the resentment has curdled into ghosts strong enough to kill a Foundation cultivator in the seventh month. Ghost Way cultivators from Long Dusk come to harvest them, monks from Sea-Crossing Temple come to release them, and the two have fought here twice. The old royal vault is still somewhere under the ash.
name: Weeping Hills
summary: The ruins of a coastal kingdom burned by the last Great Khan sixty years ago. Its dead have not left, and in Ghost Month they walk the walls.
truth: Some of the children taken north are grandparents in the Snow Wolf tribe now. The ghosts know their own blood when they see it, and do not touch it.

lore: The herds migrate in a great circle around the tableland and down to the Warm Basin's edge, and the matriarchs choose the route. The Gray Matriarch took human form sixty years ago to bargain with the last Great Khan; he got his mammoths for the ride south, most of them never came back, and she has not forgiven the tribes. Anyone who harms a calf is trampled. Anyone who returns a stolen one is owed a favor. Her herds would decide any war on the continent, and both claimants know it.
name: Clan of the Old Mammoths
summary: The awakened mammoths of the tableland, led by the Gray Matriarch, a Nascent Soul mammoth who has taken human form only once in living memory.

lore: A Nascent Soul elder of the thunder clan runs the lodge with twenty clan members and two hundred hired guards. It buys amber, ivory and mammoth calves, lends to the coastal kingdoms at kind rates, and tests local children for traces of old bloodlines; any who show one are shipped to the Floating Peak Continent. Its walls have been rebuilt three times in ten years, each time thicker. The Black Pine Tribe says the lodge is cutting a road into the forest toward the Pine of Ten Thousand Ages.
name: Thunder-Feather Lodge
summary: The trading lodge of a branch of the Floating Peak Continent's thunder-blooded clan, on the hill above Harbor of Distant Peaks. It buys, lends and tests local children for bloodlines.
truth: The clan wants the tableland's Ascent Age mammoth-king cores to refresh its thinning bloodline, and is buying the Fief of Ancient Tusks' debts to get them. The road is for the Pine's heartwood.

lore: The Cold Jiao Lord is a Nascent Soul flood dragon of the cold seas, sworn to the Sea Sovereign of the [[Azure Wave Palace]], ruling from a palace of ice beneath the outer fjords. Every ship that sails past the fjord mouths pays a tenth of its catch or a tenth of its crew. The jiao leave alone humans who pay and hunt to the last cousin those who kill their young. This winter a Whale Tooth ship killed one of the Lord's grandchildren, and the Lord has given the Whale Tooth king until the first dawn to hand over the captain's line.
name: Cold Jiao Mansion
summary: The sea clans' northern court, a lodge of ice jiao under the outer fjords that collects the Azure Wave Palace's tolls along the Black Frost Continent's western and northern coasts.
truth: The Lord failed a dragon tribulation two centuries ago and is hoarding cold for a second try. He covets the glacier more than any toll.

lore: A hot spring feeds the east half and a glacier stream the west, and they meet along a line as straight as a ruler that has not shifted in recorded history. Sitting on the line is said to give insight into the Fire and Ice Daos at once; most who try are scalded on one side and frostbitten on the other. Cold Flame Valley disciples sit there as their final trial. A Nascent Soul cultivator once tried to push the line with his qi, and the lake drowned him.
name: Lake of the Two Forms
summary: A lake divided down the middle: one half boils, the other is frozen solid, and the line between them never moves. Fire and Ice cultivators both come to sit on the line.
truth: The line is a formation. An Ascent Age alchemist built the lake as a cauldron, and the lid is still down there.

lore: Slaves, black iron, blood pills and whale oil go out; grain, salt, spirit stones and prisoners come in. The Palace's harbor master is a Core Formation elder who settles disputes by drowning the loser. The sea clans keep a tide-house on the quay where captains pay toll before sailing into the Shoreless Sea, and it is the one building in the harbor Palace disciples will not enter. Sailors, guards and dock hands are hired on the quay every morning, and some of them are sold there by evening.
name: Chain-Gate Harbor
summary: The Eternal Night Palace's ice-free port on the western fjords. A black iron chain across the fjord mouth decides who sails in and who leaves.

lore: The tower is older than the Severance, built of a gray stone that frost does not crack, and its beacon formation still holds a faint charge. Texts in the Broken Tower's library call it a Rim watch: the ancients kept a garrison here to watch the world's edge, though no text says for what. Scavengers have stripped everything that could be carried. On the nights the beacon flickers, the seal hunters will not camp below it.
name: Cliff Over the Ruin
summary: The northernmost cliff of the Utter North, where an Ascent Age beacon tower faces the Rim. On some nights its dead formations flicker on their own.
truth: Outer demons climb the Rim here. The Frozen Host's scouts came up this way during the war, and the beacon flickers whenever something is climbing now.

lore: Meltwater runs over a crust of cooling lava as thin as a door, and where it boils away frostflame lotus blooms: a fire-and-ice herb that treats qi deviation up to Core Formation. One bloom fetches two mid-grade spirit stones in Dawnless City. The crust breaks under weight it held the day before, and the Palace's herb officers take half of whatever comes out alive. Experienced pickers cross on their bellies, alone.
name: Flowing Fire Flats
summary: A lava field on the north flank of the Spine where glacier meltwater pours over living rock. Frostflame lotus grows on the steam line, and the crust breaks without warning.

lore: The [[Frost Fair]] is where tribes, Palace disciples and southern merchants trade under a truce nobody trusts, and its transfer array is the continent's only fast road south. The Eternal Night Palace taxes every stall. In summer the bay thaws, the merchants retreat to the Petrel Kingdom's wharves and ships sail for the Shattered Sea. Each winter the sea ice reaches further out than the year before, and the Fair moves to stay at its edge. Ice-cutters, porters and guards are hired by the thousand in the first week of the freeze. A seat on the truce council has stood empty since its holder was found in the ice.
name: Glass Bay
summary: A long sound on the southern coast where the Frostmilk River meets the Shattered Sea. Each winter it freezes clear as glass, and the Frost Fair is rebuilt on the ice.
truth: The ice spreads further each winter because the glacier's cold is spreading. Within thirty years the Fair will stand on ocean ice half the year, and the Snow Wolves will be able to reach it in a night's ride.

lore: It is named for the autumn crossing, when spirit elk swim it by the hundred thousand and their calls carry for days. The Black Pine Tribe hunts the crossing, and so do wolves and taiga tigers. In summer rafts of black pine logs a li long float down to the coast yards. It freezes for seven months, and its ice road is the tableland's way to the sea.
name: Deer Call River
summary: The eastern river, running from the Tusk Ridge down off the Mammoth Tableland and through the taiga to the eastern strait. Timber floats down it in summer, and elk herds cross it in autumn.

lore: Their grandfathers rode in with the Great Khan before last, liked the valley and stayed. They still cultivate the body and fight bare-handed, but they live in stone houses, grow barley and sell horses to the coastal kingdoms, and their children learn to plow as well as to ride. The coastal kings call them barbarians and hire them as mercenaries; the steppe tribes call them soft and want them as a gate. When the next Great Khan rides, they will be the first asked to join and the first burned for refusing. Their khan has not decided.
name: Khanate of the Dismounted
summary: A tribe that conquered a coastal valley three generations ago and settled down to farm and trade. The tribes call them the Dismounted, and they took the insult as their name.

lore: Whales, jiao and stranger things swim into this fjord when their time comes, and their bones pile up in the cold water: ribs like temple beams, skulls the size of houses and, in the deepest heap, Ascent Age leviathans with their cores still inside. Bone refiners would give a fortune for one rib. The sea clans post guards at the mouth, and boats that cross the line are dragged under. The Cold Jiao Lord does not negotiate about the dead.
name: Bone-Burial Fjord
summary: A fjord where old sea beasts come to die, its floor heaped with leviathan bones. The sea clans hold it sacred and drown anyone who enters.

lore: Mammoth Tribe children are put on a mammoth's back before they can walk and learn to sleep there through a blizzard. The tribe holds the best winter grazing on the steppe and forty thousand head of mammoth, and its chief lifted three ancestor stones at once at the last gathering. She means to become Great Khan by persuasion: grazing rights for every tribe that joins her, and a ride south only when the herds are fat. Her riders call the Snow Wolf claimant a dog who listens to dreams.
name: Woolly Mammoth Tribe
summary: The largest of the Iron Bone tribes, who ride and herd woolly mammoths on the northern steppe. Their chief, a giant-blooded woman, is one of the two claimants to Great Khan.
truth: She is losing. Two of her own sub-chiefs have taken Snow Wolf gold, and the Old Mammoth clan has stopped sending calves to her herds.

lore: The tribes call it the Dreaming Ice because their shamans say the demons inside the [[Demon-Sealing Glacier]] dream, and that the dreams come out as blizzards. The Seal Watch fortress of the [[Ice-Guard Fortress]] holds the glacier's southern edge and kills anyone found on the ice without a pass. Scavengers come anyway, for war relics in the old battlefield and in the rubble the glacier pushes out at its snout. The Watch hires porters and wall-builders at three times steppe wages and lets none leave early, and a Core Formation outsider who serves a season on the wall earns a Watch token every great power honors.
name: Dreaming Ice
summary: The ice sheet of the far north around the Demon-Sealing Glacier, where an outer demon army stands frozen mid-charge and the Seal Watch keeps its northern fortress. The ice creeps south every year.
truth: The glacier began creeping faster forty years ago, the year the first thawed demon escaped. The Watch's geomancers have measured it, and the Warden has sealed their report.

lore: A Morning Star sword cultivator came north for the steles three centuries ago and never left; the Observatory she founded keeps sixty disciples, teaches the Ice Dao and aurora divination, and recruits only those who can sit a full night at the steles without moving. Its readings predict storms, secret realm openings and, its elders claim, deaths. It rents the best stele seats for fifty low-grade spirit stones a week. It hates the Palace, which raids it once a generation, wants the Broken Tower's library, and resents the Armillary Pavilion, which calls its readings guesswork and copies them.
name: Frozen Radiance Observatory
summary: A small orthodox sect of Ice Dao cultivators who study the aurora from an observatory beside the Frost Steles. They sell aurora readings and rent seats at the steles.
truth: The master has worked out why the aurora is brightening and sent her figures to the Armillary Pavilion. The reply asked her, politely, to stop publishing.

lore: Fire runs close under the ground here, and the basin stays green through the polar night under a sky lit orange by its own steam. Spirit farmers terrace the springs for fire-and-ice herbs: frostflame lotus, ember moss, snow ginseng where the steam freezes. The Frostmilk River gathers in its marshes. The Eternal Night Palace, the Iron Bone tribes and the Seal Watch's quartermasters all take a share, and the farmers pay all three. Mammoth herds winter at its edges, and so do the wolves that follow them. This decade the springs at the north end have begun to cool, and nobody admits to knowing why.
name: Warm Basin
summary: A sunken basin between the ranges, the glacier and the steppe, where hot springs melt the ice into steaming marsh. The richest herb ground on the continent, and three powers tax it.
truth: The Palace is drawing the northern springs' fire through lava tubes to heat its thaw works under the glacier. When those springs die the north basin freezes, and the Musk Ox Tribe will blame the farmers.

lore: Whoever holds the ramps holds the tableland's door, and the Cliff-Climb khans have held them for two centuries by fortifying the switchbacks and charging a head of cattle per hundred. Their warriors fight from ledges with throwing axes and fall-ropes, and their children climb before they ride. The present khan is the elder half-brother of the Snow Wolf claimant and has promised him the ramps, which would give the Snow Wolves a road to the herds. The Mammoth Tribe has promised to bury the khan in his own switchbacks if he does.
name: Cliff-Climb Khanate
summary: A khanate that holds the three ramps up the tableland's southwestern cliffs and tolls every herd, digger and calf thief that climbs them.

lore: At midsummer a hundred thousand people camp here: tribes, Frost Fair traders, beast tamers, Myriad Sands monks and body cultivators come to fight in the pits. Mammoth ivory, furs, musk, eagle chicks and tempering herbs change hands for salt, tea, iron and spirit stones. Pit fights are bare-handed by law, and a foreigner who wins three in a row is offered adoption into a tribe. In winter only the stone-keepers and a few hundred guards stay.
name: Court of a Thousand Tents
summary: The great tent camp of the Iron Bone Tribes below Ancestor Mountain. It swells to a city each summer for trading, and for the stone-lifting every third summer and shrinks to a garrison in the long night.

lore: From the cliffs of the Utter North the Shoreless Sea runs toward the Rim, and on still nights a pale glow rises over the world's edge. The sea freezes far out each winter; seal hunters and whalers work the ice edge and pay tribute to the sea clans when they meet them. Exiles from every faction end up here: Palace deserters, tribal outcasts, Seal Watch men who would not go home. In the last forty years hunting parties have begun to vanish whole, and the two patrols the Seal Watch sent found only empty camps with the fires still warm.
name: Utter North
summary: The northeastern horn of the Black Frost Continent, pointing toward the Rim: ice cliffs, pack ice and lonely fiefs of hunters and exiles. Lately, fewer of the hunters come back.
truth: The second patrol found one survivor. He hummed all the way back to the fortress and was quietly killed there, and the Watch has told no one.

lore: Forty volcanoes, a dozen awake at any time. Lava tubes run for hundreds of li under its ice, and whoever knows them can cross the Spine in winter without seeing the sky. Black iron, obsidian and sulfur crop out along its flanks; fire salamanders and ash wolves hunt its slopes. Its eastern end dives under the glacier, and steam rises from the ice there all year.
name: The Burning Spine
summary: The volcanic range that runs across the western Black Frost Continent from the fjords to the edge of the Demon-Sealing Glacier. Its vents glow red through the polar night.
truth: The Spine is warming with the tide. Three volcanoes dead since the Dim Age began smoking this decade, and one of them is the mountain the Palace is built on.

lore: The stone is a black needle forty feet tall inside a ring of carved marks that count something other than hours. Under the midnight sun its shadow sweeps the ring once a day. In the polar night it casts a shadow anyway, from no light anyone can see, and that shadow moves backward. The Armillary Pavilion sends astronomers every few years to measure it and will not say what they find. Time Dao cultivators sit in the ring for a summer and come out disoriented, and now and then enlightened.
name: Circling-Sun Stone
summary: An Ascent Age gnomon on a northern headland. In midsummer its shadow circles a full turn without the sun ever setting, and Time Dao cultivators sit inside the circle.
truth: The backward shadow is cast by the Mirror. The stone is counting down the years to the tide's peak, and its count agrees with the Armillary Pavilion's own tables.

lore: Steam pours from cracks in the ice here all year, and the caves below are lined with frost-fire crystal, a stone cold on one face and hot on the other that refiners buy by the ounce. The Palace has held the mine for sixty years under a lease from the Seal Watch, guards it with its own disciples and kills anyone who comes near. Miners are hired in Dawnless City on five-year terms. None has come back early, and few at all.
name: Melt Caves
summary: Meltwater caves at the glacier's southwestern edge, where the last vent of the Burning Spine runs under the ice. The Eternal Night Palace works them as a frost-fire crystal mine.
truth: The caves are the Palace's thaw works. Its tunnels reach the Frozen Host from below, and the demon that escaped forty years ago walked out through them.

lore: The tribes call it their mother, because its valleys are where the herds survive the polar night. From the first freeze to spring its ice carries sledges, mammoth trains and riders down to the Frost Fair, and the Palace's toll posts take a fifth of every load. In summer it floods its valleys with gray water too cold to swim. Every Great Khan has ridden south along it, and every coastal kingdom watches it in winter.
name: Frostmilk River
summary: The steppe's great river, milky with glacier silt, running from the foot of the Burning Spine through the Warm Basin to Glass Bay. In winter it freezes into the ice road that feeds the Frost Fair.

lore: The Musk Ox Tribe has wintered here for a thousand years. Every spring when the herds move out the farmers plant over the grazing, and every autumn the tribe tramples it. Their warriors wear musk ox horn on their fists and fight in a wall, shoulder to shoulder, and their children learn to stand in the wall at ten. They collect the basin's grain tithe in person, and a farmer who shorts it loses a field. Their northern springs are cooling, and the tribe has decided the farmers are poisoning them.
name: Musk Ox Tribe
summary: An Iron Bone tribe that winters its musk ox herds around the basin's northern springs and counts the whole basin as its winter pasture.

lore: The stone ship is three li long, its hull a single piece of gray rock carved with formations nobody can read, and the customs house sits in its stern. The Myriad Sands Continent's oasis merchant houses keep warehouses here, and a Heavenly Scale Pavilion branch changes spirit stones and lends at interest. Ivory, furs and black iron go south; grain, tea, cloth and lamp oil come north. In summer the harbor holds two hundred ships. In a hard winter it holds none.
name: Stone Ship Harbor
summary: The main port of the Sand-Gazing Shore, built around an Ascent Age ship of stone stranded on the beach. Every cargo bound for Myriad Sands passes its customs house.
truth: The ship came down the Ladder. Its hold is sealed, and the harbor master's family has kept the key for a thousand years without knowing what it is.

lore: It flows away from every other river on the continent, north toward the Rim, and herders say water that reaches its mouth never comes back as rain. For two months in midsummer it runs fast and black with meltwater; the rest of the year it is a frozen road from the Palace's northern mines to the coast. Palace slave trains walk its ice in winter, and the Reindeer Tribe sells them meat and now and then buys a slave free. Ice Dao cultivators study stillness on its ice, and Time Dao cultivators study it in the weeks it runs.
name: River of Passing Water
summary: A river that runs north from the Burning Spine across the Aurora Waste toward the world's edge. It is frozen ten months of the year.

lore: Ice-Keeper children read crevasses before they can count, and every adult has hauled sledges to the fortress. The Watch pays them in grain, salt and iron and keeps the khans off them; the khans call them the Watch's dogs. Their grazing shrinks every year as the ice moves south, and the young want to leave for the steppe. Their shamans sleep on the ice to hear the demons dream, and sell what they hear as weather forecasts.
name: Ice-Keeper Tribe
summary: A small tribe that swore itself to the Seal Watch at the Second Sealing. They haul the fortress's supplies, herd reindeer on the ice margin and listen to the glacier.
truth: Two of their shamans have started humming the same tune in their sleep, and their children have picked it up without being taught.

lore: There are three hundred and twelve steles, each sheathed in ice and each carved with a few lines of a treatise on the Ice Dao that nobody has read whole. When the aurora is strong the carvings shine through the ice; when it fades they vanish. Cultivators sit before them for weeks, and the frozen ones who never got up still sit among the living. A Foundation cultivator who comprehends one stele gains a technique; nobody has ever comprehended ten. The Frozen Radiance Observatory controls the best seats and rents them out.
name: Forest of Frost Steles
summary: A field of Ascent Age steles carved with fragments of an Ice Dao treatise. Under the aurora the carvings glow, and cultivators sit before them for weeks.
truth: The treatise was carved by the sect that built the Slumbering City, and its last chapter is not about ice. It is about sealing outer demons, and whoever froze the Frozen Host had read it.

lore: A Myriad Sands Continent-born sword cultivator came north to hunt the tribe that killed his family and stayed to sell his sword to the coast. The Gate he founded teaches a Sword Dao made for cold: short, fast forms that do not need warm muscles, and qi circulation that keeps blood moving in a blizzard. It recruits from the coastal kingdoms' guard families and rents its disciples to whichever king pays. It hates the Iron Bone tribes and the Palace equally, and it wants a fief of its own; the debt-ridden White Walls kingdom is starting to look like one.
name: North Wind Sword Gate
summary: A small orthodox sword sect that guards the Sand-Gazing Shore for pay. Its swordsmen fight in the cold better than any south of the strait, and cost accordingly.

lore: The only real forest on Black Frost grows here, black pine and larch on hills the sea keeps milder than the steppe. The Deer Call River floats timber to the coast, and ships carry it to the Floating Peak Continent's lowland yards. The Floating Peak Continent's Nine Clans buy furs, amber, masts, mammoth calves and beast mounts, and one of them has built a trading lodge above the harbor that looks more like a fort every year. The forest tribes trap, hunt and log, and despise the coastal kingdoms for selling the forest by the shipload. Beast tamers from four continents gather here for next winter's opening of the ancestral beast realm.
name: Pine Surge Forest
summary: The southeastern taiga and coast facing the Floating Peak Continent across the eastern strait. Furs, ship timber, amber and beast mounts go south, and the Floating Peak Continent's clans keep a foothold on this shore.
truth: This is the only corner of the continent getting warmer: the forest edge has crept north a hundred li in a century. The Black Pine shamans think the Pine of Ten Thousand Ages is doing it, and they are right.

lore: The Qiu family fled Morning Star eight hundred years ago after backing the wrong prince and brought rice seed with them. Their terraces step down the fjord walls through the steam, fed by springs hot enough to cook an egg at the top and cool enough for rice at the bottom; Qiu children learn each terrace's water by taste. The rice sells to the Palace, the Frost Fair and the fortress. The family trains spirit farmers, pays them well and asks only that nobody carries seed out. They keep orthodox rites quietly, and the Palace ignores it while the rice comes.
name: Fief of Steaming Fields
summary: Spirit rice terraces on hot springs above the fjords, held by an old farming family of orthodox exiles. The only rice that grows north of the strait.

lore: Palace deserters, oathbreakers from the Seal Watch, tribal outcasts and foreign fugitives built the stockade a century ago, and its only law is that nobody asks why you came. It runs the smuggling road for relics from the Field of Broken Spears and the glacier's snout, around the Watch's patrols to the Floe Market. Its chief is a one-armed Core Formation woman who deserted the Palace after killing her master. Newcomers pay a year's labor or a year's wages.
name: Runaways' Stockade
summary: A stockade of exiles from every faction on the edge of the Utter North. No questions asked, no extraditions honored, and a smuggling road for the glacier's relics.

lore: The Iron Bone Tribes graze mammoths, shaggy horses and musk oxen here in summer and pull back to the river valleys when the polar night falls. Each tribe holds its grazing by force, and the tribes meet only at the [[Ancestor Mountain]], where chiefs lift the ancestor stones to prove their right. The last Great Khan died sixty years ago; the cycle says the next is due, and two claimants are gathering riders. Body cultivators from every continent come to learn the Fist Dao in the blizzard camps. A stranger who survives a night in the open may be adopted; the rest are left for the wolves.
name: Irongrass Steppe
summary: The southern steppe heartland of the Iron Bone Tribes around the lone peak of Ancestor Mountain. Grass grows waist-high under the midnight sun and dies to iron-gray stalks in the long night.
top: Deity Transformation (two war chiefs; the Bone Ancestor waking)
truth: The summer grass line has crept a thousand li south in a lifetime as the glacier's cold spreads. That, more than any dream, is why the tribes are ready to follow a Great Khan south.

lore: The Listeners live in snow huts just past the Watch's patrol line, write the Host's dreams in ledgers and sell blizzard warnings to caravans and the fortress alike; their forecasts are right more often than anyone's. They take in anyone who hears singing in their sleep and cannot stop hearing it, and teach them to write it down. They want the Watch to let them closer to the ice, and resent the Palace miners who chase them away from the Melt Caves. The Watch thinks them harmless.
name: Ice Listeners
summary: A fellowship of shamans, hermits and Seal Watch dropouts who sleep at the glacier's edge and write down what the demons dream. They sell blizzard warnings.
truth: They are a cell of the [[Void Choir]]. The ledgers are hymns, and the Listeners are waiting for the one who got out to call them.

lore: As the glacier creeps south it scrapes the ground and drops what it carried at its snout: boulders, carved Ascent Age blocks, war debris and things older than the war. Three years ago a cultivator in robes of a cut nobody recognized came out of the ice whole, and the [[Thousand Puppet Gate]] bought the body for a sum nobody will name. Scavengers work the moraine in summer. In winter the snout calves without warning and buries whoever is under it.
name: Pushed-Stone Moraine
summary: The ridge of rubble the advancing glacier pushes ahead of itself. It spills out Ascent Age stones, demon glass and, now and then, bodies nobody can identify.
truth: The robed body was not dead, only sealed. It woke on the ship to the Long Dusk Continent, and neither it nor the puppet master who bought it has been seen since.

lore: The fjord runs two thousand li inland between black cliffs, and its head is a cauldron of boiling springs fed from the Burning Spine's roots. Steam fills it from wall to wall, so ships ring a bell every hundred strokes and steer by the echoes. Fire coral grows in the warm shallows at its head, along with the ember eels alchemists prize. Pilots who know the echoes charge a low-grade spirit stone a day and are worth it.
name: Cloud-Swallowing Fjord
summary: The deepest fjord on the west coast, so full of steam from the hot springs at its head that clouds seem to sink into it. Ships navigate it by bells.

lore: In summer, cultivator-crewed ships carry furs, black iron and mammoth ivory to the Myriad Sands Continent and bring back grain, tea and lamp oil. In the hardest winters the sea ice reaches across the strait: no caravan can cross that much ice, but a Great Khan's riders on ice wolves can, and have. Every town here has a wall and a bell. The Thousand Lamps Temple's mission heals raiders and raided alike and is quietly becoming the richest landlord on the coast. With a Great Khan due, the kingdoms are hiring swords, building walls and arguing about tribute.
name: Sand-Gazing Shore
summary: The southwestern coast facing the Myriad Sands Continent across a cold strait: walled mortal kingdoms, a Buddhist mission and ports that grow rich on summer trade and burn when the khans ride.
truth: The strait has frozen across in four of the last seven winters, where once a decade was a hard run. The monks have told the Myriad Sands Continent. Nobody has told the coastal kings.

lore: Its trunk takes two hundred people to ring and its crown is lost in cloud. The Black Pine Tribe tends it and kills anyone who cuts it. A drop of its sap cures frost damage in the meridians and is worth a mid-grade spirit stone to any alchemist in the north. It woke once in the Rekindling and walked a hundred li, and again three centuries ago, when loggers cut a root and the forest closed over their camp in a night. The Thunder-Feather Lodge's new road points straight at it.
name: Pine of Ten Thousand Ages
summary: A black pine taller than any tree on the continent, deep in the taiga. It is a spirit plant that has woken twice in recorded history, and its sap cures frost in the meridians.
top: Nascent Soul (a spirit plant, mostly asleep)

lore: For three centuries the bells rang every dusk to show the towers were manned; now they also call the faithful to Sea-Crossing Temple's evening sutra. Children are raised on sutras and sword drills both, and the temple takes any orphan the kingdom gives it. The king wants to cede the harbor to the temple in exchange for arhat protection. His nobles want Palace mercenaries instead, and one of them has already sent an envoy to Dawnless City.
name: Kingdom of the Evening Bell
summary: A small harbor kingdom named for the warning bells that ring from its towers at dusk. Its king is a lay disciple of the Thousand Lamps Temple, and half his people have converted.

lore: Each winter the Workshop lays the Fair's foundation arrays: heat circles under every street that keep the ice firm but not lethal. It sells warming talismans in three grades, from a mortal's one-night charm to a Foundation cultivator's month-long seal, and teaches formations and talisman making to apprentices who pay with five years' labor. Everyone needs it, so it is neutral. Its masters want the empty seat on the Fair's truce council, and despise the Armillary Pavilion array keepers, who treat them as tinkers.
name: Warm Array Workshop
summary: The formation masters who lay the heat arrays under the Frost Fair's ice platforms and sell warming talismans to half the continent. Without them the Fair freezes in a night.
truth: The Workshop can switch off the Fair's heat with one command array. It has used the threat twice, and the Palace has quietly started training formation masters to replace it.

lore: The She family has held the fief for the Eternal Night Palace for six generations: four Foundation cultivators and a hundred overseers. Free miners' children grow up in warm tunnels and see the sun only in summer. Slaves who show a spirit root are sold to the Palace at eight; the family keeps the ones who show two. Black iron ore fetches a low-grade spirit stone a cartload at the mine head and five times that in Dawnless City. A giant-blooded slave from the Snow Wolf tribe has been organizing the lower galleries, and the overseers have noticed.
name: Black Iron Fief
summary: A mining fief on the north slopes of the Burning Spine, where steppe slaves dig black iron in tunnels the polar night never leaves.
truth: The She heir has been selling the family's best veins to the Yin Fire Sect behind his father's back, and means to hand his father to the slaves when the revolt comes.

lore: The city is warm and red in the darkest month. Forge Street refiners turn black iron into blades with a blood groove and sell them to anyone, including orthodox buyers in hoods. The Palace's Contract Hall posts bounties on elders' rivals; anyone may take one, and it pays in high-grade spirit stones. Slaves are sold in the lower market by the dozen. The only law is the Palace's tax, collected by outer disciples who keep whatever they can squeeze above it.
name: Dawnless City
summary: The market city below the Eternal Night Palace, carved into a black cliff and lit by lava channels. Slaves, black iron, blood pills and blades are sold here, and its Contract Hall hires anyone.
top: Nascent Soul (Palace elders come down to trade)
truth: Forge Street's best refiner is a [[Clear Heaven Sword Sect]] sword elder who faked her death forty years ago. She copies every blade order the Palace places and sends the list south.

lore: Black basalt cliffs lift the tableland above the steppe, and its winds strip snow from the grass, so the herds come up to graze through the polar night. The herds are older than the tribes, and the greatest are led by mammoth matriarchs at Core Formation and above. The giant-blooded tribe that follows them claims kinship with the herds, and the herds seem to agree. Beast tamers pay fortunes for mammoth calves, and calf thieves climb the cliff ramps every winter; the herds trample the ones they catch and the tribes hang the rest. Both Great Khan claimants want the herds for the ride south.
name: Mammoth Tableland
summary: A high basalt tableland in the east where the great mammoth herds graze through the polar night. Mammoth matriarchs, a giant-blooded tribe and calf thieves share it badly.
truth: The giant blood comes from the herds. Mammoth matriarchs who reached Nascent Soul took human form in the Dim Age and took human husbands, and the tribe's elders know it.

lore: When a mammoth knows it is dying it leaves the herd and walks to this valley, and the herd follows to see it die. Ten thousand years of bones lie here in drifts, and tusks lie like fallen trees. Beast cores from old matriarchs rest in the skulls. Ivory diggers and bone refiners would pay anything for one season inside, and some have tried; their bones are in the drifts too. The Giant-Blood tribe buries its dead here, which no other humans may do.
name: Mammoth Graveyard
summary: A valley where old mammoths go to die. Its floor is ivory and bone, and the herds kill anyone they find digging there.

lore: Their founders were cast out of the [[Jar-Mother Clans]] for breeding Gu that survive cold, and came north to prove it could be done. Snow silkworms live on frostleaf at the basin's edge and spin ice silk, which refiners make into robes that turn blades and hold heat; a bolt sells for a mid-grade spirit stone. Their cold Gu stop a heart without leaving a mark, and the Palace buys them. They teach Gu raising to girls only.
name: Snow Silkworm Stockade
summary: A stockade of exiled Jar-Mother daughters from Vast Wilds who raise snow silkworms and cold Gu at the basin's edge, where warm ground meets frozen.
truth: The Jar-Mothers want them dead and have sent a Gu north to do it. It is already inside the stockade, and it is patient.

lore: Snow Wolf children raise ice wolf pups in their own tents, and a rider and wolf who survive their first raid are bound for life. The tribe raids the coastal kingdoms and the Frost Fair's caravans, sells captives in Dawnless City and spends the proceeds on more wolves. Its chief is twenty-six and already Core Formation in body, and every tribe that has bet against him has lost its herds. He says the Ancestor has told him to ride south this winter, across the frozen strait, and that the ice will hold.
name: Snow Wolf Tribe
summary: Wolf-riding raiders of the southern steppe near the coast. Their young chief says the Bone Ancestor speaks to him in dreams and that he will be the next Great Khan.
truth: The dreams are real. The Bone Ancestor is choosing a Khan and a vessel, and does not care whether the boy survives the choosing.

lore: The water is warm, red and salty enough to float a man, and the crust on its shore is the best body-tempering salt on the continent. Outer disciples soak until their skin splits and heals, and rank in the outer court is partly decided by who can stay in longest. Salt rakers from Red Spring Fief work the far shore for wages; a sack sells to body cultivators at the Frost Fair for a low-grade spirit stone. Nobody fishes it.
name: Blood Salt Lake
summary: A warm crater lake below the Palace, red as blood and thick with salt. Palace disciples soak in it to temper their bodies for blood cultivation.
truth: The lake is red because nine hundred years of blood tithe have been drained into it. The salt tempers so well because of what it remembers, and the oldest rakers hear it whisper.

lore: The Reindeer Tribe moves its herds along the River of Passing Water and out onto the barrens, steering by the aurora; their shamans read its colors as other diviners read stars, and are right about storms more often than not. Their children can walk a day in a blizzard and find the camp at the end of it. They pay the Palace a tithe of hides when it comes to collect and ignore everyone else. Scavenger crews keep digging up their burial grounds for the ruins beneath, and the tribe has started killing crews that dig without asking.
name: Reindeer Tribe
summary: Reindeer herders of the Aurora Waste who follow the northern lights, believing the lights lead the herds to grazing. They are the only people who live here all year.

lore: Its cliffs are columns of black basalt a thousand feet high, and frost rocs nest on the ledges. The ridge breaks the north wind for the herds and funnels it everywhere else. Old lava tubes run through it, and the Hearth Clan says its ancestors walked east through them before the Burning Spine cooled. Egg hunters climb it each spring; a frost roc egg sells to beast tamers for five mid-grade spirit stones, if the climber lives.
name: Tusk Ridge
summary: The black basalt escarpment that walls the Mammoth Tableland on its west and southwest, curving like a tusk from the edge of the Utter North down toward the southeast coast.

lore: Seven salt families rule by council and marry only each other. Their pans run along the shore for three hundred li: in summer they boil seawater over peat, in winter they rake frost salt off the bay. Every tribe needs salt for the dark months, so every tribe fosters a hostage child in a salt house as surety for fair prices. The foster children grow up as brothers and sisters across tribal feuds, which has stopped two wars and started one.
name: Kingdom of the Salt Houses
summary: A small kingdom of salt pans and smokehouses on the bay's northern shore. Salt keeps meat through the polar night, and the salt families have grown rich and nervous on it.
truth: The Snow Wolf chief was a salt-house hostage. The families know exactly which of their children he loved, and which he swore to kill.

lore: Ships from the Floating Peak Continent's lowland ports bring spirit stones, formation plates and grain, and leave with furs, amber, masts, ivory and live beasts. The beast market here is the largest on the continent: frost eagle chicks, ice wolf pups, spirit elk, white bear cubs and, under the counter, mammoth calves. A Heavenly Scale Pavilion branch changes and lends. The Thunder-Feather Lodge stands on the hill above, and its people walk through the market as if they own it, which they nearly do.
name: Harbor of Distant Peaks
summary: The main port facing the Floating Peak Continent. Sailors swear that on the clearest winter days the floating peaks hang over the southeastern horizon, which is how the harbor got its name.

lore: A Core Formation Palace elder holds the fief as a reward and runs it as a business. Farmers indenture themselves for ten years to clear a debt or spare a child from the blood tithe; few finish, because the overseers add a year for every failed crop. The fields grow blood lichen, ember moss and nightbloom, the core herbs of the Palace's pills. Indentures who escape run to Spring Gardens, and the Palace sends hunters after them.
name: Fief of Herb Fields
summary: The Eternal Night Palace's herb plantation on the basin's western slopes, worked by indentured farmers under a Palace overseer. It grows the herbs for the Palace's blood pills.
truth: The overseer skims a third of the harvest and sells it at the Hundred Herb Market. Three people knew; two of them are buried in the lichen beds.

lore: When the war ended, the survivors of the northern line were promised relief that never came, so they stayed. Their descendants keep the old earthworks, drill their children on them from the age of six and consider the Seal Watch a newcomer. They own salvage rights to the battlefield by an old Watch decree and kill scavengers who skip the tenth. Their ancestral hall holds the shields of three thousand dead, and the elders read the names aloud every Long Night.
name: Fief of the Left-Behind
summary: A fief of the descendants of the Outer Demon War's northern line, who stayed where their ancestors fought and still man the old walls south of the glacier.
truth: One shield in the hall has a blank where its owner's name should be, like the blank on the Seal Watch's founding stele. The elders have never shown it to the Watch.

lore: In deep winter, when the bay ice is clear as glass, a building shows through it a hundred feet down: tiled roofs, a courtyard, a bronze gate. Divers go down on ropes with warming talismans, and the cold kills most within a quarter hour. What they bring up sells at the Fair's appraisal stalls: jade tiles that hold formations, bronze fittings and once a sealed box that three Core Formation cultivators fought to the death over. The gate has never opened.
name: Shadow Pavilion
summary: An Ascent Age hall drowned at the bottom of Glass Bay. On the coldest days the ice is clear enough to see its roofs, and divers cut holes to reach it.
truth: The hall was a waystation for envoys coming down the Ladder, and its gate opens to an Upper Realm token. The [[Armillary Pavilion]] has been quietly buying every fitting the divers raise.

lore: An Eagle-Master child climbs to a frost eagle eyrie at twelve and comes down with a chick or not at all. Their eagles carry messages between the tribes, the Frost Fair and the fortress, spot raiders a hundred li off and can be trained to take a man's eyes. Beast tamers buy their surplus chicks for a mid-grade spirit stone each. Both claimants want their eagles, and the chief is auctioning the alliance in all but name.
name: Eagle-Master Tribe
summary: Falconers of the western steppe who tame frost eagles. Every tribe uses their birds for scouting and messages, and every tribe suspects they read the messages first.
truth: They do read the messages, and they have sold copies to the Eternal Night Palace for thirty years.

lore: Yin fire burns blue, gives almost no heat and melts black iron in a breath; the sect draws it from vents too deep for mortals to survive. It makes the Palace's blood blades and armor and sells the seconds in Dawnless City. It recruits by buying slave children who can stand near a vent without fainting, and teaches the Fire Dao, artifact refining and the blood quench. It hates the Hearth Clan, who sit on the best vents, and wants the Earth Heart Fire said to be waking under the Spine. Bring it a fire salamander core and you get a month at its forges.
name: Yin Fire Sect
summary: A demonic refining sect, sworn vassal of the Eternal Night Palace, that forges with cold blue fire drawn from deep vents and quenches its blades in blood.
truth: The sect's master forged the cages the Palace keeps thawed demons in, and kept a sliver of demon flesh for himself. He has been eating it a crumb at a time.

lore: The Stockade sells mounts to the Frost Fair, the Floating Peak Continent and the Myriad Sands Continent, trains tamers for a fee or seven years' labor, and takes children whom animals follow home. Its masters teach beast taming, beast medicine and the patience to wait a week beside a den. Its most profitable line is mammoth calves stolen from the tableland and raised in the forest, where the herds cannot follow. The Old Mammoth clan knows where the Stockade is and has not come yet; its master thinks that is because she pays the Cliff-Climb khan.
name: Beast-Tamer Stockade
summary: A school of beast tamers in the taiga that breaks frost eagles, ice wolves, spirit elk and white bears to the saddle, and buys stolen mammoth calves without asking.

lore: From its north wall you can see the Frozen Host through a hundred li of blue ice. The glacier pushes the wall south every decade, so the Watch builds a new one and leaves the old inside the ice. Formation masters keep the cold-seal arrays charged with spirit stones the great powers pay for, and geomancers measure the ice every month. Orthodox and demonic elders share a mess hall and do not speak. The fortress hires porters, cooks and ice-cutters on three-year contracts, and nobody is let go early.
name: Ice-Guard Fortress
summary: The Seal Watch's northern fortress on the southern edge of the Demon-Sealing Glacier. Elders of every great power serve here in rotation and watch a hundred thousand frozen demons.
truth: This rotation's Palace elders keep volunteering for the night watch on the west wall. From there, nobody else can see the steam rising from the glacier's underside.

lore: Hot springs pour into the heads of the fjords, so the inner harbors stay open while the outer sea freezes. Whalers and sealers sail from here into the Shoreless Sea and pay toll to the sea clans' northern court, or do not come back. The Eternal Night Palace ships slaves and black iron out of Chain-Gate Harbor; the fjord lords keep small fleets of their own and feud over fishing grounds and wrecks. Spirit farmers grow rice on terraces above the steam. This winter a Whale Tooth ship killed a jiao calf, and the sea clans want the killer's whole line.
name: Steaming Fjords
summary: The western coast, cut by deep fjords where the Burning Spine's hot springs keep the water open through the polar night. Whalers, spirit rice terraces and the Eternal Night Palace's western port.
truth: The Palace paid the Whale Tooth captain to make that kill. It wants the sea clans to burn the fjord kingdoms so it can take their harbors.

lore: Every tribe's ancestor stone rests in Heavy Stone keeping between gatherings, and to steal one is to declare war on every tribe at once. Their children carry stones before they can talk. Their shamans crack mammoth shoulder blades in the fire and read the cracks, and chiefs pay in cattle for a reading before a raid. Foreign diviners may learn bone reading for a price paid in labor: a year of hauling stones.
name: Heavy Stone Tribe
summary: The small tribe that keeps the ancestor stones at the foot of Ancestor Mountain. They judge the stone-lifting, read mammoth shoulder blades for omens and take no side.
truth: The stones grow a little heavier every year, and the keepers have been shaving them to hide it. They are running out of stone to shave.

lore: Tribal law forbids bloodshed within a day's ride of the mountain, and it is the one law every tribe keeps. The gathering at its foot every third midsummer decides chiefs by stone-lifting and, every few generations, raises a Great Khan. In the last ten years the mountain has shaken a dozen times, its springs have run hot and then cold, and herders swear they have heard breathing from the cracks on the north face. The stone-keepers forbid anyone to climb above the snow line.
name: Ancestor Mountain
summary: A lone black peak in the middle of the Irongrass Steppe, sacred to every Iron Bone tribe. Chiefs lift the ancestor stones at its foot, and lately the mountain has begun to shake.
truth: The Bone Ancestor, a Deity Transformation body cultivator of the Dim Age, sleeps in a chamber at the mountain's heart and is waking. The shaking is his heartbeat.

lore: When the shard passes close, a dark basalt arch opens on the tableland's rim and breathes warm air. Inside is a world of beasts that died out in Severed Heaven sixty thousand years ago: giant elk, saber-tusked cats, mammoths twice the size of today's. Their cores are prized above anything living, and their young can be tamed by someone patient and lucky. The next opening is next winter, and beast tamers from four continents are already arriving at Harbor of Distant Peaks.
name: Realm of Ancestral Beasts
summary: A shard world of Ascent Age beasts whose gate opens on the tableland's rim every twenty-four years for three months. Anyone below Nascent Soul can enter.

lore: From the Star Dial on the highest floating peak of the Floating Peak Continent, Armillary Pavilion astronomers chart the Mirror and the Shard Worlds and publish the calendar of secret realm openings every sect depends on. They rebuilt the transfer arrays eight thousand years ago and have never let anyone else learn how they work. They are strictly neutral, and will move an army for anyone who pays.
name: Armillary Pavilion
summary: The world's masters of formations and star reckoning. They run every transfer array between continents and tax every crossing.
truth: The Armillary Pavilion is rebuilding the Heaven Ladder. Every array toll for the last thousand years has gone into it. The Pavilion Master is a Body Integration formation master, and two Star Lords at Void Refinement keep the inter-continent arrays running.

lore: For half the year the sun never rises over the Black Frost Continent. Its southern steppes feed the Iron Bone Tribes, who temper their bodies in blizzards and despise qi cultivators as soft. The Eternal Night Palace rules the black ranges, where fire runs under the ice. In the far north an entire outer demon army lies frozen in the Demon-Sealing Glacier, and the Seal Watch keeps a fortress on its edge.
name: Black Frost Continent
summary: Ice, steppe and black volcanic ranges under a long polar night. Demonic sects, body-cultivating tribes and a frozen outer demon army.
top: Body Integration (the Night Sovereign, who never sleeps)
truth: The glacier is advancing south a few li every year. The tribes' shamans say the demons inside are dreaming.

lore: Built eight thousand years ago in the Rekindling. Every great power pays the Armillary Pavilion's tolls and resents it. The arrays avoid the Shattered Sea: something about Heaven's Scar scrambles them.
name: The Heavenly Circuit
summary: The chain of transfer arrays linking each continent's great city, run by the Armillary Pavilion. One jump costs more spirit stones than a village earns in a lifetime.
